Voters in an autonomous southern Philippine region will cast their ballots Monday in the region's first parliamentary elections, seen as a crucial step in the quest for self-determination and lasting peace after decades of insurgency and violence.

The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, or BARMM, covers five provinces, three cities and 63 villages across eight special geographic area clusters. It has nearly 2.4 million voters, with election officials aiming for an 80% turnout after polling was postponed for several years.

Here’s what to know about the Sept. 14 vote.

80 seats are at stake in the elections

There are 80 seats at stake in the elections that will determine members of parliament, the region’s legislative body. These include 40 political party representatives, 32 district representatives and eight sectoral representatives.

Unlike the direct voting under the presidential system of the national government, the region’s chief minister, who heads the executive branch, is not elected by voters. Members of parliament will choose the chief minister from among themselves by a majority vote during their first parliamentary session.

Voters will choose one regional party, one district representative and six sectoral representatives. The 40 regional party-representative seats will be distributed to nominees based on a party’s vote share.

The region has a history of strife

Centuries of colonialism by Spain, the U.S. and Filipino Christian settlers turned Muslims into a minority group in resource-rich Mindanao, the southern third of the Philippine archipelago from which the BARMM was carved out. The region has seen decades of intermittent but bloody conflicts over land, resources and political power.

Since the 1970s, about 150,000 combatants and civilians have died in the southern Philippines, while development was stunted in the country’s poorest region. Western and Asian governments feared the tenacious insurgencies could help foster Islamic extremism in Southeast Asia.

The presence of private armies and long-running clan wars has added to the violent mix.

Under a 2014 peace deal brokered by Malaysia, the largest Muslim rebel group — the Moro Islamic Liberation Front — gave up its goal of a separate Muslim state in the south of the largely Catholic country in exchange for broader autonomy. The group’s 40,000 fighters would be “demobilized” and given livelihoods and other help to bring them back to normal life.

The Bangsamoro region was established under the peace deal to replace a poverty-wracked five-province autonomous region with a larger, better-funded and more powerful area, which has been governed by former guerrilla leaders under a transition period that ends with the first regular elections on Sept. 14.

Challenges still remain in the region

The Moro Islamic Liberation Front last year suspended the disarming of its remaining 14,000 fighters after claiming that the government has not fully complied with socio-economic commitments it made under the 2014 peace deal. Then-presidential assistant David Diciano, who had been helping oversee the transformation of the Bangsamoro region, said in a statement at the time that the Muslim rebel front’s central committee had decided “to postpone the decommissioning of 14,000 of its combatants and 2,450 of their weapons.”

The Institute for Autonomy and Governance, a nonprofit policy and research center based in the region, has noted that the incomplete decommissioning of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front’s combatants as well as the organization’s split into two rival political parties vying in the elections pose a potential danger of violence that may affect voters’ confidence to go out and vote.

More than 20,000 military and police personnel are being deployed to secure the elections, officials said.

“We have just one goal: for them to be able to vote. All our preparations and efforts would be in vain if our fellow citizens couldn’t vote,” Commission on Elections Chairman Erwin Garcia said.

Sustaining parliamentary democracy

Michael Henry Yusingco, a senior research fellow of the Ateneo Policy Center, in an article published by the online portal Access Bangsamoro, said: “Without a party ethos that is rooted in collective responsibility, mutual respect, and orientation toward the common good, parliaments risk devolving into arenas of personal rivalries, factional disputes, or transactional politics."

He said it is the right time for regional parties to show they can embody such party ethos to sustain parliamentary democracy.

“Clearly, the BARMM’s history of clan politics, electoral violence, and patronage-based loyalties presents formidable challenges.”

The “Made in Benin” tags on Fatoumata Dosso’s fabrics represent an ambition much bigger than her fashion business: keeping more of the value of Africa’s largest cotton producer at home.

The founder of DAF Collection said that the tag means her country is trying to take full advantage of the abundant raw material produced in Benin. For her, there is also the opportunity to support more women in her community who hope to earn a living from cotton.

“I am more focused on promoting the traditional fabric of northern Benin,” she said inside her showroom in the northern city of Parakou. “What comes from elsewhere is already everywhere. I wanted to do something special.”

Betting on cotton for years to come

Dosso is responding to government policy that discourages the export of raw material and stipulates that the West African country must do more to export finished products — from pineapple juice to garments marketed by world-famous brands, but still marked with Benin.

Benin is Africa’s top cotton producer, according to data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture. Benin produced 1.15 million bales of cotton between 2025 and 2026, accounting for 0.9% of global production.

That sounds like a tiny share of the global market — by comparison, China produced 35.8 million bales in the same period — but cotton has long been the top cash crop for Benin, its primary export. The country is still betting on cotton for years to come, even as production has been in decline in eastern and southern Africa.

A hive of activity

Benin, which had been exporting almost all of its raw cotton to Bangladesh, moved toward value addition in 2020 with a private-public partnership involving the infrastructure developer Arise IIP.

The deal established the Glo-Djigbé Industrial Zone, or GDIZ, where young Beninese workers can be found processing pineapples, cashew nuts, ceramics and other export goods.

GDIZ processes about 40,000 tons of Beninese cotton to produce between 7 and 10 million garments annually. The expansion of the GDIZ and shifting exports toward finished products helped reduce Benin's current account deficit — when a country sends more money for goods and services abroad than it receives back — from 6.2% of gross domestic product in 2024 to 5.7% in 2025, according to the African Development Bank.

GDIZ is located 45 kilometers (28 miles) from the Beninese commercial capital of Cotonou. Associated Press journalists recently toured the garment section, a hive of activity as station managers surveyed employees doing the work that goes into making garments: straightening collars, stitching buttons and pressing T-shirts with flat irons and folding them delicately. Garment makers like U.S. Polo Assn. and Kiabi were represented.

A grassroots network

A manager at GDIZ declined to answer questions, and laborers there weren't allowed to speak to journalists. A brief tour of the hub showed the ambition of GDIZ, a small-city-like industrial hub set on about 16 square kilometers (6 square miles) of land.

Souhaïbou Gambari, executive secretary of a national association of cotton producers in Benin, told the AP that his federation — and Benin's garment exports in general — rely “on a strong, well-structured grassroots network” of at least 183,746 producers organized in 2,206 village cooperatives across the country.

“Beyond farm operators alone, the cotton sector directly or indirectly supports the livelihoods of more than 2 million people in rural areas, making it the leading driver of social inclusion in Benin’s farming communities,” he said.

Cotton is an easy decision

Bales of cotton are ferried from far north, supplied by cooperatives of farmers who are united in the pursuit of strong prices and ease of access to farming supplies.

Growing cotton is an easy decision for smallholder farmers like Toussaint Bapetem. Although the price of a kilogram — 300 West African francs, or roughly $0.50 — has remained the same for years, Bapetem's produce has a market guaranteed by price-setting authorities.

Cotton, unlike maize and other rain-fed crops, doesn't attract thieves, he said, inspecting his offseason cotton plantation in a remote area near the Nigeria border.

With the help of about 18 workers, the father of four regularly plants three acres (more than a hectare) of his land with cotton, with another four acres (more than 1½ hectares) reserved for corn. His last harvest yielded 3.8 tons of cotton.

“Cotton is more profitable” than corn, which fetches 120 West African francs (about $0.20) per kilogram, he said.

Repaying debts and ensuring education

His cotton earnings since 2024 helped him “take care of my family and ensure my children’s education,” he said. “With the money from cotton, I repaid a debt of 500,000 francs ($885) and purchased a motorcycle.”

Bapetem said that he knew that some of his cotton was used to make garments locally, including attire he buys at the nearby Bétérou market “once or twice a year.”

Locally available garments are increasingly made by homegrown entrepreneurs such as Dosso. Her DAF Collection retains the services of about a dozen women employed as weavers, who huddle over rickety contraptions tethered to rocks as they stitch yarns of cotton and polyester into pieces of fabric.

Beloved especially by Fulani herders, the fabric known as pagne in French is wrapped around the waist or worn as a headscarf, a thing of everyday fashion.

Quitting her job as the mayor's secretary

“I was in a region where women were learning cotton weaving, but they didn’t have a market for their products,” said Dosso, who quit her job as a private secretary to the mayor of the northern town of Gogounou to focus solely on the fashion business that she started in 2016.

“That’s when I started to promote this skill,” she said.

She now advocates for “Made in Benin,” representing her country at international fashion shows and espousing the goal of having showrooms in all the major cities of Benin.

“My clients are all kinds of people. They are diverse and come from all social classes,” she said. “I can boast that I am one of the first in my field to talk about ‘Made in Benin.’”

‘It benefits us greatly’

One of Dosso’s contracted weavers, Chabi Baké, said that she understood the idea of making finished goods at home to be the appropriate one for Benin. The mother of five makes roughly $545 a month as a weaver, enough to encourage her to start building a house for her family.

“I am pleased with this thinking because it benefits us greatly,” she said. “It allows people to buy our products.”

News.title: Tora Bora’s last midwife struggles under Taliban rule as aid runs dry
News.content:
The small clinic, crowded with pregnant women, sits in the shadow of Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan. Twenty-five years ago, those mountains commanded the attention of the world’s most powerful military. Roughly 15 miles from the clinic, in the Tora Bora cave complex, Osama bin Laden was believed to be hiding as American bombs rained down in the hunt for the architect of 9/11.

Today, another consequence of the West’s long entanglement with Afghanistan is playing out beneath those same mountains – in the struggle to keep mothers and babies alive.

In the baking courtyard of Gandab Kharoti health centre, dozens of women enveloped in sapphire blue burqas sit shoulder to shoulder beneath trees waiting to see Shila Ibrahimi, a 27-year-old midwife.

The women rest against walls, dusty, barefoot children play, and mothers cradle sick babies beneath folds of cloth. Some have walked for hours through the mountains to reach her.

Among them is Fawzia, 30, seven-and-a-half months pregnant with her seventh child. Suffering from headaches, she has walked for miles through the heat.

Her husband works far from the village, so she makes the journey with her children and mother-in-law, hoping the Taliban do not stop her for the “crime” of travelling without a male escort.

Under the Taliban’s morality rules, women face restrictions on travelling alone, while UN monitors have documented the regime’s morality inspectors ordering some health facilities not to treat unaccompanied women.

But enforcement varies and Fawzia says nobody challenged her on her journey here. Asked where she would give birth if the clinic closed she says: “We have nowhere else to go. We cannot afford that. We are poor.”

News.title: Springboks look like World Cup champions elect… again
News.content:
In doing so, Erasmus while still relying on his veteran performers, managed to expose some of the next generation to invaluable white heat pressure, including Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van den Berg and Cameron Hanekom, who all look to the manor born.

And the substance of the series victory is heightened by the fact it came against a regenerated and rejuvenated All Blacks side, who rediscovered their high-octane and relentless attacking identity under new coach Dave Rennie. At times the handling and precision of the All Blacks were so sumptuous that it felt like they might be in a position to level the series in Baltimore.

But the narrative of the previous two Tests continued. At key moments they were let down by their discipline and turnovers in attack to gift the Springboks’ transition ball, and their directness, backed by their power both in collisions and set piece enabled them to pick up points much more easily than their opponents.

At the end, the scoreboard ran away from the All Blacks, which was harsh on them. But one had wondered if they would be able to maintain their intensity at the end of the first half, when it took 32 phases for Will Jordan to score a try to cut the deficit to three points.

News.title: Emotions run high and Sabalenka smashes racket after Rybakina clinches US Open
News.content:
The polarities reversed in set two, as Sabalenka began to get her flamethrower of a forehand working. After almost 90 minutes of play, she finally chiselled out some break points – two in game 10, which she couldn’t convert, but then another in game 12 which set up the decider.

The huge contrast in personalities became all too evident in set three. Sabalenka appeared to be at war with herself, emoting and venting almost as if she were an actress projecting her feelings to the whole of this 24,000-seater stadium. As she faced the prospect of slipping a double-break down, she hunkered down on her haunches in despair.

Meanwhile, Rybakina could have been relaxing in a flotation tank for all the stress she showed. Admittedly, she did hit a couple of double-faults as she served out for victory, but she also came up with two aces and two forehand winners in the same game.

Sabalenka, meanwhile, allowed her racket to slip to the ground in frustration and barely managed a brief embrace at the net. She had earned a code violation in the first set for slamming a ball out of the stadium, and could easily have picked up a second – and thus a point penalty – after another ball that she batted away struck a cameraman, but chair umpire Greg Allensworth showed leniency.

Asked about tossing her racket, Sabalenka said: “It’s really tough to control your emotions when you lose in the final of the Grand Slam and when you were trying to go for three-peat. So I just wanted to let it go, because if I would hold it inside, right now or here or there on the court, I wouldn’t be able to say a word or I would just go not really nice over there.

“So I just wanted to let all of that aggression and disappointment go outside.”

The trophy was presented by 2006 champion Maria Sharapova – one of the few women who can look down on 6ft Rybakina, especially when wearing heels. The fans in Arthur Ashe Stadium had given at least 80 per cent of their support to Sabalenka, who won the previous two US Opens on this court, but they applauded warmly, knowing when they had seen a performance for the ages.

News.title: Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Kick off 8pm.

News.title: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

News.title: Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players
News.content:
Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

News.title: Lando Norris on pole for Spanish GP but adds voice to critics of ‘Madring’
News.content:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen predicted that overtaking would be “practically impossible” in the race. “[The Madring] has a tendency of maybe creating some big shunts in some places,” the Dutchman said. “It reminds me a little bit of Jeddah in a way – fast corners and the walls being very close.

“The only thing that’s already a bit disappointing is that many of the braking zones are angled. This means it’s practically impossible to attack a competitor because you’re braking and simultaneously turning right or left. And that’s the worst thing you can do if you want to create an overtaking opportunity.”

Norris agreed with Verstappen that it would be very difficult to overtake, although that is no bad thing for him provided he can hang on to the lead at the start.

The Briton, though, described the decision to build what is now the longest pit lane on the F1 calendar as a big disappointment.

“I think it has a lot of potential,” Norris said of the Madring. “Just certain things need to be improved. Like the pit lane, which is like six kilometres long. It’s the longest pit lane of the year and the biggest pit loss of the year [in terms of the time it will take to pit – an estimated 25 seconds]. So that just makes overtaking worse. Not overtaking, but it makes the desire to box and do different strategies worse.

“You know, if we’re going to build a new track and spend so much money in building a new track, this is probably one of the main factors, I would say, is you have a short pit lane so people can pit and you then create overtaking.”

Norris described his pole lap as “one of the best laps of his career” and his team principal Andrea Stella fully agreed, describing it as “a masterpiece”.

News.title: Bomb squad rescues rusty Red Roses
News.content:
Mia Venner, Sadia Kabeya, Lucy Packer and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald went over for further tries to add to player-of-the-match Abi Burton’s first-half score.

Moloney-MacDonald’s try wide out on the left was a show-stopper for the crowd of 9,251 in the North West and demonstrated that England have style to go with solidity. But it was the power game that did for Australia.

The Wallaroos scored tries of their own through Faliki Pohiva and Eva Karpani but spent the vast majority of the game manning the defensive barricades. They did so admirably for 40 minutes but when the dam wall blew it blew spectacularly.

They did not help themselves with sin-binnings in either half for Samantha Wood and Karpani, but over 80 minutes the odds will always be stacked in favour of the full-time side against the part-timers.

“The reality is that even at our best we’re probably not good enough. We will be,” said Tim Walsh, Rugby Australia’s director of women’s high performance. “We need an environment where they can concentrate on being full-time athletes. That’s the vision Rugby Australia have and that’s where we’re headed.”

The game was England’s first with the smaller ball being trialled in the women’s game by World Rugby and they only converted four of their eight tries, a statistic which may be seized upon by those who do not care for it. A rugby pitch is not a sterile laboratory though and the swirling, blustery conditions should be taken into account in any dissection of its value.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca brands Man Utd the Premier League’s biggest long-ball merchants ahead of Manchester derby
Sports.content:
ENZO MARESCA has branded Manchester United the Premier League’s number one long-ball merchants.

The Manchester City boss expects United to go direct in today’s powder keg derby.



The Italian has done his homework as City look to improve on just one win in their last four Old Trafford visits.

Maresca said: “They are the team in the Premier League at the moment who plays the most balls in behind.



“It’s quite clear that they’re very dangerous and they don’t need many passes. They are quite direct when they recover the ball.”

Maresca is not the first Prem boss to slap the Red Devils with that label.

Arne Slot did so last October when United, then bossed by Ruben Amorim, won 2-1 at Liverpool.

Slot said: “It is always difficult to play against a team that defends in a low block and mainly plays the long ball.”

City have won all three Prem games so far.

United boss Michael Carrick is trying to build on the 5-2 win over ­Ipswich in their last home Prem game.

“Players who have already won, and know how to win — it is important they’re in our squad.”

Sports.title: Arsenal ratings vs Sunderland: David Raya shows why he’s Prem’s best goalkeeper as Ezri Konsa endures brutal battle

DAVID RAYA stole the show as Arsenal maintained their perfect record in the Premier League.

The Gunners had to battle for all three points against Sunderland but came out on top with a 2-0 win.



Raya played a key role as he saved a penalty from Enzo Le Fee before Bruno Guimaraes fired in the opener.

Ezri Konsa was saved his blushes by Raya as he gave away the penalty and had a tough battle with Brian Brobbey for the 90 minutes.



Here’s how SunSport’s Simon Collings rated the Gunners at The Stadium of Light…

David Raya 9

Didn’t have a single save to make in the first half, but came up trumps after the break with a heroic penalty save.

Underlined why he is the best goalkeeper in the Premier League right now with another incredible stop late on.

Ben White 6

Picked to start for the sixth game in a row, but only lasted until half time due to what looked like a groin injury. Arsenal’s bad luck with injuries at right-back continues.

Had a tough night as he was in a proper battle with Brian Brobbey, who caused him problems.

Gave away a penalty after tussling with Dan Ballard – but it felt like a harsh call on the Gunners defender. Rallied well and made some big blocks late on.

Had one hairy moment where he was almost involved in a mix-up with David Raya from a long throw.

Other than that, the Brazilian was solid and even went close with a long-range strike in the first half.

Had Arsenal’s first shot of the game with a signature run into the Sunderland penalty area.



Did not get forward as much as he can do, but solid defensively.

Thriving in a deeper role this season. Mopped up so much in the middle of the park and sprayed the ball around nicely, too. A classy performance.

Sports.title: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 2: Bruno Guimaraes toast of North London AND Tyneside as £75m star maintains 100 per cent start
Sports.content:
BRUNO GUIMARAES was the toast of North London AND Tyneside after his thunderbolt helped down Sunderland.

The ex-Newcastle captain came off the bench to fire home and cap off two minutes that could prove key to the Gunners retaining the title.



Bukayo Saka’s additional-time penalty wrapped it up as Sunderland ended the game with ten men after Reinildo Mandava was sent-off for a second booking for fouling the winger.

But this night belonged to Guimaraes. He ignored a barrage of abuse to rifle home from 25 yards just 121 SECONDS after goalkeeper David Raya had saved Enzo Le Fee’s penalty.



It came right when the Gunners were rocking. But those two moments of brilliance continued Arsenal’s 100 per cent start to their Premier League defence.

The result piles the pressure on rivals Manchester City – who trail by three points ahead of the derby at United.



One of the key reasons behind Arsenal’s rampant form has been their success at getting Marton Odegaard into more advanced positions.

Including the Community Shield, the Norwegian has scored four in six, after just one in their entire title-winning Prem campaign.

Sunderland had clearly done their homework. They were on him like wasps throughout the first half.

Ex-Arsenal captain Granit Xhaka sent the Gunners skipper sprawling to the floor first, causing a foot-stomping strop from Arteta.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Arsenal ratings vs Sunderland: Raya shows why he's Prem's best keeper as Konsa endures brutal battle DAVID RAYA stole the show as Arsenal maintained their perfect record in the Premier League. The Gunners had to battle for all three points against Sunderland but came out on top with a 2-0 win. Raya played a key role as he saved a penalty from Enzo Le Fee before Bruno Guimaraes fired in the opener. Ezri Konsa was saved his blushes by Raya as he gave away the penalty and had a tough battle with Brian Brobbey for the 90 minutes. Here’s how SunSport’s Simon Collings rated the Gunners at The Stadium of Light…

The Spaniard was fuming again when Odegaard went down clutching his foot after Nilson Angulo had trodden on him.

He was even more frustrated when he was booked by referee John Brooks for repeatedly leaving his technical area midway through the first half.

Frustration was the theme throughout. But it will have come as no surprise. Regis Le Bris’ side were one of only eight teams to stop Arsenal from winning on the road last term.

That came courtesy of a 94th-minute equaliser from Brian Brobbey. The Dutchman was up for it again here, battering and bettering Ezri Konsa all the time.

And when the overwhelmed England defender dragged ex-Arsenal academy ace Dan Ballard to the ground after a rapid Sunderland storm of attacks, they looked set to leave upset again.



The Gunners tried every trick in the book to delay the spot-kick, and it worked as Raya got down to his left to tip Le Fee’s effort onto the post.

And the Arsenal celebrations were in full gear just over two minutes later.

An attack down the left found Rice, and he capped his 150th appearance for the club by teeing up Guimaraes to unleash a glorious strike from outside the D into the top corner.



Bruno will get the credit, but Raya is Arsenal's hero That wasn’t pretty at times, but Arsenal got the job done, says SunSport’s Simon Collings. It feels like a massive win, given that they were in Naples on Wednesday night. A word on David Raya — I think he’s the hero from this game. I know Bruno Guimaraes will get a lot of the headlines, that brilliant goal coming off the bench, particularly as a former Newcastle captain. But Raya’s penalty save was the moment where that momentum swung in the second half. If that goes in, suddenly Arsenal were in all kinds of trouble. And it really is a moment in the spotlight for the Spaniard, who doesn’t probably get loads of credit because he plays behind that brilliant defence. This was a great night for him.

The 28-year-old, who captained Sunderland’s bitter rivals Newcastle to Carabao Cup glory in 2025, enjoyed every second of it by cupping his ears in celebration in front of the irate Mackems.

You could hear the cheers from Tyneside. Guimaraes faced dog’s abuse getting off the team coach and warming up during the first half.

But after replacing Myles Lewis-Skelly, first English teenager to start in Arsenal’s opening four league games since both Tony Adams and David Rocastle did in 1986, he showed Arteta exactly what he got for the £75m they paid Toon.

It was a moment of magic just when his side were on the ropes. The Black Cats had stood toe-to-toe with the champs and flew out the traps following half time with both Thomas Meunier and Le Fee going close.

Bukayo Saka failed to connect properly after being slipped in behind the defence by Rice early on but from then on it was the hosts doing most of the swinging.



Xhaka’s inviting free-kick flew past everyone for Ballard at the back post, but the ex-Gunners academy ace failed to replicate his scoring heroics from this fixture last year by bundling wide.

Brobbey was bullying Konsa with tackles flying in everywhere, Reinildo Mandava receiving the first booking for a foul on Saka.

The best Arsenal could muster was a long-ranger from Gabriel until Kai Havertz held off Kevin Danso, chested it, spun and hit one on the volley but Robin Roefs tipped over.



Then, out of nowhere, it was Xhaka that came to the rescue right on the whistle as he flicked it away from the German’s toe as he waited to pounce from Saka’s knockdown.

Sunderland began the second period like caged animals, forcing the Gunners defence to be camped inside their own box.

But it was Raya, who reproduced his heroics late on with a super save to keep out an attempt from Nordi Mukiele with one hand after another super Xhaka delivery, who knocked the wind out of their sails.

Arsenal right-back Jurrien Timber, on for Ben White at the break, almost capped his first outing since the Champions League defeat with a goal.

However, his celebrations after heading home Odegaard’s cross were cut-short by an offside flag.



Not that it mattered. This night belonged to Guimaraes.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi caught in heated confrontation with Mathys Tel on pitch after woeful Tottenham draw with Everton
Sports.content:
ROBERTO DE ZERBI was caught having a heated conversation with Mathys Tel after toothless Tottenham’s latest flop.

Spurs bored their home crowd with a drab goalless draw against Everton on Saturday evening — extending their winless Premier League start to four games.



De Zerbi‘s side have lost two of those, and still haven’t even scored a goal.

So, unsurprisingly, the Italian boss was far from happy at full time as boos rang down.



The 47-year-old was spotted on the pitch to have an animated chat with attacker Tel, 21.

De Zerbi appeared to be raising his voice with the versatile forward responding in that appeared to be a deflated manner.

The ex-Brighton boss was asked about the incident during the post-match press conference.

And the former Marseille manager insisted he was simply “coaching” one of his players.

De Zerbi responded: “Yes, I coached him on the pitch. What did you understand?”

The reporters asked for more details and the Tottenham boss explained he was instructing Tel how to position his body.

And the former Shakhtar Donetsk manager insists there is no problem between the two men.

De Zerbi added: “The body shape. He is a striker and the striker can play with the shoulder on the goal.

“If we are playing with [James] Maddison, [Mohammed] Kudus and Savio, he has to play as a striker and the striker has to look at the goal or the cross from [Andy] Robertson.

“He has to stay inside because he started as a striker, eh? Now he is playing as a winger but he started his career as a striker, but I love Mathys as a player, as a guy and there is not a problem.”



De Zerbi saved Tottenham from relegation last season in a dramatic season finale.

Sports.title: Jamie Redknapp launches blistering attack on ‘absolutely diabolical’ Tottenham after failing to score in first 4 games
Sports.content:
JAMIE REDKNAPP launched a blistering attack on Tottenham after they went goalless in the Premier League yet again.

Spurs have failed to score in any of their first four league games of the new season.



Their latest blank came in the goalless draw at home to Everton on Saturday afternoon.

Spurs forked out a fortune on new players in the summer in order to avoid finishing 17th for a third consecutive season.



However, after struggling in front of goal in the opening weeks of the campaign they are now 17th and have just two points on the board.

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp hit out at the club on Sky Sports after the draw with the Toffees.

He labelled Roberto De Zerbi‘s side as “absolutely diabolical” during his damning assessment.

The former Tottenham and Liverpool midfielder said: “After spending £300million, I didn’t think there would be a problem scoring goals.

“I thought that they might struggle to win games, a few teething problems, but I thought with the players they’ve got in midfield… surely they have goals in this team.

“To not score in the Premier League in six hours of football is absolutely diabolical, whatever way you look at it.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“They defended better today, the centre-backs were better than what they had been.

“But there was just not enough. How can you not score in six hours of football?

“They have not got the right balance in the team. There are so many problems to solve in a game just to score a goal.”

Spurs were very active in the transfer window as they spent £100mi on Sandro Tonali, £85m on Mateus Fernandes and £85m on Savio.



Striker Omar Marmoush was another high-profile arrival as he joined from Manchester City on loan with a £60m obligation.

Spurs have netted five goals this season but they all came in a single game – the Carabao Cup win over Championship side Charlton Athletic.

De Zerbi will be hoping his players can break their duck in front of goal in their next league game against Aston Villa on September 19.

Before then, they have the tricky trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Furious Arteta rages over 'unacceptable' Sunderland penalty call
Sports.content:
A furious Mikel Arteta described Sunderland's penalty in Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light as "unacceptable".

The home side were awarded a spot kick in the 54th minute when defender Ezri Konsa was adjudged to have held Sunderland's Dan Ballard by referee John Brooks.

"The referee's call of penalty to Sunderland for a holding offence by Konsa on Ballard was checked and confirmed by VAR," said a statement published by the Premier League Match Centre.

The statement continued by quoting the interaction between on-pitch referee Brooks and the VAR.

David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee's spot kick and Bruno Guimaraes scored Arsenal's opening goal just 121 seconds later but Arteta vented his anger at the decision despite the result.

"The first question we have to discuss is this," he said at the start of his press conference. "This is not acceptable at this level.

Rybakina ​won ‌her ​first US Open, beating top seed ‌and defending champion ⁠Sabalenka ​6-4 ​5-7 ⁠6-2 on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

The 27-year-old had already been guaranteed to replace Sabalenka at No 1 in the rankings next week.

Sports.title: Guimaraes haunts Sunderland as Arsenal continue winning start
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes scored a stunning goal two minutes after David Raya had saved a penalty as Arsenal beat Sunderland 2-0 to move above Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.

The Black Cats had the chance to go in front when Ezri Konsa was penalised for holding Dan Ballard in the second half, a decision which enraged Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, but Raya brilliantly tipped Enzo Le Fee's spot kick onto the post.

Just 121 seconds later, Guimaraes, whose every touch had been booed by the home fans due to his Newcastle connections, crashed a stunning strike in off the underside of the crossbar from outside the Sunderland box for his first Arsenal goal.

The victory, Arsenal's fourth in a row in the Premier League and sixth in all competitions, maintains their strong start to the campaign and puts the champions three points above Manchester City, who face Manchester United live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

For Sunderland, the defeat is made all the more painful by the identity of the player who opened the scoring, coming so soon after they appeared poised to strike first from the spot. They remain on four points, the latest side to be dispatched by Mikel Arteta's men.

Raya to the rescue again for Arsenal as he saves Mukiele's close-range effort 90+7: GOAL! Saka's penalty squirms past Robin Roefs after Reinildo's red card for hauling him down

Arteta rages at Sunderland penalty call

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta to TNT Sports: "It's a huge win but it could have been something very different.

"I'm so upset. It's unacceptable (Sunderland's award of a penalty). This can change the course of a season, the championship, and it's not acceptable.

"I've seen it 10 times to make sure because I watched it live and I said it's not possible that it's going to be a penalty because it's a judo role, that's what it is. It cannot happen.

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any context, in any league."

Is Raya the world's best goalkeeper?

Sky Sports' Nick Wright:

Guimaraes didn't hesitate when asked after the game if he sees David Raya as the best goalkeeper in the world. "Definitely," he said.

The midfielder's sensational goal completed the two-minute turnaround but it was Raya who made it possible.

Arteta was adamant the spot kick should never have been awarded. But Raya's sole focus was to stop it from going in. Le Fee, who scored a penalty last weekend, struck it well. Raya, though, showed his athleticism, diving low to his left to make the save.

It was a brilliant piece of goalkeeping and there were plenty of other examples over the course of the 90 minutes at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are about as physical as opponents come but he dominated his box, claiming crosses and exuding calm.

His save to deny Mukiele, following a fabulous centre by Granit Xhaka, when Arsenal were still only a goal up, was another crucial intervention. And he was straight back up on his feet to scramble away the follow-up. Raya is always alert to danger.

He had to settle for a place on the bench with Spain at the World Cup. But there can be little doubting his status as the Premier League's best, if not the world's, and his value to his team-mates and manager is abundantly clear.

He was Arsenal's difference-maker - and not for the first time.

Guimaraes: A beautiful moment for me

Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes to TNT Sports: "It's unbelievable. I feel very good.

Image: Bruno Guimaraes celebrates his goal against Sunderland

"Everyone knows I had a difficult start with injuries in a short time but I'm glad to be back, to play.

"I scored a beautiful goal. It's a beautiful moment for me and my family and I'm very happy.

"A beautiful goal in a very good place. Everyone knows my past. I had an amazing history at Newcastle but now I'm trying to create a new history here and I've started in the right way."

Le Bris: Proud but disappointed

Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris: "Proud and disappointed. These are the two words I have in my mind at the minute.

"Proud because we showed we were really close to achieving something really big against one of the best teams in Europe right now.

"Our second half was excellent. We got the momentum, created chances. A big save from Raya on the penalty. The league is relentless. We conceded the goal but we stayed in the game.

"We created other chances but didn't score and this is the difference today."

Sports.title: Shelton relishing challenge of first Grand Slam final against Zverev at US Open
Sports.content:
Ben Shelton finds himself in unfamiliar territory after reaching his first Grand ‌Slam final at the US Open, with the American now ready to "do it for the USA" when he takes on top seed Alexander Zverev in Sunday's showdown.

Shelton is the first black American man to reach the US Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972, and is aiming to become the first home male player to win the title since Andy Roddick in 2003.

He will have a raucous Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd behind him when he takes on German top seed and title favourite Zverev.

The Spaniard's words of wisdom helped his son reset after his sensational five-set win over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-final.

"I think you learn from your experiences," said 60-year-old former ATP pro Shelton. "He won Montreal, he went to Cincinnati and we said: 'this is going to be the toughest day you're going to have', playing in the first round in Cincinnati after winning a title.

"Very few people come from that and have another good tournament the next week, and he didn't, you know? He lost first round.

"I remember talking to Rafa a couple of days after that match. Rafa was, like, 'you know, you got to be able to get through that first one and have the day off and then be able to get your best tennis again the next week'.

"So it was a lesson for Ben that you've got to be able to bounce back when good things happen, just as you have to bounce back when adversity happens or tough things go on.

"So we talked about him beating Carlos and how important it's really going to be for him to understand that this one is going to be even tougher, you know, to bounce back after that, because a lot of people want to rest after they've had something good and want to celebrate it.

"What we say is don't celebrate until you separate. So you've got to win the next match. You've got to consolidate it. Then somewhere, hopefully next week, we can celebrate a little bit."

Sports.title: West Ham secure first WSL win of season against London City Lionesses
Sports.content:
West Ham claimed their first Women's Super League win of the season with a 2-1 home victory over London City Lionesses.

Kelly Gago put the Hammers ahead after 21 minutes, racing onto Seraina Piubel's pass from near halfway before rounding City goalkeeper Elene Lete.

Viviane Asseyi scored a similar goal three minutes after the break after being released by Riko Ueki, running clear from 40 yards out before firing home.

Image: West Ham's Viviane Asseyi celebrates after scoring to make it 2-0

London City set up a frantic finish after Danielle van de Donk's clever back heel crept in at the near post 14 minutes from time.

But the Lionesses struggled to reproduce the fluency that had seen them overcome Manchester United on the opening weekend.

Guarino: We must show same spirit in every game

West Ham head coach Rita Guarino

"I'm very happy.

"I'm happy with the result, it's three important points at home in front of our supporters, but also for the performance in the way the team played today, and the way the team trained in the week.

"I'm very happy with the result and performance.

"I saw the spirit that I want to see every time, it's part of our identity. We can't forget that we have this kind of value and we need to show it in every single game.

Sports.title: Iraola bemoans Liverpool's lack of cutting edge and explains Barcola plan
Sports.content:
Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola bemoaned lack of creativity and cutting edge after his side were held to a 0-0 draw by Fulham at Anfield.

The result leaves Iraola unbeaten so far this term, but Liverpool have yet to win at home in the Premier League this season.

Liverpool struggled to create opportunities against a Fulham team that had lost their opening three games, with Iraola insisting afterwards that his side's shortcomings were evident.

"I think what was lacking, I think it was quite clear," Iraola said.

"I think it's the first game since I'm here, I think we've had problems to create chances, to score goals, to make the difference offensively.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Liverpool’s match against Fulham in the Premier League

"That's the main reason. We couldn't create as many chances as we wanted and we haven't scored a goal. And that's why we go just with one point."

Iraola: Players lacked freshness

Image: Fulham's Gonzalo Garcia and Liverpool's Ronald Araujo battle for the ball

The Reds lacked the energy they showed in their midweek Champions League win over Atletico Madrid, but Iraola refused to use fatigue as an excuse for his side's failure to pick up all three points.

"Our players were tired," he said.

"I think there is a lack of freshness, definitely. We cannot hide it.

"I think it's the worst turnaround in terms of 60-something hours between the games, after a very big game (against Atletico Madrid) the other day.

Image: Oscar Bobb is challenged by Milos Kerkez

"But this is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, maybe. But sometimes it's going to happen the same way during the season. We have to adapt to these circumstances.

"It's this kind of game that you need to win, sometimes with a set play, sometimes with a shot from the edge, sometimes from a moment of brilliance from the offensive players and we haven't had that today.

"We've been clearly not as good offensively as we've been in other days."

Barcola makes full PL debut from left

Bradley Barcloa made his full Premier League debut in the game and was deployed from the left in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Victor Munoz starting the game on the right.

Explaining his thinking, Iraola said: "I think I said it a lot of times. I think we have four wingers. Probably, before the season, everyone will say there are more left wingers than right wingers, because they play more there.

"I think all the wingers will play on the right and will play on the left. Depending on the match-up, depending on where we think they are going to be more dangerous, depending on the defensive demand, depending on what we feel, what we analyse, we position them in the right or in the left.

"But I think Bradley, I think everyone. The four of them already have played both sides and it's going to be a whole season like this because of the wingers, with a lot of times the same preferences."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thierry Henry explained why Liverpool supporters should be excited by new signing Bradley Barcola after the France forward completed his move from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal worth up to £123m

Iraola added: "I think with Bradley now we are building also his physical condition, because he hasn't had any in pre-season and I think there is a good part where today he played, I think, a little bit more than three days ago against Atletico Madrid.

"He had a good chance in the second half, they blocked the shot but he arrived well.

"Probably, we know he has more, but now it's about giving him the minutes, keep building his confidence also and he's a player that is worthy of our support."

Sports.title: Guimarães and Saka fire Arsenal to win at Sunderland after Raya spot-kick save
Sports.content:
As the final whistle blew Bruno Guimarães wore a mischievous smile, Enzo Le Fée was a study in dejection and Arsenal’s immaculate start to the season remained unblemished.

Two minutes after David Raya had rather majestically saved Le Fée’s second-half penalty, Guimarães delighted his new north London public and plenty of old friends in Newcastle by sending a shot curving past Robin Roefs from the edge of the area.

Mikel Arteta’s champions were en route to another win in a campaign that has now produced six victories in six games in all competitions, including the Community Shield. No one, though, should be deceived by the emphasis lent to the scoreline by Bukayo Saka’s stoppage-time penalty; this was most definitely the toughest test this term for Arsenal.

If Sunderland can keep playing like this, Régis Le Bris and his players should have real cause for optimism – even if they could have done without Reinildo’s late sending-off for felling Saka when conceding that penalty and collecting a second yellow card.

His penalty miss aside, chapeaux off to Le Fee, who has deservedly made Zinedine Zidane’s provisional France squad for the forthcoming Nations League matches. Sunderland’s attacking playmaker knew another good performance here could only enhance his chances of moving from longlist to shortlist and he did not take long to draw a foul and win a dangerous free-kick.

View image in fullscreen Players tussle in the Sunderland penalty area during a even first half. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

Arsenal’s former captain Granit Xhaka delighted in curling the meanest of dead balls in Dan Ballard’s direction but the home central defender, a one-time Gunners youth captain, could not quite connect.

There had been a similar reprieve for Le Bris’s rearguard when Saka failed to make the most of Declan Rice’s fine early delivery. Yet, bar a Gabriel Magalhães shot from distance that whizzed just wide of Roefs’s goal, a Kai Havertz shot on the turn saved smartly and a low 20-yard effort that Le Fée dragged fractionally wide of an upright, that was pretty much it in terms of first-half goalmouth action.

Mikel Arteta’s side were taking their time to establish a settled passing rhythm. If Sunderland’s superb organisation hardly assisted the visiting cause, Arsenal looked a little fazed whenever the outstanding Nordi Mukiele – surely another candidate for the France squad – advanced from right-back.

Ezri Konsa, meanwhile, did not appear to be either relishing or winning his extremely physical contest with Le Bris’s ever-combative centre-forward, Brian Brobbey. If a packed Stadium of Light enjoyed that little subplot, the roof was nearly lifted off by the roar of approval that greeted Reinildo’s full-blooded early challenge on Martin Ødegaard.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta is booked by John Brooks for leaving his technical area. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

One constant was Arteta’s excursions outside his technical area and eventually the referee, John Brooks, responded by jogging over to the touchline and waving a yellow card in the Arsenal manager’s face. While that booking was hardly unmerited, it seemed a shame that Brooks turned a blind eye to some persistent shirt-pulling from both sides at corners.

With the match even at the interval, Arteta replaced Myles Lewis-Skelly and the hobbling Ben White with Guimarães and Jurriën Timber. The Brazilian’s past as Newcastle’s captain ensured Guimarães’s every touch was booed, while Sunderland started the new half strongly, with Brobbey continuing to bully Konsa.

A penalty area encounter with Ballard at a throw proved no more welcome and when Konsa grappled the defender to the ground, Brooks – much to Arteta’s chagrin – had no hesitation in pointing to the spot.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães, who had been jeered by Sunderland fans for being a former Newcastle player, taunts them after scoring. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

Le Fée attempted to squeeze his kick just inside an upright but Raya, excellent throughout, guessed correctly and tipped the ball quite brilliantly on to the woodwork. Talk about a sliding-doors moment. Two minutes later and very much against the run of play, Arsenal broke from another Sunderland throw and Guimarães did the rest.

With no option but to take risks, Le Bris switched to 4-4-2 and also introduced Malick Fofana, newly signed from Lyon, and he quickly created chaos in Arsenal’s box.

Although it took Roefs, who saved superbly from Saka, and Ballard, responsible for a vital header off the line, to keep Le Bris’s side in the game, while Timber had a headed “goal” disallowed for offside, Arteta had reason to look slightly nervous as Mukiele volleyed Le Fée’s corner over the bar.

By now Xhaka, booked for sliding into Guimarães, was enjoying himself in midfield and from one of his corners Mukiele again went close.

A comeback beckoned but Saka had different ideas as Arsenal issued a reminder that they will not surrender their title lightly.

Sports.title: De Zerbi says Spurs have ‘mental block’ after wait for league win continues
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi says his Tottenham players continue to lack physical fitness and must “unblock” themselves in psychological terms after they drew their latest Premier League blank in a home 0-0 with Everton. It is now four games in the competition since the start of the season without a goal for Spurs; they sit 17th in the table with two points and were booed off by frustrated fans.

De Zerbi gave a number of explanations for Spurs’ slow start, chief among them the injuries that a clutch of players sustained on the long-haul pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia. He lamented the impact of the World Cup on the return dates of certain players and mentioned how Sávio and Omar Marmoush had signed late in the transfer window.

De Zerbi talked up a positive opening 30 minutes from his players against Everton but accepted they ran out of steam and that there was a psychological problem.

“There is a word in Italian – sbloccarsi – that literally translates as if we unblock ourselves,” De Zerbi said. “[It is] a mental block because four games, no wins, no goals scored … it is tough for the players. The team is extremely strong, we can score goals and we can win games. And then we have to respect the history of the players in their careers. Forget Dominic Solanke and Marmoush – the other players … they didn’t score many, many goals in their careers and we have to find these goals. I think we can do so with the quality of our play.”

De Zerbi warmed to a familiar theme when he went back to the pre-season tour. “I said we started this season late for many, many reasons; too late,” he said. “Many players at the World Cup, many injuries, many problems in Australia. Micky van de Ven suffered an injury in Australia. Domi Solanke the same. James Maddison the same. Mateus Fernandes suffered an injury in Australia. He lost 15 days and it’s not so quick. Sávio and Marmoush, they came 10 days ago. I started to work with this [whole] group not last Thursday but two Thursdays ago. So, I think we have not the right physical condition yet.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and then maybe the energy, maybe the fact we didn’t score … maybe we lost in some players a little confidence. We have to be not positive but realistic.

“If we extend that part of the game to 60, 70, 80 and 90 minutes, in my opinion, we are going to win many games. We have to improve in the last third of the pitch, for sure. The last decision, the last pass and we have to shoot more times, especially when we have space and time. But I can’t say nothing bad about the players.”

Sports.title: Hull stun Chelsea with Mohamed Belloumi double before João Pedro rescues a point
Sports.content:
The chants from the away end about winning the league were sung in jest, but Hull continue to show they are here to stay. Sergej Jakirovic’s dogged, intelligent side are third in the Premier League after extending their unbeaten start to four games and can even count themselves unfortunate not to have beaten another of the Big Six after pushing Chelsea to the limit in an absorbing battle at a frustrated Stamford Bridge.

Hull were 2-1 up at half-time and they had the chances to snatch the points during the second half. It took two big saves from Emiliano Martínez to prevent an upset, but this was not a good day for the Chelsea goalkeeper or his new teammates. He was one of several at fault when Hull, having dusted themselves down after conceding from Morgan Rogers early on, went ahead through Mohamed Belloumi’s quickfire double. The ease with which Chelsea’s advantage was handed over left the normally calm and considered Xabi Alonso accusing his side of being “soft” without the ball.

Alonso craves the comfort of a forgettable win. Chelsea have been exhilarating in attack, but they cannot defend. They are conceding two goals per game and the basketball nature of Alonso’s approach has created chaos rather than control. “It’s all entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win,” he said. “It will take time. When we get the lead you still need to be competing and not to give the chance so easily for them to come back.

“Especially in the first goal, we can do much better. It was too soft to give them hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances, but that changed the mood. We will get better, but it’s having an impact on our performances.”

It is ridiculous that Rogers, Cole Palmer and João Pedro are having to do so much in attack. Chelsea led after seven minutes, surging forward when they left four players forward at a Hull corner. João Pedro’s pass reached Rogers and the £117m signing from Aston Villa drove past Regan Slater before beating Konstantinos Tzolaki at his near post with a low, hard and early shot from the left.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro fires home Chelsea’s equaliser in the second half. Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA

Chelsea should have pushed on after becoming the first side to breach Hull since their promotion. Pedro Neto tested Tzolakis from the right, but the hosts became vague and complacent. This was the first time they have dominated possession in a league game this season and the result was not convincing. Hull limited them to an xG of 0.89, highlighting Chelsea’s issues against low blocks, and were clinical when they attacked.

The soft defending Alonso referenced for the equaliser started with Malo Gusto failing to deal with a long punt from Tzolakis in the 28th minute. Ryan Giles outmuscled the right-back and hooked a cross to the far post. Jorrel Hato misread the Hull left-back’s delivery, leaving Belloumi to rap a shot past Martínez.

Chelsea are without a win against promoted sides in five home games. They do not smell danger, while Alonso’s decision to leave Maxence Lacroix out at centre-back and shift from a back three to a 4-2-3-1 system backfired. Hull had so much space on the flanks. They pushed again and Belloumi’s flick found Lewie Coyle, who ran off Rogers but saw his shot cleared off the line by Levi Colwill.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it,” Alonso said. “Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

There was no response from Chelsea after Colwill turned Coyle’s shot wide. A corner came in from the left, Martínez flapped and Semi Ajayi’s header hit the bar. The ball came to Belloumi, whose shot flew in thanks to a deflection.

Alonso reacted at half-time, Hato making way for Pep Chavarría at left-back. Reece James drew a save from Tzolakis with a free-kick but Hull carried a threat on the break. They almost extended their lead when Martínez spilled a shot from Slater.

Martínez redeemed himself, blocking the rebound from McBurnie, and Chelsea soon levelled. Palmer, otherwise quiet, surprised Hull with a direct run. The No 10 drove down the left and picked out João Pedro, who lashed a shot into the roof of the net.

Hull refused to lie down. Ajayi, Giles and John Egan were outstanding at the back and the visitors maintained their shape when losing Nobel Mendy after a nasty collision with João Pedro.

Jakirovic made bold substitutions. Alonso threw Danny Welbeck on. Palmer scooped over from 20 yards and Tzolakis thwarted Rogers, but Hull had the best chance. Giles crossed again and Mohamed-Ali Cho shot straight at Martínez from close range.

Hull settled for a point. Jakirovic quashed talk of qualifying for Europe, insisting that survival remains the aim. The Bosnian has everyone pulling in the same direction. Before the start of the season he told his staff he would give them seven days off if Hull took eight points from their first five games. Mission completed with a game to spare.

Sports.title: Frustrated Liverpool lack any spark as Fulham claim deserved first point
Sports.content:
Álvaro Arbeloa was often the obstacle to Andoni Iraola’s international ambitions back in the days when both were vying for a right-back role with Spain. On his return to Anfield, and under the watchful eye of former manager Rafael Benítez, Arbeloa thwarted Iraola once again to claim his first Premier League point as Fulham head coach against an ineffective Liverpool.

Fulham belied their lowly position and run of three league defeats to take a merited point from a Liverpool team that was a pale imitation of the one that beat Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday. Iraola fielded a front four that cost almost £400m but the most impressive forward on display was the Fulham academy graduate Josh King. The draw was Liverpool’s third in four league games under their new head coach and the seventh in 12 Premier League matches at Anfield in 2026. Progress can be painfully slow at times.

“It is the first game we’ve had problems creating chances and making the difference offensively,” Iraola said. “It is easy for me to say the players were tired (after Atlético). There was a lack of freshness and, we cannot hide it, it was the worst turnaround in terms of 60-70 hours. But this is going to happen in the season and we have to adapt. Sometimes you need a set play or a moment of brilliance to win these kind of games but we were not as good offensively as other games.”

Liverpool were sluggish and sloppy – Florian Wirtz and Kostas Tsimikas put simple passes straight out of play in the first half, setting the tone for a disjointed performance – while Fulham bypassed the central midfield pairing of Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch repeatedly. The visitors’ confidence and composure on the ball, along with their defensive organisation, was hugely impressive considering the start to the season under the former Real Madrid interim coach and Liverpool defender. With more conviction in front of goal, Arbeloa’s side could have capitalised on Liverpool’s malaise.

Bradley Barcola created an early, difficult chance for Alexander Isak that the striker swept wide of the far post. Victor Muñoz went closer still with a glancing header from a Szoboszlai corner. Bernd Leno, the Fulham goalkeeper, reacted superbly to claw the ball away. But that was the sum total of Liverpool’s first-half enterprise.

Fulham were gifted a glorious opportunity when Alisson played a ridiculous pass to Gravenberch, who was under pressure from Sander Berge. Berge’s challenge fell to King, who was sent flying by the Liverpool goalkeeper but the referee, Thomas Bramall, played a good advantage as Gonzalo García received the loose ball. García had time to pick his spot but Jérémy Jacquet blocked his shot in front of the goalline.

View image in fullscreen Jérémy Jacquet clears the ball off the line to deny Fulham the lead. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

The visitors prospered down their left and Oscar Bobb missed another good opening when, unmarked and 18 yards out, he miscontrolled Alex Iwobi’s pinpoint delivery. Jacquet came to Liverpool’s rescue once again seconds later when preventing García breaking through with an excellent challenge.

Liverpool were deserving of a few home truths during the break – chiefly, you would have been lambasted for this last season under Arne Slot – and performed with more intensity in the second half. But not with any more threat. The introductions of Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister and Milos Kerkez brought modest improvement but Fulham continued to contain the hosts comfortably. The new signing David Affengruber had a fine debut and Calvin Bassey was commanding against Isak.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors remained dangerous on the counterattack and Alisson pushed away a King effort that was heading for the top corner. King’s replacement, Rodrigo Muniz, let a decent chance run away from him inside the area and the substitute Kevin dragged a shot wide from 18 yards. Isak finally escaped Bassey’s attentions in stoppage time but his flicked header from a Szoboszlai corner sailed wide.

Arbeloa said: “When you are not winning games it’s not so easy for your players to believe in your ideas. But they believe in the way we have been working and I showed them the things that we were doing so well. We were more balanced and controlled the transitions well. I’m happy with the point but more with the performance of my players and the character, the personality and the ambition they showed in this stadium.”

Sports.title: European football: Dortmund win again but Freiburg top after Gladbach rout
Sports.content:
Felix Nmecha scored twice and Fábio Silva grabbed another as Borussia Dortmund won 3-0 at home to promoted Paderborn to continue their perfect start in the Bundesliga. Dortmund’s win made it three from three in the league this campaign, their best start in 11 seasons, dating back to Thomas Tuchel’s time.

Starting up front alongside Serhou Guirassy for the first time this season, Silva converted a clever pass from the Guinean to give the hosts the lead after five minutes. Guirassy had two goals disallowed for offside in the first half but Dortmund were rarely troubled by the toothless visitors, who are yet to score since returning to the top flight.

Nmecha came off the bench to score twice, wrapping up victory for the hosts with a stunning late bicycle kick.

Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck made his first appearance since picking up an ankle injury at the World Cup and told Sky Germany he kept his comeback under wraps. “We just hadn’t communicated that much yet because I didn’t want to,” Schlotterbeck said, adding “I missed it terribly. It was a serious injury but I’m glad to be back now.”

Freiburg thumped a poor Borussia Mönchengladbach 5-0 at home to climb to the top. Yannik Engelhardt and Igor Matanovic netted twice each and Maximilian Eggestein added a late fifth as the hosts sent Gladbach, who finished with 10 men, to the foot of the table.

View image in fullscreen Freiburg’s Matthias Ginter (centre) congratulates Igor Matanovic on the opening goal against Borussia Mönchengladbach. Photograph: Philipp von Ditfurth/DPA/AP

A 2-2 home draw with Bayer Leverkusen ended Augsburg’s short stint as leaders. Augsburg were top after the last matchday for the first time in their history but were held by Leverkusen despite a double from Michael Gregoritsch.

Eintracht Frankfurt won their first match of the campaign with a 3-1 victory at neighbouring Mainz, with Can Uzun’s double either side of a Jonathan Burkardt goal. Frankfurt’s goalkeeper Noah Atubolu kept his remarkable penalty-saving record alive when he stopped a first-half effort from Nadiem Amiri. Atubolu’s save was his sixth in a row, extending his own Bundesliga record.

West Ham loanee Niclas Füllkrug kept his excellent run of form since returning to the Bundesliga going, scoring the equaliser for Werder Bremen in a 1-1 draw at Cologne. Thijs Dallinga missed a penalty after eight minutes but teammate Linton Maina put Cologne ahead moments later.

Füllkrug’s goal came in the 69th minute and is his third in four games since returning to Germany. He only found the net three times in 29 matches for West Ham and scored just once in 20 games on loan at Milan last season.

Elsewhere, Hoffenheim won 2-1 at home against Stuttgart thanks to a double from Adam Hlozek. On Sunday, Bayern Munich travel to promoted Elversberg – who have a 100% record – while RB Leipzig host Hamburg.

In Spain, Kylian Mbappé scored twice ⁠as Real Madrid enjoyed a 4-1 victory over Rayo Vallecano ⁠in La Liga ⁠at ​the Santiago Bernabéu. Goals from Álvaro Carreras and Jude ⁠Bellingham made the result comfortable for José Mourinho’s side.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé celebrates scoring Real’s fourth against Rayo Vallecano. Photograph: Manu Fernández/AP

A 14th-minute ⁠penalty from Mbappé was followed three minutes ​later by ‌a simple finish ‌from Carreras, with Mbappé turned provider ‌this time. A relaxed Real found little resistance from Rayo thereafter and, 11 minutes before half time, Vinícius Júnior raced down the left to set up ‌Bellingham for a neat finish into the corner.

Six minutes into the ​second half, Sergio Camello pulled a goal back for Rayo following sloppy Real Madrid play. Despite whistles from the ⁠home crowd, Real kept Rayo at ​bay, ​before closing out the ​game with a 90th-minute goal ​from ‌Mbappé.

The result ​moved ​Real on to 12 points, level with leaders Barcelona, who have a game in hand. Barça are at Levante on Sunday afternoon. Alavés missed the chance to go top overnight with a 2-1 defeat at Racing Santander.

In Italy, Diego Moreira scored twice as Milan came from two goals down to hold early season Serie A pacesetters Lazio 2-2 in Rome on Saturday. Moreira came off the bench at half-time and hauled Milan level after Matteo Cancellieri and Tijjani Noslin had given the hosts the lead at the interval.

Despite losing their 100% record having started the season with three wins, Gennaro Gattuso’s side move to the top of the table. Ruben Amorim’s Milan are fourth on eight points, after also drawing last weekend at Juventus.

View image in fullscreen Milan’s Diego Moreira celebrates scoring in his side’s 2-2 draw with Lazio. Photograph: Riccardo Antimiani/EPA

Cancellieri opened his account for the campaign after 10 minutes when he connected with a Mattia Zaccagni cross. A dominant Lazio had good chances to pull further clear before Noslin doubled their lead after 39 minutes with a close-range finish.

Amorim attempted to stem the tide by making three substitutions at half-time, bringing on playmaker Christian Pulisic and Moreira. His changes bore fruit after 65 minutes as Moreira volleyed home to halve the deficit. Less than two minutes later, the former Strasbourg player equalised with a fierce strike from outside the box, but neither side could find a late winner.

Atalanta slumped to a 2-1 defeat at home to Cagliari, with Sead Kolasinac handling the ball in the box to concede a second-half penalty that gave the visitors the win. Cagliari took the lead in the 19th ⁠minute when 19-year-old forward Paul Mendy rattled in the opener off the underside of the crossbar, ​but Gianluca Scamacca levelled for the home side ​four minutes before the break.

Mendy had the ​ball in the net again early in the second half only for the goal to be ruled out ​for a narrow offside, but ‌they took the lead ​again after Kolasinac was penalised, ​Daniel Maldini firing home from the spot to secure the three points.

The result moved Cagliari up to fourth in the table with nine points from their four games, while Atalanta are in ninth spot on six points. Earlier, hosts Genoa, who have yet to win this season, were held 1-1 by newly promoted Frosinone, who have seven points.

Champions Inter host Udinese on Monday, with Roma heading to Torino and Como at home to Parma. Inter and Roma have both won each of their first three matches.

Sports.title: Farke’s blueprint for revitalised Leeds continues upward trajectory
Sports.content:
Eleven years have passed since Daniel Farke mounted a magnificent palomino horse and rode round the perimeter of the pitch at Lippstadt, waving farewell to a capacity crowd. It seemed a fun way for the lower-tier German club’s centre-forward turned manager and sporting director to say goodbye. Yet few in the stands knew Farke was scared of horses and hauled himself into the saddle only out of politeness towards his chair, who had arranged this special surprise.

“I couldn’t deny him,” he said. “But it cured my fear – it was enjoyable.”

These days the Leeds manager is demanding similar bravery, as well as instant adaptability, from his players. “We want to be hard to predict,” said Farke as he prepared to welcome his compatriot Matthias Jaissle’s rapid counterattacking Newcastle team to Elland Road on Monday night. “We have different approaches. For example, if a team has two very good centre-backs who dominate aerially it makes sense to build with more low passes.

“It’s always in our DNA that we want to be on the ball and, in the buildup, we always want to be brave. Also it’s possible to break the [opposition] pressing by playing good football out from the back.”

View image in fullscreen Daniel Farke says ‘anything is possible’ for Leeds this season ahead of match with Newcastle on Monday. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Not that Leeds are averse to taking the direct route. This season only Hull and Nottingham Forest have played a higher percentage of their passes long than a Leeds XI invariably spearheaded by the formidable Dominic Calvert-Lewin. As Farke says: “We very often have a physical target player up front that we can be a bit more direct into.”

If such tactical variety is designed to keep rivals guessing, a fusion of alternative styles also befits a coach who admires the contrasting approaches of his close friends Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp.

Adaptability almost certainly saved his job last season. From 4 October to 29 November Leeds played seven Premier League games, losing six. They have since completed 28 league fixtures, losing five, while reaching an FA Cup semi-final.

Farke is negotiating from a position of strength as he discusses extending a contract that has less than a year to run. “Daniel’s done great,” the Leeds managing director, Robbie Evans, said this week. “We want him to be here long term and we’re working on it.”

View image in fullscreen Daniel Farke’s half-time changes against Manchester City in November transformed Leeds’s fortunes. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

Everything changed on 29 November. Leeds lost 3-2 at Manchester City but Farke’s half-time switch to a back three, allied to Calvert-Lewin’s introduction, provided him with a timely lifeline. The changes enabled the visitors, trailing 2-0, to level in a transformative second-half performance spoiled only by Phil Foden’s stoppage-time winner.

It marked the start of an upward trajectory that has continued this season as Leeds, alternating between three and four at the back, have remained unbeaten, like Newcastle.

A watershed perhaps came when England’s James Trafford arrived this summer from City for £40m – a record fee for a British goalkeeper. Given Newcastle had tried to buy Trafford on three occasions his signing represents something of a coup for Leeds. Throw in the abundance of diggers, hard hats and hi-vis vests on view at Elland Road as the stadium is expanded from a capacity of just under 38,000 to 53,000 and the sense of a club on the up is almost palpable.

“Something’s going well here,” Trafford said after signing. “They [the owners, 49er Enterprises] want to take the club back to where it has been historically and I think everyone here believes that is going to happen.

“With the energy, physicality and quality in this team anything is possible this season. The spirit is incredible. It’s really, really good and that can take you a long way.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion
