If such harmony can be attributed to Farke’s “no dickheads” policy when it comes to potential signings and the midfielder Ethan Ampadu’s impressive embrace of the captaincy, astute recruitment is steadily raising the team’s calibre.

The Bosnia and Herzegovina centre-half Tarik Muharemovic is proving an outstanding defender and a fine distributor. The £34m buy from Sassuolo is emblematic of the amalgam of robust athleticism and technical ability that increasingly characterises a Leeds team further enhanced by Harry Wilson’s arrival from Fulham.

View image in fullscreen Tarik Muharemovic scored for Leeds against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup and has already proved to be an astute summer signing. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Not that Farke is getting carried away. After seeing Trafford’s deputy, Michael Zetterer, overwhelmed as a rotated Leeds lost 6-3 at Chelsea in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday he was not in the mood for excuses.

“Let’s be honest, it was a nightmare debut,” Farke said on Thursday. “You feel a bit for him, but sometimes in life you have the worst possible start. He will have pressure next time, but he’s a good goalkeeper. They live a privileged life and he’s playing for a big club.”

On Monday, he will offer Jaissle a somewhat warmer greeting. They share a friendship with Klopp and Thomas Tuchel, but the Newcastle manager’s recent posting in Jeddah with Al-Ahli helped ensure that, until now, their paths have not crossed.

“He’s made a bright start,” Farke said. “Newcastle are very dangerous, especially counterattacking and it will be difficult. But we want to be on top of their challenge. We want as many points as possible.”

Sports.title: Febrile Manchester derby awaits amid growing rift between United fans and club
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s nine victories from 10 Premier League games at Old Trafford in 2026 cast their stadium as a fortress Manchester City aim to ransack on Sunday, to join Leeds in departing with three points during this calendar year.

Michael Carrick has overseen the division’s highest home points-per-game return in that span: 2.7, ahead of Arsenal’s 2.27 (from 12 matches) and Manchester City’s 2.25 (11); and his side have scored the most goals: 26, to City’s 23, and the champions’ 20.

When Enzo Maresca’s side motor across town, the 199th edition of a local squabble that draws a riveted global audience will be as febrile as ever – on and off the pitch.

A United fan group, the 1958, has called for a “peaceful protest” before kick-off, starting at a pub near the stadium, against what it believes is disproportionate action in the club’s drive to eradicate ticket touting. United said on Friday that 685 accounts had been subject to a ban and 464 supporters had received a reduced sanction or final warning.

Then, when the whistle blows, United will attempt to end City’s perfect start of four victories in all competitions, improve a disappointing return of four points from three league games and repeat the opening result of Carrick’s second interim tenure, achieved in January four days after his appointment: a 2-0 downing of Pep Guardiola’s visitors in which Bryan Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu were on target.

A 2-1 defeat by Leeds on 13 April is the sole blemish on United’s league record at Old Trafford since. The sequence shows how impressive Carrick’s stewardship has been and last month’s 5-2 hammering of Ipswich came in his first home game as the permanent manager.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes has been integral to Manchester United’s recent success at Old Trafford. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

Scan the results of his 10 away league games and you find four wins (at Arsenal, Everton, Chelsea and Brighton), four draws (West Ham, Bournemouth, Sunderland and Everton) and two defeats (Newcastle and Hull): 16 points from 30, compared with 27 from 30 when United play in front of their crowd.

A major factor behind the home record is easy to identify: Bruno Fernandes. In the 10 Old Trafford games the 31-year-old has provided 10 assists and scored five times. Without the captain Carrick’s team would surely struggle, as his hat-trick against Ipswich underlined.

Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha have been key support acts, scoring four goals each (Cunha also has two assists), and Benjamin Sesko has impressed with five goals at an average of one every 70.8 minutes.

United’s rearguard is the achilles heel: 13 goals conceded in the 10 home matches (Arsenal have allowed seven, City nine) is hardly parsimonious, so on Sunday the visitors will hope to prosper by hogging the ball, stymieing the opportunity for fast breaks that Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha and Sesko thrive on, and going at pace at the creaky defence.

City did not do this enough in Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League victory at Porto, perhaps because Elliot Anderson was stood down, and perhaps, too, because Maresca’s nascent team are in the work-in-progress phase.

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson has settled quickly at Manchester City after his £116m move from Nottingham Forest. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP

Anderson has looked a natural schemer since his £116m transfer from Nottingham Forest, running contests. In last Saturday’s 1-0 win over Coventry his display was Rodri-esque: a big call, but no exaggeration as the 23-year-old sprayed passes around, snuffed out danger, demanded to be found when under pressure and showed a spurt of speed to escape traffic.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United have their own midfield lieutenant: Kobbie Mainoo, who has started nine of the 10 home league games under Carrick, scoring once and assisting once. The match he missed? The Leeds reverse, which is surely no coincidence because the 21-year-old’s ability to mould time and space is priceless in the hurly-burly of the 100mph Premier League – as his masterclass versus Ipswich reiterated.

Harry Maguire calls the lad from Stockport United “midfield monster” so in the showdown between Mainoo and Anderson we may witness the derby’s defining battle – and the future of England’s engine room.

A United victory would send those of the red persuasion home happy, bragging rights secured in the workplace and local hostelries. But an underlying discontent will remain: at the longstanding grievance regarding the Glazers’ ownership that has haemorrhaged resources and saddled the club with a near £1.3bn debt, and at the recent initiative designed to eliminate the black market resale of tickets.

It is a worthy act but the accusation from fans is of a draconian approach. In July United began contacting supporters who used six or more devices to access accounts linked to the club or to forward tickets, on the basis this suggested the potential buying of seats to resell. Those in question were asked why multiple accounts were accessed, to identify the differing devices used, and for photo ID to prove validity.

A joint statement by six fan groups complained “of longstanding supporters who have followed Manchester United for decades, often across multiple generations of the same family, being treated as suspects”.

The dispute continues. On Tuesday the 1958 said: “Supporters are now facing serious sanctions which can remove their right to attend matches. We believe nobody should face such action without being told clearly what they are accused of and being shown the evidence used to justify it. If there is clear, substantive evidence of serious wrongdoing or organised ticket touting, show it. No loyal supporter should be treated as guilty without being given a fair opportunity to understand and challenge the case against them.”

United said that in addition to the sanctions and warnings, they had identified 1,617 accounts that required further review owing to “unusual activity”.

So before the derby will be the latest protest against the latest issue that shows the fracture between proud institution and proud fanbase. Against this backdrop Carrick hopes to extend United’s proud home record – which viewed through the prism of the disconnect between club and supporters is particularly impressive.

Sports.title: Emery takes responsibility as Forest strike late at winless Aston Villa
Sports.content:
This summer there were a couple of significant pieces of the puzzle for Oliver Glasner to put into place at Nottingham Forest. The first was a mobile striker to lead the line and the other was a right wing-back to fit his favoured 3-4-3 system. Enter Liam Delap and Daniel Muñoz, both of whom had a big say in Forest’s first win under Glasner, though the match-winner was one of the old brigade in Igor Jesus.

Delap registered his first Forest goal in style, a powerful shot from 25 yards and Muñoz was involved in the slick move that culminated in Igor Jesus reading Morgan Gibbs-White’s exquisite backheel to down Aston Villa, who remain winless in the Premier League.

That the winner came down Villa’s left made things even more painful from their perspective. For the final 12 minutes, including six in stoppage time, John McGinn was operating as an emergency left-back after Ian Maatsen’s injury reduced them to 10 men. By the 63rd minute, after sending on Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye for their Villa debuts, Unai Emery had used all five substitutions; Pau Torres was forced off with a hamstring problem midway through the first half that could sideline him for a month and Tammy Abraham and Alysson, who pulled Villa level, arrived at the interval. Abraham replaced Nicolas Jackson, who Emery felt was at risk of a second yellow card.

Those changes left Villa unable to replace Maatsen after the full-back was cynically fouled by James McAtee, whom Emery felt should have been sent off for the challenge. Emery said the video assistant referee, Timothy Wood, should have flagged the incident to the referee, Andy Madley. “It’s a clear tackle behind the player and, for me, it should be a red card,” he said. “But it’s not an excuse for how we played the second half. We played so poorly and this is my responsibility.”

View image in fullscreen Unai Emery, the Aston Villa head coach, is without a win in the Premier League this season. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

For the second successive season, Villa are winless in their opening four league matches and for so long it seemed they would again fail to score. Alysson’s header from McGinn’s dainty cross after a short corner meant they were spared ruminating on the moment Matz Sels twice denied Victor Lindelöf. In between Sels repelling Lindelöf with his feet and taking his side-foot shot to the face, Murillo smacked an attempted clearance against his own post. Lindelöf has scored one goal in almost six years, his last in November 2023.

Villa were rattled by Forest seizing the lead 45 seconds into the second half. Murillo dispossessed Emiliano Buendía, snapping into a challenge after Boubacar Kamara’s flick and then Delap jinked clear of Ross Barkley. Delap’s next couple of touches took the ball out of his feet, dribbling diagonally across the pitch before sending an unerring right-foot shot into the Villa net.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Emery sent on Mbaye and Manzambi in place of Buendía and Barkley but their arrivals did not bring instant success. Instead Delap thought he had doubled his and Forest’s tally, only for the offside flag and a VAR check to deny him. A few moments earlier Tyrone Mings, a first-half substitute for the injured Torres, made a desperate block to thwart Dan Ndoye after superb holdup play by Delap.

Forest, without key defenders Nikola Milenkovic and Jair Cunha through injury, had been readying Igor Jesus when Villa scored, but the striker still arrived to replace Ndoye, who, after a first-half collision with Maatsen, was left with what Glasner described as “a nose like a boxer in the 12th round”. At that point, Villa Park was primed for a grandstand finale, but Forest also roused. Zion Suzuki was twice called into action, his best save clambering down to his right to keep out a Xaver Schlager header, but then Igor Jesus popped up with the winner.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap (right) opened his account for Nottingham Forest with a 46th-minute strike. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Muñoz exchanged passes with Gibbs-White, who eliminated three Villa defenders with a sumptuous flick before Igor Jesus coolly passed the ball past Suzuki to maintain Glasner’s pristine record against Emery. Glasner has not lost in eight meetings against Emery, winning six and drawing two.

“I spoke to him before the game and it’s still 5-2 for him, five European trophies to two,” said Forest’s head coach. “So I said to myself: ‘Oliver Glasner, stay humble.’ And this is how I will stay. The players deserve all the credit, because they did so well, and our fans deserve credit because they supported us, and so now we all go back and will have a lovely Saturday evening.”

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli ends seven-month goal drought with sensational 32-minute hat-trick
Sports.content:
Gabriel Martinelli ended his seven-month exile from the scoresheet as he netted a stunning hat-trick for Al Hilal.

After Ollie Watkins found the opener in the Saudi Pro League clash, Martinelli found his first of the day on 18 minutes with a low finish.

2 Martinelli ended his wait for a club-level goal by scoring three for Al Hilal Credit: Getty

The former Arsenal winger's second followed two minutes before the half-time whistle as he cut inside and fire into the bottom corner.

Moments into the second half, Martinelli completed his treble with a tap-in on the line.

There were 32 minutes separating the first and third goals, the last of which was his final contribution before being substituted.

Martinelli has scored his first goals for Al Hilal since signing from Arsenal in a £60million move at the end of the summer window.

He has also netted at club level for the first time in seven months.

The 25-year-old's most recent goal before his weekend performance came in Arsenal's 4-0 FA Cup win over Wigan Athletic in February.

New challenge for Martinelli

Just weeks after winning the Premier League title, Martinelli finalised an exit from Arsenal.

The forward totalled 62 goals and 36 assists in 278 appearances across seven seasons for the north Londoners.

Martinelli was not named in their squads for the wins over Coventry City and Aston Villa at the start of this season amid exit speculation.

Turkish giants Galatasaray made an initial enquiry to sign the Brazilian international and later submitted a verbal offer worth £38.4m.

2 Martinelli scored his final goal for Arsenal in February Credit: Getty

However, he rejected the move and eventually joined Al Hilal, with the £60m switch being a record sale for Arsenal.

Leandro Trossard was another left winger to leave the Gunners as he joined Besiktas.

Christos Tzolis was brought in from Club Brugge but, with a total of five forwards completing exits, Arsenal's squad depth was questioned.

talkSPORT's Adrian Durham claimed that they have become 'weaker' now that the transfer window has closed.

But Arsenal have already made an excellent start to the defence of their league title by winning all of their four opening matches.

Victories against Coventry, Villa, Chelsea and Sunderland have put them top of the table with eight goals scored and one conceded.

Sports.title: Aston Villa warned record signing Nicolas Jackson’s discipline is an ‘absolute disgrace’ after being hooked at half time
Sports.content:
Aston Villa warned record signing Nicolas Jackson’s discipline is an ‘absolute disgrace’ after being hooked at half time

Jason Cundy has cautioned Aston Villa over Nicolas Jackson and his ill-discipline after he was booked against Nottingham Forest.

The striker was shown a yellow card by referee Andy Madley before half-time in the 2-1 Premier League defeat at Villa Park.



4 Jackson was booked late on in the first half of Villa's home defeat to Forest Credit: Getty

Tammy Abraham was then brought on to replace Jackson at the start of the second half by manager Unai Emery with the score 0-0.

It was a change that didn't deliver the desired effort on the pitch as Villa extended their winless league run to four.

Reacting to the substitution on the GameDay Phone-In, Cundy said: "It's a big call that, bringing off Nicolas Jackson and bringing on Tammy Abraham at half-time, that's a big call.



"Whenever you see that, you think, 'Right, he's obviously not doing what he wants'. If you take a striker off and go with a straight swap... that's a strange decision, and then it doesn't work..."

Villa fan Ez then called into the show and explained what happened in regards to Jackson's yellow.



"He got needlessly booked in the first half. We were in possession two thirds of the way down the pitch and for some reason, we look back and there's a Forest player on the floor."

Jackson discipline is a 'problem'

talkSPORT's resident Chelsea fan Cundy then recalled what he saw in regards to Jackson and bookings at his beloved side before the 25-year-old signed for Villa in a club-record £65million deal.



"I promise you now, Nicolas Jackson's discipline is an absolute disgrace. I watched him pick up red and yellow cards for fun, he won't learn. He has a discipline problem."

Ez then revealed: "We must have had a little break for an injury or something, and the players gathered around the touchline by Emery.

"I could see him absolutely bawling at Nicolas Jackson, and then he didn't come on in the second half. So, I think it's a discipline thing."

4 Jackson was hooked at the start of the second half Credit: Getty



4 Emery is said to have been furious with the striker on the touchline Credit: Getty

Jackson received 18 yellow cards in 81 appearances at Chelsea and was also shown two straight reds, with Cundy offering more insight into the ill-discipline.

"The thing with Jackson, he will pick up a yellow card not for a tackle.

"He'll pick it up for saying something to the referee, pulling someone's shirt... kicking the ball away, all of that, not when you put in a mistimed tackle."



"His ill-discipline is terrible," he added. "Maybe that's it, maybe that's why Emery has gone, 'Right, I ain't having that. I've warned you, off.'"

Emery revealed after the full-time whistle that the booking played a role in his decision to bring Jackson off.

"Nico Jackson had a yellow card and the referee was telling us that he needed to keep calm.

4 Villa lost out on the three points as Thiago bagged a late winner for Forest Credit: Getty



"If not, he was close to having another yellow card. I know Jackson and he could have one action with his power being dangerous for another yellow. It was my decision."

Jackson's appearance against Forest was his fourth for Villa since the summer move from Chelsea.

Liam Delap and Igor Thiago scored either side of an Alysson goal to hand Forest their first win of the season.

Sports.title: Frustrated Roberto De Zerbi gives immediate post-match lecture to star as Spurs set unwanted club record
Sports.content:
Frustrated Roberto De Zerbi gives immediate post-match lecture to star as Spurs set unwanted club record

Tottenham's disastrous start to the season officially sank to its lowest ebb.

Roberto De Zerbi's side were held to a scoreless draw at home against Everton on Saturday evening, prolonging Spurs' wait for a first win of the season.

3 Spurs had the majority of the ball but nothing to show for it against the Toffees Credit: Getty

Worryingly, the result extended Spurs' Premier League goal drought.

The 0-0 scoreline meant it is the first time in Spurs' history that they have failed to score in any of their first four league fixtures in a single campaign.

Tottenham's wait for a goal was not aided by an overwhelmingly toothless display in the final third against the Toffees as they mustered just two shots on target.

Roberto De Zerbi in heated exchange with Mathys Tel

Amid his side's attacking woes, De Zerbi was left frustrated by substitute Mathys Tel.

Immediately after the full-time whistle, the Italian went on to the pitch and animatedly gave a lecture to Tel, who stood with his hands on his hips.

Tel, who entered the contest just after the hour mark, struggled to make his mark as he completed just 12 passes and mustered only one shot.

De Zerbi later addressed the incident in his post-match press conference, explaining that his gestures to Tel were intended to convey that 'the striker can't play with his back to the goal.'

Why did De Zerbi give a post-match lecture to Tel?

"He has to play like a striker, looking at the goal, or on the cross for [Andy] Robertson," De Zerbi said.

"He has to stay inside. He started as a striker, now he's playing as a winger.

"But I love Mathys as a player and a guy, there is not a problem."

3 De Zerbi made sure he got his point across to Tel Credit: AFP

The Frenchman was not alone when it came to an anonymous display, prompting ex-Spurs midfielder and talkSPORT host Jamie O'Hara to unleash in a furious post-match rant.

Jamie O'Hara reacts to Spurs' draw

"It's absolute guff," O'Hara said on the GameDay Phone-In.

"Honestly, I can't get my head around it. They are bang average. They [Everton] just sat there, parked the bus.

"It's like 11 lads on the pitch who have never played with each other.

"It's a joke. We are a joke. We can't score a goal.

"How can you play in the Premier League and not score a goal?"

3 Spurs' draw with Everton was their second in a row from the opening four games Credit: Getty

O'Hara also questioned a string of Spurs' summer arrivals, especially given their gargantuan transfer spend.

"Savio runs down dead ends," O'Hara said.

"Marmoush looks like he's got cement in his feet. Solanke's miles off it. Bergvall comes on and looks like a kid. Tonali, we spent £100m and he's non-existent in a game.

"What is going on with this side? It's absolutely shocking."

Sports.title: Unai Emery fears Aston Villa star could be sidelined for a ‘long, long time’ in brutal injury blow
Sports.content:
Unai Emery fears Aston Villa star could be sidelined for a ‘long, long time’ in brutal injury blow

When it rains at Villa Park, it pours.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery fears Ian Maatsen faces a 'long, long time' on the sideline after he suffered an ankle injury in the 2-1 loss to Nottingham Forest.

3 Maatsen had established himself as Villa's starting left-back following Lucas Digne's departure Credit: Getty

Maatsen was scythed down by Forest's James McAtee in the 80th minute but could not continue.

Unfortunately for Villa, they had made all of their substitutions, so they could not replace the Dutch left-back.

It meant John McGinn, who began the match at right wing, had to moonlight as a makeshift left-back.

In a brutal twist, Forest's winner came down that side as Daniel Munoz's cross was deftly flicked on by Morgan Gibbs-White to Igor Jesus, who swept home from close range.

Unai Emery gives worrying update on Ian Maatsen's injury

Speaking after the contest, Emery conceded he did not have a concrete update on Maatsen's injury.

"But the information I have, an ankle injury, it may be a long, long time," Emery said.

The Villa boss was also frustrated that McAtee was allowed to remain on the pitch.

"The tackle, it was one for VAR," Emery continued.

"I think VAR should call the referee to watch it and show a red card.

"We finish with 10 men and they finish with 11."

3 Emery's side are now winless in their opening four league fixtures Credit: Getty

Worryingly, Maatsen wasn't the only Villa starter who picked up an injury against Forest.

Star centre-back Pau Torres also exited early, coming off in the first half with a hamstring issue.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis set for Champions League inclusion

The Spaniard's injury now looks set to result in Taylor Harwood-Bellis being drafted into Villa's Champions League squad.

Harwood-Bellis joined Villa this summer from Southampton for an initial £25million but was a notable omission from Villa's 23-man squad for Europe this season.

However, the one-time England international now looks set to be jettisoned into Villa's Champions League list.

Per UEFA rules, a player who has been injured or ill for at least 60 days can be temporarily replaced by a player who was registered with their club before the List A deadline.

3 Torres' absence will be keenly felt due to his importance in Villa's build-up play Credit: Getty

Speaking on Harwood-Bellis, who was not included in the matchday squad for the loss against Forest, Emery noted 'his time is coming after Pau's injury'.

Villa will look to pick up their first domestic win this season next Wednesday when they make the short trip to Coventry City in the Carabao Cup third round.

Sports.title: ‘Atrocious’ – Chelsea make unwanted 65-year history as ex-Premier League boss left stunned
Sports.content:
Hull City became the latest club to breach Chelsea's fragile defence and condemn the west London club to an unwanted record.

Mohamed Belloumi's 28th-minute leveller ensured the Blues have now gone 20 league games without a clean sheet for the first time in 65 years.

5 Hull's leveller ensured Chelsea reached the defensive milestone

The Blues reached the unwanted feat in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Hull at Stamford Bridge.

It is the first time they have conceded two or more goals in the first four matches of a league campaign in ten years as well.

Xabi Alonso’s side were aiming to banish the memories of last weekend’s defeat at Arsenal and started in blistering fashion.

Morgan Rogers’ expertly-taken finish fired Chelsea into a seventh-minute lead but some suspect defending handed Hull a way back into the match.

A hopeful ball into the box was misjudged by Jorrel Hato, allowing Belloumi to fire the Tigers level.

Chelsea, who have conceded three times in two of their three home games in all competitions this season, once again showed their defensive frailties and talkSPORT co-commentator Steve Bruce issued his own scathing assessment.

Defensive flaws

“Absolutely atrocious from Chelsea,” Bruce said on Game Day Live. “A long punt up the middle. They haven’t dealt with that one for a start.

“Then it’s gone into the corner flag, then they haven’t stopped the cross coming in.

“The cross is one of these looping things that’s come into the box.

“Hato’s misjudged it badly, got underneath it, bounced over the top of him and there was Belloumi to strike it with his left foot and give the ‘keeper no chance.

5 The Chelsea boss was seen deliberating with his side as they chased a leveller Credit: Getty

“It’s the first time they’ve been anywhere near Chelsea’s goal, I can’t remember the goalkeeper touching the ball but they’ve got themselves level.”

Things got even worse for Alonso’s men just six minutes later when Belloumi lashed home from the edge of the box to fire the Premier League new boys in front.

Chelsea got themselves back on level terms in the 66th minute when Joao Pedro produced a neat finish after good work from Cole Palmer down the left.

But there is plenty of work to do for Alonso and his shaky backline who conceded three in the midweek Carabao Cup win over Leeds.

The Spaniard lined up against Hull with a back four comprising of Hato, Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Malo Gusto.

The midweek cup goalfest followed Sunday's 2-1 defeat at Arsenal and the 4-3 win over Brighton.

5 Joao Pedro rescued a point for his team with a well-taken finish

The Blues set the tone for a potentially leaky campaign by shipping twice in their season opener at Fulham.

Chelsea's only clean sheet this season came in the 2-0 Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town last month.

Bruce lauds Hull's start to the season

"If one team was going to win it towards the end it was Hull," the former Tigers boss said.

"Chelsea threw everything at them in terms of forward players on the pitch.

"God knows what formation they were playing at the end but every attacking player was on there and they left themselves wide open defensively.

"Hull brought on their subs and had a bit of pace and power and caused them all sorts of problems in forward areas.

5 Steve Bruce was left hugely impressed by his former club's display at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

5 Hull City fans rightly serenaded their players after the hard-fought 2-2 draw Credit: Getty

"They had a big opportunity with about two minutes left and they'll be regretting that chance they missed.

"Hull have done very, very well I have to say," Bruce continued. "They're well-drilled, well-organised, difficult to play against, difficult to beat.

"On the counter attack, they're a threat. You can understand why they've picked up a few points.

"They've got big confidence from the number of points they've picked up over the last few weeks.

"They've given themselves a right opportunity and who'd have thought with the fixture list that they started with this season, they'd be practically top of the Premier League."

Sports.title: Sorba Thomas makes Premier League appearance one day after rollover car crash
Sports.content:
Sorba Thomas was brought on for Hull City against Chelsea a day after being involved in a rollover crash.

Images of the Wales winger's car upside down on a residential road spread across social media on Friday morning.

2 Thomas has returned to the pitch following his crash Credit: Getty

Hull later revealed that Thomas, who was signed from Stoke City in a £10million deal, escaped was 'completely unscathed'.

He was named in their matchday squad for the Premier League trip to Chelsea, with the 27-year-old featuring as a substitute.

Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic opted to bring him on for Elliot Stroud in the 60th minute of the 2-2 draw at Stamford Bridge.

It was his second league appearance for the Tigers, with the first coming in the 0-0 draw with Aston Villa last weekend.

Many were surprised to see him in action given the state of his car just over 24 hours ago.

Chelsea and Hull battle for draw

Thomas entered play as Hull led 2-1 courtesy of two goals from Mohamed Belloumi.

But Joao Pedro brought Chelsea level, having assisted Morgan Rogers for their opener earlier in the match.

Chelsea became the first side this season to score against Hull, who did not concede versus Manchester United, Coventry City or Villa.

However, the Tigers remain unbeaten on their top flight return and have the joint-best defence with Arsenal and Leeds United.

They are third in the table and may well have dismissed any fears over relegation back to the Championship.

2 Chelsea and Hull shared the points in a tight contest Credit: AFP

As it stands, Hull could be in contention to qualify for Europe later in the season.

It would be a remarkable story for a club who last played Premier League football before the current campaign in 2016/17.

Chelsea on the other hand are a point behind them in fourth and have conceded at least two goals in every leage match.

The reverse fixture at the MKM Stadium is scheduled for March 20.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers joins elite Chelsea group just four league games into Blues career
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers joins elite Chelsea group just four league games into Blues career

Morgan Rogers continued his stunning start to life at Chelsea with yet another goal.

The club-record £117million signing from Aston Villa found the target inside six minutes of the 2-2 draw with Hull City on Saturday.



2 A fine strike from Rogers put Chelsea ahead at home to Hull Credit: Getty

Rogers was fed the ball from Joao Pedro, and then fired low into the bottom corner to hand Chelsea an early lead.

He has joined an elite group of Chelsea heroes who have scored or assisted in each of the first four Premier League games of a season.

Didier Drogba was first to do so in the 2010/11 campaign as he netted four and assisted four.



Cesc Fabregas followed him with six assists in 2014/15, as Diego Costa scored seven in that same run.

Costa also bagged four goals and an assist in 2016/17, and then Eden Hazard hit two goals and two assists at the start of 2018/19.



Hull then equalised shortly before the half-hour mark as Mohamed Belloumi struck after some poor Chelsea defending.

The Algerian scored a second moments later as the visitors fought back to lead.



However, Joao Pedro was on hand to score a second for Chelsea by thumping into the roof of the net.

Rogers goals and assists for Chelsea so far

On his Premier League debut for the club, Rogers scored for Chelsea in their 3-2 victory against west London neighbours Fulham.

He then assisted Pedro Neto as they beat Brighton 4-3, before hitting an early opener in the 2-1 loss at Arsenal.

2



Rogers' goal against Hull came after he came off the bench and assisted three times in the 6-3 Carabao Cup win over Leeds United.

Whilst their attacking quality was on show once again, Chelsea still have concerns over their defence.

They have conceded two goals in all of their matches this season bar one, the 2-0 Carabao Cup win over Luton Town.

Saturday's result at home to Hull has left them fourth in the table and a point behind their opponents.

Sports.title: Derby player stretchered off in neck brace after lengthy stoppage as manager gives update
Sports.content:
Derby player stretchered off in neck brace after lengthy stoppage as manager gives update

Derby striker Henrik Meister was stretchered off in a neck brace after going down off the ball during the clash with Birmingham.

The worrying scenes unfolded at the start of the second half at Pride Park, as the Dane went to ground, causing play to be temporarily halted.

4 Meister received immediate medical attention after going down with no one near him

4 The striker was stretchered off the pitch and was seen in a neck brace

Appearing to have suffered a head injury, medical staff immediately came on to the pitch, before a stretcher was called for.

A seven-minute delay followed, as Meister received treatment, with it becoming clear the player would be unable to continue.

Meister was ultimately moved onto a stretcher and was carried off the pitch to a standing ovation from both sets of fans.

Reporting the incident at the time, Derby wrote on X: "A lengthy delay at the start of the half as Meister goes down off the ball and is stretchered from the field.

"We're all with you, Henrik."

Meister 'OK', says Derby boss

After the match, which saw Birmingham claim a 2-1 win, Derby boss John Eustace revealed Meister was in a stable condition, and said he will undergo concussion protocols.

Giving an update, Eustace said: "To lose him just after half-time was tough.

"It was difficult, but he's OK now. He's having concussion protocols. We'll just have to see how he is. I've been speaking to him and he seems okay."

Meister had been making his first start for Derby after being handed his debut in a 3-0 Championship defeat at West Ham last weekend.

The 22-year-old joined the club on a season-long loan from Serie B side Pisa less than two weeks ago.

4 Henrik Meister joined Derby this summer

With the score at 1-1 at the time of Meister's substitution, Birmingham went on to take the lead through Paik Seung-ho on 64 minutes.

The Rams went in front on 40 minutes, as Bobby Clark fired in from a tight angle.

But Birmingham hit back immediately, as Carlos Vicente equalised less than two minutes later.

The Blues opted for an early substitution at half-time, as manager Chris Davies brought Paik on for Jhon Solis in midfield.

And the switch paid off almost instantly, as the South Korean headed home from Liam Millar's corner.

This proved to be the winning goal, as Birmingham held on to their lead even through 13 minutes of second-half injury time, largely due to Meister's injury.

4 John Eustace is navigating a tough start to the season

The result leaves Derby still in the Championship relegation zone, as they remain 21st in the table.

John Eustace's side have made a disappointing start to the campaign which has seen them win just once.

The Rams have lost six of their opening seven league matches, as well as claiming a draw against Cardiff in their second game.

As for Birmingham, victory moves them into eighth place on 10 points, with this the last of the Championship play-off places following the league's decision to expand this last term.

Sports.title: Elena Rybakina WINS the US Open: New world No 1 dethrones racquet-smashing Aryna Sabalenka in electric three-set battle in New York
Sports.content:
Elena Rybakina WINS the US Open: New world No 1 dethrones racquet-smashing Aryna Sabalenka in electric three-set battle in New York

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

First, she took her status as No1, and then Elena Rybakina dethroned Aryna Sabalenka as reigning US Open champion, dissecting the two-time winner in New York 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to win her third Grand Slam title.

For Rybakina, victory adds lustre to the top spot, earned with a quarter-final win that felt incongruous. The Kazakh knew it, and stressed that she could not celebrate this mammoth achievement yet, not with the tournament ongoing. Now, she has put herself just one major away from the full set after wins in Melbourne and Wimbledon. She has also become the third woman this century to win both of the hard-court Slams in a single season.

The second was Sabalenka. She had hoped to make history herself, as the third woman in the Open era to ‘three-peat’, and become the undisputed Queen of New York. Instead, she stuttered, unable to consistently channel the ruthlessness which has defined her run over these two weeks, and was left in tears as she vowed to 'do better' next year.

Throughout the tournament, Sabalenka has stressed the importance of maintaining focus: tuning out the noise around concerns over her form, or whether she might hold on to her ranking, and channelling everything into her performance. But yesterday, she appeared to step onto court bubbling over, frustrated with the deficiencies in her performance even in the earliest stages of the match.

Sabalenka looked unsettled as the pair exchanged opening holds, the opposite of Rybakina’s picture of calm on the other side of the net. Rybakina normally makes the sport look effortless, but this was thrown into sharper relief by the quick unravelling of Sabalenka.

With every unforced error - 15 to Rybakina’s five - there seemed to be an expression, hands thrown up, head tipped back, frantic miming to her box, but rather than offer a release, Sabalenka only wound herself tighter. After the double fault that handed her opponent the first-set break, she was given a warning for smacking a ball away, but hitting was similarly frustrated in-play as Sabalenka looked for desperate winners she couldn’t make.

Elena Rybakina is the new Queen of New York after winning the US Open in three thrilling sets

Aryna Sabalenka crashed her racquet into the court as the final set slipped away from her

Join the discussion What does Rybakina's intense victory say about the mental toughness needed to dominate tennis today?

Much has been made of the potency of Rybakina’s serve, but the Kazakh carried off the opener well below her lethal best, making only 27 per cent of her first serves. When she pulled them off, Sabalenka was flummoxed. But even when she didn’t, there was an accuracy to her second that continued to cause problems for her opponent.

Rybakina, by contrast, had the very measure of Sabalenka’s serve, and was capable of dragging out the Belarusian’s service games and bullying her into defence under-fire. The 27-year-old peppered her with four break points before the fifth finally told for 3-2.

Sabalenka stepped back onto court visibly more settled. There were fewer errors, and fewer admonishments. But there was no drop in Rybakina’s level, as she continued to play her game, and play it well. She chased Sabalenka to 5-4, and pulled off an enormous hold in the 10th game to deny her rival her first break point.

Rybakina wasn’t to hold on for long, however. The two rivals’ meetings often spill into three sets, and Sabalenka’s improved accuracy - and mood - swung the second set.

This was the fuel Rybakina needed to act more decisively in the third, and immediately, she was all over Sabalenka’s serve, looking for cracks in her game. The pair met at deuce three times before the 28-year-old could see out her opening hold, while Rybakina skipped through hers, hungry for the next attempt to break her opponent.

She would not have to wait long, with Sabalenka again the picture of fury as she crashed her racquet into the floor, sent spinning by a string of Rybakina’s forehand winners. Instead of a second code violation warning, the punishment instead was the break Rybakina snatched.

In the seventh game, 2-4 down, Rybakina reached break point again, with the gift of a double fault from across the net. Sabalenka bent down to her knees, tipped her head to her racquet, as if praying for composure. Instead, more faults, more errors, broken again. Sabalenka’s last effort was to give the court another thrashing with her racquet. She all but walked off as Rybakina sent down her championship-winning ace.

But the new champion will not have needed grace from her opponent. She has her trophy instead.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia destroys Conor Benn with brutal second-round TKO to retain WBC welterweight title in Las Vegas showdown
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia destroys Conor Benn with brutal second-round TKO to retain WBC welterweight title in Las Vegas showdown

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ryan Garcia sealed a stunning second-round TKO win over Conor Benn in Las Vegas on Saturday night, retaining his WBC welterweight title in the process.

Benn ran blindly to the slaughter - in a fight which was always a lunge too far - and was left groveling on hands and knees at the feet of the new face of American and Mexican boxing.

Garcia took just four minutes and 25 seconds to devastate and humiliate the upstart son of Nigel the great.

Benn’s predictable sally forth from the first bell was as pointless, desperate and doomed to disaster as The Charge of the Light Brigade.

He was stopped in his tracks by the barrage of left hooks which have taken Garcia to the welterweight championship of the world, over which he will reign for as long as he likes.

The first round was but a prelude to the carnage to come in the 85 seconds which the first round lasted. A punishment doubled by the dynamite which also explodes from Garcia's right fist.

Ryan Garcia sealed a stunning second-round TKO win over Conor Benn in Las Vegas

Garcia took just four minutes and 25 seconds to devastate and humiliate the British star

The 28-year-old retained his WBC welterweight title after the devastating display in Sin City

Conor was reduced to crawling on the canvas by a two-fisted assault to which he had no answer. When he staggered drunkenly to his feet referee Thomas Taylor looked long and hard into his glazed eyes before letting him carry on.

The kill was mercifully swift. A combination of lefts and rights which the third man in the ring could no longer ignore. Any more and Benn would have heading to hospital.

This is a warning which his handlers must not forget. This was fight too much, too soon. As Garcia had warned he done nothing to deserve the tilt at the WBC belt his father had worn with such pride.

Nor his elevation the top of a bill in the T-Mobile arena nor in this Mecca of boxing Whether he will ever be ready to mix with the company of prize-ring loyalty is doubtful.

He was not only outclassed, out-sped an out-thought but was treated to punching of almighty power with which his dad could not gift him.

The last 24 hours before the first bell had been consumed by doom-casts about Benn’s drastic weight draining to reach the welter limit of 147 lbs.

Followed by extraordinary claims that he had put on more than two stones following Friday’s weigh-in which, if authentic, would have catapulted him into the ring three divisions even heavier than the super-middleweights.

The truth would out as his robe slipped off. But if he had gorged himself between stepping on the scales and the first bell that might done him much good. Such drastic shifts in poundage are as debilitating as dehydration.

If this was another of the mind games played by Benn and Garcia throughout the wind up and build up it seemed doubtful that any of that would have a material effect on the fight itself. Would anyone in this hardest of all games risk being beaten by indigestion.

Conor was reduced to crawling on the canvas by an assault to which he had no answer

The referee swiftly waved off the bout after a barrage of punches from the American star

The substantive issue was Garcia’s boxing class and knock out power versus Benn’s frenzy and punch resistance.

For the high-paying fans – Benn’s long-haulers from the old country and Garcia’s Gen Z armies of groups from his two nations of identification the US and Mexico – what mattered most was that both delivered the barn-burner of a fight they promised.

Quite beautifully those three congregations fell silent together in commemoration of one boxer who never gave in, never gave up, never delivered a disappointing fight, never offended anyone, never betrayed a friend.

The giant screens in the 02 went into black and white mode for a nostalgic picture of Ricky Hatton who died too young as the previous British fighter to top the bill in what was until recently the fight capital of the world. Over to you Master Benn.

Garcia came to the ring to the strains of a patriotic Mexican song, wrapped in that country’s flag and to rapturous acclaim from the baying Amex majority in the house.

Unabashed and as expected Benn went instantly on the offensive only to be met by barrage of Garcia’s trademark left hooks.

Less than three minutes later it was all over.

Sports.title: Ollie Robinson is England's most lethal bowler for more than a century - tougher tests are to come, but here's why - and how - he's grabbed his second chance by the horn, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Ollie Robinson is England's most lethal bowler for more than a century - tougher tests are to come, but here's why - and how - he's grabbed his second chance by the horn, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

The coffee machine was on the blink at England's team hotel on Friday morning, with Ollie Robinson – his four-week-old daughter Evie cradled in his arms – waiting patiently at the head of the queue. It felt like one of the few times this summer he had been held up by circumstances beyond his control.

Even after Pakistan's No10 Razaullah put a small dent in his figures that evening with his six-laden innings of 81, Robinson finished the home Test season with numbers once thought possible only in the era of uncovered pitches and rudimentary batting techniques.

After taking seven wickets at 11 in his only Test against New Zealand at Lord's, including a first over that turned into a triple-wicket maiden, he hoovered up 21 at under nine against Pakistan.

It all added up to 28 at 9.32, making him the first seamer to take 20 wickets in an English summer at an average below ten. And no English bowler of any hue has achieved the feat since Tony Lock with his left-arm spin ran through New Zealand in 1958.

'It'll probably never happen again,' he said with a smile as he awaited his latte. The Australians, due here next summer to defend the Ashes, will be hoping he's right.

One of the kneejerk responses on social media to his success has been to decry the quality of Pakistan's batting, or to point out the assistance Robinson has received both from the pitches and from a Dukes ball that England are convinced is staying harder for longer.

The sensational Ollie Robinson finished the summer with 28 Test wickets at a 9.32 average

Yet, faced with exactly the same factors, none of his team-mates has matched his feats. Josh Tongue's 27 wickets this summer have come at 26, Jofra Archer's 23 at 24, and Gus Atkinson's 14 at 30. Good numbers, certainly – but nothing to touch Robinson.

Equally, there have been bowler-friendly summers before, but Robinson is nudging his way into some serious statistical company.

Only three England bowlers have taken more than his 104 Test wickets at an average lower than his 19: SF Barnes took 189 at 16, Johnny Briggs 118 at 17, and George Lohmann 112 at ten. Of those, Barnes played most recently – in 1914. There is a case, then, for arguing that Robinson is England's most effective bowler for 112 years.

Plenty has been said about his long absence from the side under Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes – essentially because of his relaxed attitude to fitness, which drove the management to distraction and eventually, in India in 2023-24, tipped them over the edge.

And history appeared to be repeating itself when the Bazballers didn't trust him to get through the decider against New Zealand at Trent Bridge in June, after he missed the Oval Test because of a knee niggle.

But, under Joe Root, Robinson was straight into the side against Pakistan, and took a wicket with the first ball of the series, nipping one back into the pads of Azan Awais at Headingley, and rarely pausing for breath.

Of his 28 victims this summer, 12 have been leg-before, and another five bowled. Nine have fallen for ducks, 11 more in single figures. He has been relentless.

'I've been trying to set the tone and land it on the spot,' he told Ian Ward on Sky Sports before play on Friday. 'Luckily, the batters are either nicking it or missing it.'

He has been thrown into the deep end under Joe Root after a lack of trust from Ben Stokes

He was being unduly modest. Robinson worked on his fitness while playing grade cricket for the University of Sydney over the winter, and was then made captain of Sussex's red-ball team – a move he said had given him the 'drive and motivation to love the game again'. England now use him to select which ball to pick from the box of options supplied by the umpires.

He has also been tweaking his skills and his action, working on his wobble-seam deliveries, while passing on advice to Tongue, and standing up a fraction taller at the crease. That has reduced his pace, from an average of nearly 83mph against South Africa four years ago to 78 against Pakistan.

Previously, England might have held that against him. But he has been so accurate that it hasn't mattered. Besides, the speed is provided by Archer, Tongue and Atkinson. They dovetail nicely, even if Razaullah made them look pedestrian for two hours on Friday evening.

He has been helped, too, by the wicketkeeping of Jamie Smith and, in Pakistan's second innings at Edgbaston, Jordan Cox, who were both excellent standing up to the stumps and creating a sense of claustrophobia from which the batsmen rarely escaped.

Above all, it all feels like a second chance for a 32-year-old who thought his time had gone. 'I thought I'd never play for England again,' he said after Root's team sealed a 3-0 win. 'But I've got a new ambition to keep going and push on. There's still a lot of hard work to do, but I'm just getting started.'

The three-match series in South Africa starting on December 17 will present a different challenge, with pitches in Johannesburg, Centurion and Cape Town less likely to do his bidding. For now, though, he can reflect on a job done so remorselessly that the record books have had as little respite as Pakistan's batsmen.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford reborn: How the Man United forward found his smile again after Old Trafford exile, Michael Carrick's role in easing his return and the key differences staff have noticed in training
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford reborn: How the Man United forward found his smile again after Old Trafford exile, Michael Carrick's role in easing his return and the key differences staff have noticed in training

It's the look of pure joy on Marcus Rashford’s face that stands out all these years later.

Leaping into the arms of Anthony Martial at the Etihad, Manchester United’s new local hero had just scored what turned out to be the winning goal 15 minutes into his first derby a decade ago.

The 18-year-old controlled a pass from Juan Mata and audaciously nutmegged Martin Demichelis to leave the Manchester City defender on his backside before sweeping the ball under Joe Hart.

‘Putting Demichelis on his a**e got as big a cheer as the goal itself,’ chuckles Dave Horrocks, one of Rashford’s first coaches at Fletcher Moss Rangers.

It crowned a quite remarkable breakthrough for Rashford at his boyhood club under Louis van Gaal in early 2016, which began with a two-goal debut off the bench against Midtjylland, at the time replacing George Best as United’s youngest-ever scorer in Europe.

Ryan Giggs, by then a coach on Van Gaal’s staff, recalled on The Debrief podcast with Rio Ferdinand this week how Rashford had convinced the Dutchman he was ready.

Rashford capped off a remarkable breakthrough at his boyhood club under Louis van Gaal in early 2016 with the winning goal against rivals Manchester City at the Eithad

Ryan Giggs recalled how he had been asked by Van Gaal to tell Rashford he had made the first team after the pair had been left impressed by him

‘I remember we got told about him,’ said Giggs. ‘The first team had finished training, so me and Louis went over and watched the reserves.

‘Marcus was playing in a small-sided game and he scored two goals: right foot, left foot, bang, bang. It was like, “what have we just seen?”. Louis turned to me and went, “you will tell him he is in my team”, and just walked off!’

Still, Rashford was only down to be on the bench in a Europa League tie against the Danes until Martial was injured in the warm-up. Horrocks was having dinner with Fletcher Moss secretary Ronny Jamieson in Didsbury as the story unfolded.

‘My phone pinged: “Marcus is in the squad”,’ says Horrocks. ‘Then ping: “He’s starting”. Ping: “He’s scored!”.’

The junior club’s membership doubled overnight, and there weren’t enough coaches to cope with all the kids.

Rashford made his Premier League debut against Arsenal at Old Trafford three days later and, incredibly, scored two more goals in another United win. A first England call-up soon followed.

Ten years on, he faces City again in Sunday's 199th Manchester derby at Old Trafford having made a fresh start at United over the summer.

Rashford has played in this fixture more than any other, and it’s one that has mirrored the ups and downs of his career.

As well as that memorable strike in 2016, his five goals to date include a late winner at Old Trafford in January 2023.

Rashford faces City again in Sunday's 199th Manchester derby at Old Trafford having made a fresh start at United over the summer

Then there was the 26th birthday bash at Chinawhite nightclub in the wake of a dismal 3-0 defeat to City in October of the same year that enraged Erik ten Hag, and Ruben Amorim’s decision to axe Rashford from the squad for the Etihad derby in December 2024 due to concerns over his attitude. Rashford didn’t play for United again before going out on loan to Aston Villa and Barcelona.

Giggs recounted the story this week of a dinner with Pep Guardiola eight years ago during which the City boss revealed that Rashford was the one United player he would like to have signed.

More recently, City were said to be hovering before Rashford agreed his current contract, although United’s insistence that their neighbours were one of only two clubs (the other was Liverpool) excluded from having the option to buy him for £40million this summer demonstrates the level of opposition to such a move inside Old Trafford.

Had things worked out differently, though, City could have got their hands on Rashford much earlier.

The youngster had joined Fletcher Moss at the age of six when his mother Melanie signed him up, and he was soon fast-tracked into one of United’s development centres.

But as the single mum worked to support her three boys and one daughter, Marcus spent his childhood moving between houses in Hulme, Moss Side, Chorlton, Withington and Wythenshawe.

When the family settled in Fallowfield, close to City’s academy on Platt Lane, a football-mad Rashford was inevitably drawn there on the nights he wasn’t training at United.

Fortunately, Horrocks agreed to drive Melanie, Marcus and his older brother Dwaine to The Cliff whenever he could because the family didn’t have a car and the journey meant taking several buses.

City are understood to have spoken to Rashford’s mother, but she had given United her word and Marcus signed at the age of nine.

‘He’s a United fan, so I don’t think City ever stood a chance,’ says Horrocks. ‘You have to understand he’s a Manchester lad, and the derby is the pot of gold for him – I hope he’s on the up again.’

Amorim axed Rashford from the squad for the Etihad derby in December 2024 due to concerns over his attitude and Rashford didn’t play for United again before loans at Villa and Barcelona

On a good run, it takes about 20 minutes to drive the ten miles from The Coffee House Cafe, where a mural of Rashford covers an outside wall in the heart of Withington, to the temporary black gates in the Mobberley countryside behind which sits the multi-million pound luxury home and golf course project that has been hindered by problems for some time.

It’s been quite the journey for the 28-year-old who was earning around £3,000-a-week when he first signed professional terms at the age of 17. Since agreeing a new contract in 2023 after a career-best 31-goal season, Rashford has been on £325,000-a-week.

The mural was daubed with racist graffiti when he missed a penalty as England lost to Italy on a shootout in the final of Euro 2020, shortly before receiving an MBE at Windsor Castle for his campaign to tackle child poverty during the pandemic.

Rashford sought the help of a sports psychologist during the darkest period of his career, and physically faced longstanding problems with his back and left shoulder.

There was the infamous tequila bender in Belfast which landed him in hot water with Ten Hag again, and the fallout with Amorim who stuck him in the bomb squad.

What hurt more than anything were the questions over his commitment to United and love of football, fuelled by concerns inside and outside the club over his demeanour.

Rashford felt sufficiently misunderstood to do an article for The Players’ Tribune titled Who I Really Am.

Perhaps leaving Old Trafford on loan has been the best thing. Had it not been for his wages, Rashford might well have joined Barcelona permanently this summer after winning the La Liga title there last season.

It’s understood he rejected interest from a dozen more clubs in England, Italy and Turkey before returning to United. Safe to say that if Amorim had still been in charge, there would have been no way back.

But Michael Carrick is a very different character. He was on the pitch that day in 2016 when Rashford scored against City, and has since been his first-team coach, caretaker manager and now head coach.

Carrick was on the pitch that day in 2016 when Rashford scored against City, and has since been his first-team coach, caretaker manager and now head coach

The two are said to have a good relationship which has eased a return that had looked so unlikely.

The rather sullen figure who left at the start of last year has been, according to sources, more cheerful than at any time they can remember from the moment he rejoined the squad at United’s pre-season training camp in Dublin. Once a poor time keeper, Rashford is now one of the first into training.

‘He couldn’t be making more of an effort on his side to make it work,’ said one insider.

Rashford was rested for Thursday’s Champions League tie against Sabah but got a good reception from the fans when he warmed up, some of whom had turned against him in the past.

He has played well enough to earn a place in Thomas Tuchel’s squad for the upcoming Nations League games, having returned to the England squad in time for the World Cup. Were it not for a minor hip problem, Rashford would probably have featured more in North America.

These are still early days, of course. With two years left on his contract at United, there are no guarantees about what will happen next.

For now, though, Rashford is back where many people feel he belongs – and City are in his sights again.

Sports.title: Zian Flemming keeps Ipswich on track with 3-2 win but Pierre Sage's Crystal Palace have to find answers soon, writes BOBBY MANZI
Sports.content:
Ipswich Town profited from Axel Disasi’s disastrous mistake to secure their second win of the season.

Crystal Palace controlled the affair and were good value for their lead after 14 minutes when Anan Khalaili capped an incisive move with a delightfully drilled finish into the bottom corner.

Against the run of play, though, Ipswich got back into the game when the Palace backline switched off, allowing Leif Davis to cross from the right with Emersonn on hand to guide a free-header past Walter Benitez.

The defence had completely stopped - Ipswich opened Palace up far too easily.

Palace continued to look comfortable after their blip in concentration until Disasi was late on Jack Clarke in the middle of the park, flying over the ball with his studs up and catching him on the shin.

Dismissing the centre-back was a simple decision for referee Chris Kavanagh, leaving Palace to defend for 55 minutes with 10 men.

Ipswich had been dull but the red card sparked them into life and it was Davis and Emersonn who combined again - this time in reverse order - to nudge Ipswich in front.

Emersonn’s miscued attempt fortuitously struck his shoulder and fell for Davis at the far post. The Palace defence had let a man roam free in the area yet again.

There was a retreat in the second half, though, as Ipswich looked to close the game out and that could have cost them. O’Neil must be wary of that and breed greater consistency into the performances, as they escaped without punishment but easily could have left frustrated.

They allowed Palace back into the game as Jorgen Strand Larsen shrugged off Issa Diop to get a shot away from just inside the area and drill it past Kjell Scherpen.

At that point, Palace appeared the team more likely to win the game - the impetus had swung in their favour despite being a man down.

Khalaili, who had scored his maiden Palace goal in the first half, should have wrapped up three points when he skied over the gaping net from just a few yards out.

Palace paid for the miss when the clock struck 90 minutes. Davis latched onto a cross from deep and headed goalbound. His attempt struck the crossbar but dropped kindly for substitute Zian Flemming, whose scuffed contact secured all three points.

Zian Flemming scored late-winner against ten-man Crystal Palace

‘It wasn’t perfect but we won,’ O’Neil said. ‘Palace had a couple of moments that we struggled with and we need to get better with that because we could easily have been punished in that small spell. But looking at the game as a whole, only one team deserved to win and thankfully we did.’

All things considered, it has been an impressive start from Gary O’Neil’s side. This was the first time Ipswich had come from behind to win in the Premier League since beating Tottenham Hotspur away in December 2001.

Yes, they have lost twice, but those defeats came against Liverpool and Manchester United.

Their defence is fragile but their attack is efficient. The reality is they have beaten two of the Premier League’s middling clubs and they are the outfits they must get results against if they have any chance of staying up. For now, they are heading in the right direction.

Palace, though, should be apprehensive considering their defence’s dismal start to the season.

Pierre Sage’s side have shipped 11 goals in their first four Premier League games, and the personnel inconsistency is not helping, with the starting back three changing in every game.

‘I’m aware we are conceding too many goals,’ said Sage. ‘We conceded the same goal three times: a cross in the box and not winning the ball in our box. We have to work on it and prevent crosses into the box.’

They did have 10 men for just under an hour on Saturday, but basic errors and lost concentration had been prevalent in the previous games, too.

For Ipswich’s first goal, the defence expected the linesman to raise his flag for offside and froze, gifting Ipswich a lifeline.

Pre-empting the whistle would be deemed criminal on a school playground, let alone in elite football. Most worryingly, Sage conceded that his players had made the same mistake in training this week.

There is no stability; Jaydee Canvot - one of Palace’s best talents - was dropped from the squad after one bad game. How can Sage expect his backline to gel if a young player is scapegoated for a poor performance?

Meanwhile, Palace have not kept a clean sheet in their last 10 Premier League matches - the problems precede Sage but he has shown little sign of finding the solution.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta seethes at penalty decision against Arsenal - despite 2-0 win sending them top - as he gives awkward interview about 'judo roll' incident: 'I'm so upset. It is unacceptable!'
Sports.content:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta lambasted the 'unacceptable' decision to award Sunderland a penalty in his side's hard-fought 2-0 win over the Black Cats. Arteta's side maintained their 100 per cent record in their title defence on Saturday night thanks to goals from Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka, but it could have been a very different story. The score was 0-0 when Sunderland were awarded a penalty after referee John Brooks adjudged Ezri Konsa to have dragged Dan Ballard to the floor at a Sunderland corner. After a VAR check, the decision stood, but David Raya dived low to his left to keep out Enzo Le Fee's effort. The Gunners' goals came after that moment, but that didn't stop Arteta making his feelings on the decision known post-match. 'Yeah it's a huge win, but it could have been something very different,' the Spaniard, who was booked in the game for leaving his technical area, said on TNT Sports. “It’s not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league” 😳 Mikel Arteta reflects on Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Sunderland 👀@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/2BUZILexk3 — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) September 12, 2026 Mikel Arteta branded the decision to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal 'unacceptable at this level' Ezri Konsa was adjudged to have fouled Dan Ballard - with the Black Cats missing the spot kick When questioned on how things could have been different, he replied: 'You know in what way, in the way that they could have changed the game. You know who.' Then, after the reporter brought up the penalty decision, Arteta let loose. 'Yes, yes,' he snapped. 'I'm so upset, it's unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This can change the course of the season, the championship. It is not acceptable. 'I've seen it 10 times to make sure because I watched it live and I said it's not possible at this level that it can be a penalty, because it is a judo roll, that's what it is, it cannot happen. 'In my view, in any view of someone who has played football. It is not a penalty in any case, in any game in any context in any league.' He added that he would speak to Brooks to make his feelings clear after the interview. The result had looked in doubt for much of the game, with the opener from Guimaraes – a former Newcastle captain – coming in the 58th minute. Sunderland had plenty of chances, too, taking five shots for 1.64 expected goals, but Arsenal's resolute defence stood firm once again. The Arsenal boss was also booked during the match for leaving his technical area 'We have unbelievable players with spirit and courage to go again and again,' Arteta continued. 'I am so pleased in one sense and so worried in another. On £75million summer signing Guimaraes he added: 'Here, you know what it means, to play with such personality and he decided the game. 'Raya is also a player who decides football matches when we need it, big credit to Sunderland for the way they play, the way they are coached, what they do. I don't want to take any credit away from them.'

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes silences Sunderland boos with brilliant strike before late Bukayo Saka penalty adds gloss to the grit of 2-0 win that should strike fear into Arsenal's title rivals, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
The talk in September of Arsenal running away with the Premier League title had seemed rather premature, to put it mildly. These matters are never straightforward, nor predictable, as the history books show. As recently as last season, for example, Liverpool had been tipped to rule supreme after a summer splurge of around £450million. A first title in 22 years transpired for the Gunners, of course. Yet, the credentials Mikel Arteta's men are already showing are a scary sight indeed for rivals, bolstering just why many observers are widely tipping them for major honours once again. Their heads could have dropped on 54 minutes when referee John Brooks pointed to the spot. Ezri Konsa, who had a tough night at the hands of many wrestling jousts with Brian Brobbey, was embroiled in another such battle – this time with Dan Ballard. Both had hold of each other's shirts in the area as the ball arrived. It made Brooks's call for a penalty seem rather soft, the pair each culpable for the holding. Enzo Le Fee stepped up to take the resulting penalty, which David Raya sprang at full stretch to tip onto the left-hand post. Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes scored a stunning goal to put Arsenal ahead against Sunderland The Black Cats could have taken the lead, but David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee's penalty It was a stunning save, using all his elasticity. Just two minutes later, substitute Bruno Guimaraes had found himself just outside the area with a sight at goal. The Sunderland player had stepped off him, fatefully. A curling strike, kissing the underside of the crossbar and into the net followed, along with his ears cupped to the booing home crowd. These few minutes encapsulated an Arsenal free of the shackles of being perennial runners-up, a belief that they really are better than the rest. They were not at their best here. Far from it. In fact, on another day, Sunderland may have walked away with something, particularly if Raya's stupendous save didn't deny Le Fee's soft penalty. But therein lies why this was an important performance: Arsenal didn't wilt. They had learned from what happened on this ground just under a year ago – a drenching, windy and heated encounter here in the North East back in November. At that point, Arsenal had won five league games in a row and looked supreme in the eyes of many. That narrative was shot to pieces after drawing 2-2 with the Black Cats, Brobbey's injury-time equaliser ending the run – and proving to the league that Arteta's team wasn't impregnable, as many had concluded. An identical blueprint had been copied and pasted by Regis Le Bris again: be physical and aggressive early, and make Arsenal work hard for opportunities from open play. The Gunners were far from their best - but showed they may well be better than the rest Brobbey pinned Konsa back, often from the halfway line, using his weight to dictate terms. Konsa often had little choice but to compromise to the striker receiving the ball and laying it off; it amounted to bullying at times. A number of Sunderland's players left strong challenges on the opposition's players, resulting in loud roars from an insatiable, proud home faithful. Martin Odegaard found himself on the floor from a Granit Xhaka push. Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz were felled by meaty challenges. Still, Arsenal used this as fuel. Sunderland were right up for this in a fortress where they had only lost four top-flight games at home in the 2025-26 season. The visitors, though, were in some form, with Odegaard having rediscovered his best form to score four in five matches and the team in general ticking along well across the pitch. Before kick-off, Havertz had covered more distance than any other Premier League striker this season (32.9km), a reflection of the hard yards Arteta's team were putting in to cut themselves adrift from the rest. Arteta opted for the same starting line-up which beat Chelsea last weekend, though Jurrien Timber made the Arsenal squad for the first time since the Champions League final in May. This was a boost, Timber a key part of Arteta's plans, his performances last season registering him as arguably the league's most complete right back. Bukayo Saka put the icing on the cake late on with an injury-time penalty to make it 2-0 The north London club were going into this match on a five-match unbeaten run across all competitions. Those assertions that Arsenal can't be chased were again surfacing. Declan Rice had got his eye in early, playing a few chipped passes into the area. Christos Tzolis received one, mis-controlling the ball, before Saka did the same while through on goal. Against the tidal wave of pressure coming their way, he ought to have done better. MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 6.5; Mukiele 6.5, Ballard 6.5, Danso 6, Mandava 5; Sadiki 6, Xhaka 6.5; Meunier 6, Le Fee 5.5, Angulo 6; Brobbey 7. Manager: Regis Le Bris 6.5 ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 8; White 5.5 (Timber 46, 6.5), Konsa 5.5, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 6; Rice 6.5, Lewis-Skelly 6 (Guimaraes 46, 8); Saka 6, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 6.5; Havertz 6. Goals: Guimaraes, Saka Booked: Arteta Manager: Mikel Arteta 6.5 Granit Xhaka's curling free-kick evaded every Arsenal shirt, reaching Ballard on 16 minutes, his header going wide. The Gunners nearly had their goal before half-time, Havertz chesting the ball down before swivelling and striking on the half volley which goalkeeper Robin Roefs saved. It was some effort. There was a sense going into the break of Arsenal's pressure slowly eroding the seams around Sunderland's resolute defence. Though the Black Cats were growing in confidence – and their chances were to arrive. Guimaraes and Timber came on at half-time, Guimaraes's name particularly met by boos. Yet it was the Brazilian's heroics which turned the match. Timber struck late on via a header which was ruled out for offside, and Raya dealt with a skirmish in the area which nearly resulted in the ball bundled in. But Arsenal held. The lessons of last season's encounter in the North East had been learned emphatically. Saka added the gloss with an injury-time penalty, awarded after Reinildo Mandava pulled the winger back. It earned Mandava a second yellow card, too.
