World.title: He was a ‘Traveller’, a ‘Bad Man’, a ‘Rude Boy’, a real ‘Land Shark’: Chinese liquor ‘durr’ busted on bicycle with schoolbag full of Revel and no liquor license
World.content:
He was a ‘Traveller’, a ‘Bad Man’, a ‘Rude Boy’, a real ‘Land Shark’: Chinese liquor ‘durr’ busted on bicycle with schoolbag full of Revel and no liquor license

By Breaking Belize News Staff: An Orange Walk businessman has been charged with keeping alcohol without a liquor licence after police allegedly found 16 small bottles of rum inside a school bag.

Police say two cops were on foot patrol on Baker Street at around 7:30 p.m. on September 9 when they saw Wu Peng Ling riding a bicycle carrying an empty Belikin crate and a brown school bag.

A search of the bag reportedly uncovered 16 small bottles of Gold Revel Rum along with a container holding money.

Police say Ling was unable to produce a liquor licence and was arrested.

According to the police report, officers had encountered Ling on two previous occasions in recent weeks — on September 2 with 22 small bottles of Revel Rum and on August 26 with another nine small bottles and money.

Ling was formally arrested and charged on September 10 with keeping alcohol without a licence. Police say he remained silent when cautioned.

World.title: Man allegedly stabbed by girlfriend at wedding reception with boxcutter over $20
World.content:
Man allegedly stabbed by girlfriend at wedding reception with boxcutter over $20

By Breaking Belize News Staff: An argument between a couple at a wedding reception near Ladyville allegedly ended with a man being cut on his hand with a box cutter.

Police received information at around 6:10 p.m. on September 10 of a stabbing at Hakim Shipyard near Mile 6.5 on the Philip Goldson Highway.

A 32-year-old man later told police that he had invited his girlfriend to the wedding, but an argument began after she became upset because he had not been answering her telephone calls.

According to the man, his girlfriend asked him to pay $20 to a relative who had transported her to the event. He initially refused but later agreed in an attempt to calm the situation.

The man alleged that as he handed over the money, his girlfriend reached into her purse, pulled out what appeared to be a black box cutter and swung it at him, cutting his right hand.

He reportedly ran into the establishment for assistance while his girlfriend left toward Ladyville.

The man was treated at the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital and requested court action. Police have listed the woman as wanted as the investigation continues.

World.title: Police investigating man who allegedly choked 10-year-old boy who hit his son with stick
World.content:
Police investigating man who allegedly choked 10-year-old boy who hit his son with stick

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating an allegation that an adult man choked a 10-year-old Belize City boy following an altercation between the child and another boy on Friday afternoon.

According to police, the 10-year-old reported that he and another boy were striking a cement verandah with separate pieces of stick when the other child struck him on the leg.

The boy said he retaliated by striking the other child below the eye.

Police say the other child’s father subsequently came outside and allegedly placed his hand around the 10-year-old’s neck and choked him.

The child visited the Precinct One Police Station with his mother and was issued a medico-legal form for his injuries.

Police have identified Abraham Baptist as a person they are seeking in connection with the investigation.

World.title: Man allegedly jumps fence and damages woman’s motorcycle
World.content:
Man allegedly jumps fence and damages woman’s motorcycle

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating after a Belize City woman reported that a man jumped into her fenced yard and caused about $200 in damage to her motorcycle.

The 31-year-old woman told police that at around 4:00 p.m. Friday she received a call from her nine-year-old daughter informing her that a man was damaging her green Lifan motorcycle.

When the woan returned home approximately 20 minutes later, she found damage to the clutch, mirrors, brake light and signal light.

According to the report, the woman had loaned the motorcycle to a friend and believes the vandalism may be connected to a previous dispute between the friend and a man she knows only as “Javier.”

She alleged that the man jumped over the fence to enter the yard before damaging the motorcycle.

The woman has requested court action and police are investigating.

World.title: Belize City woman reports $40 stolen from her room during 15-minute nap
World.content:
Belize City woman reports $40 stolen from her room during 15-minute nap

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 20-year-old Belize City woman has made a police report after $40 disappeared from her room while she briefly dozed off Friday evening.

The woman told police she was inside her room on Dean Street at around 5:00 p.m. when she left two $20 notes on a table near the door and lay down on her bed.

About 15 minutes later, she reportedly woke after hearing the door squeak and immediately noticed that the $40 was gone.

The woman questioned her landlord and neighbours but was unable to determine who had entered the room.

She told police she had not given anyone permission to enter and made the report for future reference in the event that she is able to identify the person responsible.

World.title: 25-year-old Belize City man charged for crack pipe possession
World.content:
25-year-old Belize City man charged for crack pipe possession

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 25-year-old Belize City man has been charged with possession of a utensil after police say they found a small metal pipe during a search on Orange Street.

Police say officers were conducting cycle patrol at around 5:20 p.m. on September 11 when they stopped Brian Adam Fuentes and informed him that he would be searched for drugs and firearms.

During the search, police allegedly found a silver-coloured metal pipe with a blue plastic tip concealed at the front of his pants.

The object was taken as evidence and later measured at approximately 2½ inches long.

Fuentes was taken to the Raccoon Street Police Station and was subsequently formally arrested and charged with possession of a utensil.

Police say he chose to remain silent when cautioned on the charge.

World.title: Belmopan woman says cousin broke into her home through the ceiling; Stole milk, bread, hotdogs and $25 from son’s piggy bank
World.content:
Belmopan woman says cousin broke into her home through the ceiling; Stole milk, bread, hotdogs and $25 from son’s piggy bank

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a burglary in the Salvapan area of Belmopan in which a woman says an intruder entered her home through the ceiling and stole food along with $25 from her son’s piggy bank.

A Belmopan woman told police that when she returned home at around 8:45 p.m. on September 8, she noticed that her front door, which she had secured before leaving, was slightly open.

Inside, the woman reportedly followed dirt tracks on the white tile floor toward the bathroom, where she discovered a crack in the ceiling believed to have been used to enter the residence.

Missing were a box of Lala milk valued at $4.25, bread valued at $2.75, hot dog sausages valued at $5.25 and $25 from her son’s piggy bank, for a total loss of $37.25.

Police say the woman later reviewed security footage and identified the alleged intruder as her cousin, who had visited the residence days earlier.

The woman has requested court action. Police are investigating.

World.title: Belmopan man loses $150 in Facebook folding table scam after seller deletes account
World.content:
Belmopan man loses $150 in Facebook folding table scam after seller deletes account

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belmopan man reported losing $150 after ordering three folding tables through Facebook, only for the seller’s account to disappear shortly after he transferred the money.

Police say a 49-year-old man saw a post on August 19 from an account advertising folding tables for $50 each.

The man reportedly contacted the seller through Messenger and agreed to purchase three tables. He then transferred $150 to a bank account provided by the seller and was told the tables could be collected after 6:00 p.m. that evening.

However, when the man checked Facebook at around 6:30 p.m., he reportedly discovered that the account had been deleted along with their Messenger conversation.

Tatum told police he has neither received the tables nor heard from the seller since. The matter was reported as obtaining a money transfer by deception; however, the police report states that Tatum did not request court action.

World.title: ‘Really, really sad’
World.content:
An undated picture of seven-year-old Keriecia Hutchinson and her four-year-old brother Samson Cameron, who died in a house fire in Smith Lane, Central Kingston, on Saturday.

GRIEF and anger were palpable in the Central Kingston community of Smith Lane on Saturday as it was confirmed that seven-year-old Keriecia Hutchinson and her four-year-old brother Samson Cameron had perished in a mid-morning house fire.

Residents remembered the two children who they said were promising and full of life while anger surged as people assigned blame for their deaths.

Keriecia was a grade one student at Calabar All-Age School, while Samson was a student of Calabar Basic School.

“The mother locked them up in the house and gone to a wholesale. She could have just left them out and asked any of wi to look on them,” charged one neighbour who, like her colleagues, refused to give their names.

“The mother do nothing wrong, the [son’s] father was here and him run go up there [to the room] before the fire get wicked and him run down back and say him can’t reach the children,” charged another neighbour.

Police on the scene refused to speak with the media to confirm or deny either claim, but the contention morphed into a physical battle between one woman — who was defending the children’s grandmother — and another female resident who was chastising the parents.

Police on the scene fired a number of shots in the air to separate the combatants and at least three people were later taken into custody.

But for most residents in Smith Lane the death of the two children was their main concern.

“Right yah now me feel really, really sad that the two kids lose them lives,” said one of the few residents willing to speak to the media on condition that she not be named.

“What I get to understand, the mother wasn’t here, she gone to the wholesale, but why did she lock the children inside? And when people call out and the father run inside, the door lock, and is like him forget the key so him panic. So when the door finally open and people a throw water — even me a throw out water — it did not save the children. It really, really sad,” said the woman.

She told the Jamaica Observer that Keriecia moved to live with her mother in Smith Lane when she was about two years old, while the son, “him a must be about four or five years old now, and him born right here so inna mi hand”, added the neighbour.

She said many residents tried to put the blaze out before the Jamaica Fire Brigade team arrived but they were unsuccessful.

Residents also had praise for a neighbour who they said soaked himself in water before entering the burning house after being told that the children were inside, but he was unable to rescue them.

“He is a hero, man. Him really try, but the children were not in the front room, they were in the back, and the little girl died hugging her brother trying to save him. You could see she was trying to help him,” said one man, who, like others, refused to give his name.

At press time Saturday the fire brigade had not determined the cause of the blaze, while there was no word on whether the people involved in the physical altercation had been charged.

An unofficial count by the Sunday Observer has shown four children have died in fires across the island since the start of this year.

World.title: Shabba Ranks files lawsuit against publishing arm of Greensleeves Records
World.content:
Shabba Ranks

Iconic dancehall trailblazer and deejay, Shabba Ranks, has filed a lawsuit against the publishing arm of Greensleeves Records, in a move to reclaim the rights to several of his crossover hits as well as the 1990 song Dem Bow.

According to a report in Billboard magazine, Shabba Ranks (born Rexton Gordon) filed the suit on Friday (Sept. 11), and it aims to reclaim compositions including the Billboard Hot 100 hits Slow and Sexy, Housecall, Mr Loverman and Let’s Get It On.

Shabba Ranks’ catalogue also includes the 1990 song Dem Bow, the namesake for reggaetón’s iconic dembow rhythm that is currently at the centre of a long-running copyright infringement lawsuit entangling the entire genre.

Friday’s lawsuit, meanwhile, centres on copyright termination — the provision of United States (US) copyright law that enables authors to claw back their intellectual property decades after signing it away.

Shabba Ranks first notified Greensleeves in 2023 that he wanted to exercise his termination right, but the publisher said no. According to Greensleeves, his 1989 publishing deal stipulated that his compositions were “works made for hire,” which are explicitly excluded from the copyright termination statute.

Shabba, however, is contesting the validity of that work-for-hire provision, and he wants a judge to declare that his copyright termination is effective regardless.

“The compositions are not and could not have been works made for hire under the US Copyright Act, regardless of the language of the assignment,” wrote Shabba Ranks’ attorneys at Reitler Kailas & Rosenblatt.

“Gordon was never at any time an employee of [Greensleeves], and musical compositions are not recognised in the US Copyright Act as a type of work that can be deemed a work made for hire simply by agreement between the hiring party and a non-employee author.”

Copyright termination is a hot topic in music law in the United States at present.

Pioneering rap outfit Salt-N-Pepa is battling Universal Music Group (UMG) over the provision in a case that has caught the industry’s attention.

Meanwhile, all three major labels are currently trying to get the Supreme Court to reverse a controversial recent ruling that extended the termination right overseas.

Shabba Ranks, raised in Seaview Gardens, rode high in the late 1980s into the mid-1990s with a steady streak of hit songs. He signed with Epic Records and scored back-to-back wins at the Grammy Awards when As Raw As Ever and X-tra Naked won the Best Reggae Album awards in 1992 and 1993, respectively.

Both albums have been certified gold by the Recording Industry Association of America.

World.title: Seville beaten in Ultimate 100m final
World.content:
US' Kenneth Bednarek (2R) wins ahead of US' Ronnie Baker (L), Botswana's Letsile Tebogo (2L) and Jamaica's Oblique Seville in the men's 100m final during the World Athletics Ultimate Championship at the Gyula Zsivotzky National Athletics Centre, in Budapest on September 12, 2026. (Photo by Jewel SAMAD / AFP)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Oblique Seville just failed to add the World Athletics Ultimate Championships title to his World Championships and Diamond League titles after placing second in the men’s 100m final on Saturday’s second day at the National Athletics Center in Budapest, Hungary.

American Kenny Bednarek spoiled the party after he ran a season’s best 9.85 seconds (-0.6m/s) to beat the Jamaican who repeated the 9.90 seconds he ran to lead the semi-finals.

Another American Ronnie Baker was third in 9.93 seconds.

Jonielle Smith was fourth in the women’s 100m with 10.94 seconds (-0.2m/s), the same time awarded to her compatriot Tina Clayton while Lavanya Williams was seventh in 11.07 seconds.

American Melissa Jefferson-Wooden ran a world-leading 10.62 seconds to win the trophy, just beating Julien Alfred of St Lucia- 10.74 seconds with Sha’Carrie Richardson of the USA third in 10.76 seconds.

National record holder Nickisha Pryce was third in the women’s 400m final, running 49.56 seconds as favourite Marileidy Paulino of the Dominican Republic won with 49.07 seconds, coming from fourth place over the last 120 metres to take the trophy.

Norway’s Henriette Jaeger was second in 49.28m.

In the other final that included a Jamaican, Diamond League winner Tajay Gayle was fifth in the men’s long jump with a best of 7.90m (-0.1m/s), getting only three jumps as only the top four advanced to the fourth and final round.

Gayle improved with each jump, starting with 7.52m (1.0n/s); he then had a 7.72m (-0.2m/s) jump in the second round.

Meanwhile, Commonwealth Games champion Sanique Walker who ran a big personal best of 53.77 seconds and Rushell Clayton, advanced to Sunday’s final of the women’s 400m hurdles.

Walker lowered her personal best from 54.00 seconds that she set while winning at the Commonwealth Games to place third in her semi-final, running from lane nine, behind Americans Jasmine Jones who ran a season’s best 52.77 seconds and Anna Cockrell, 53.31 seconds.

Clayton was fourth in her semi-final with 53.84 seconds after she came off the seventh hurdle in seventh place.

Emma Zapletalova of Slovakia won with 52.93 seconds, followed by Panama’s Gianna Woodruff- 53.73 seconds and Belgium’s national record holder Paulien Couckuyt- 53.81 seconds.

Commonwealth Games gold medalist Navasky Anderson just missed advancing to the men’s 800m final, finishing fifth in the first semi-final in 1:44.83, just behind Kenya’s Emmanuel Wanyoni who got fourth place in 1:44.43 and a place in the final.

-Paul A Reid

World.title: Build better, faster
World.content:
Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness (right) engages in a lively discussion with Donald Mullings (left), chairman, M&M Jamaica Limited; Martin Miller (second left), managing director, National Housing Trust (NHT); and NHT Chairman Linval Freeman during Friday’s ground breaking for the construction of 700 houses at Greater Bernard Lodge in St Catherine. The houses are being built will under a partnership agreement with the NHT, the Housing Agency of Jamaica, and M&M Jamaica Ltd. Photo: Garfield Robinson

BREAKING ground Friday for the construction of 700 new homes at Greater Bernard Lodge in St Catherine, Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness challenged local contractors to embrace technology and invest in equipment that can accelerate the pace of delivery.

“The building technologies that we are using today are outdated and expensive. We need more of our private contractors and our private developers to start using modern technology. It’s not just to build the houses more cost-effectively, but we have to move away from building the matches boxes, the heat boxes, to building things that look modern, aesthetically pleasing and sustainable. That is my challenge today to our developers,” Holness said, adding that he expects that within the next 18 months he will be back at the location to present keys to the owners of the new units.

“The role of Government is to use legislation, and fiscal incentives, and moral suasion to guide and sometimes direct the private developers into the underserved areas of the market. But we are seeing an influx of overseas private contractors who have solved the problem of being able to build quickly and deliver quickly at a reasonable price because they have integrated significant technology and equipment into their operations,” Holness said.

“Almost every day we are getting proposals. The only thing they want from us would be land. But I am thinking that I want my local contractors to do this. I want my local contractors to develop the capability to deliver these houses quickly. I can’t just give away everything to overseas and foreign investors. I want my local contractors to benefit, but at the same time I want the people to get houses,” the prime minister said.

The units — 280 one-bedroom and 420 two-bedroom houses — will be built under a partnership agreement with the National Housing Trust (NHT), the Housing Agency of Jamaica (HAJ), and M&M Jamaica Limited, across two parcels of land.

They will form the D2 and D3 phases of the Greater Bernard Lodge housing development programme and will include paved roads, storm water drains, perimeter walls, street signs, and other essential amenities.

The $11.62-billion project will expand the supply of housing available to NHT contributors.

Arguing that the practise of squatting will persist if enough isn’t done to provide shelter for the many Jamaicans who have no home for themselves, Holness reiterated that his Administration remains committed to its election promise of building 70,000 houses.

“So, the 70,000 is very ambitious. I’m hanging my hat where I will have to stretch to reach it,” he said.

“We have been stretching. The NHT was tasked to build 42,000 of that, and my last check showed that they have seen their way in terms of what they have already constructed — what is in contracts, what is in procurement, and what is in planning. They are over 40,000, so they have seen the slate of what they should construct. The chairman told you that since the start of the year we have broken ground for 2,000. We are now at over 8,000 houses under construction or out of construction,” the prime minister said.

Lynvale Freeman, the NHT chairman, said that Friday’s ground-breaking represented not just the turning of soil but the expansion of homeownership in Jamaica. He said it was important to do it in St Catherine because of its close proximity to Kingston, among other important factors.

“The common goal is to build as many houses at the lowest price point,” Freeman said.

World.title: ‘EDUCATION EMERGENCY’
World.content:
La Sonja Harrison, president of the Jamaica Teachers’ Association, speaking at a meeting of the Rotary Club of Kingston at Jamaica Pegasus hotel on Thursday. Garfield Robinson

DECLARING that Jamaica is facing an “education emergency”, president of the Jamaica Teachers’ Association (JTA) La Sonja Harrison is urging the Government to implement a five-year national learning recovery and acceleration plan to tackle the existing gaps in the sector.

But Harrison is adamant that the five-year initiative must put educators at the forefront of the conversation.

“If it is as educators, we are the first responders, we are the people on the ground, I am saying that there can be no conversation about how we go nationally without the teachers in a meaningful way. And I’m not talking about us, leaders of the Jamaica Teachers’ Association, I’m talking about the people who are on the ground, the foot soldiers, and the people on whom you will depend [on] anyway to carry out whatever vision you have for education.

“Those persons need to be invited at the table from the beginning of the conversation, not at the tail end,” Harrison told the Jamaica Observer on Thursday following a meeting of the Rotary club of Kingston at the Jamaica Pegasus hotel.

“We have TREND [Transforming Education for National Development], and we have ETOC [Education Transformation Oversight Committee], because they continue to update the nation quarterly concerning same. So ETOC will have some educators represented there, but is it reflective of the system, the people who work in the trenches of the system, and are they at the table for the conversation and posit the solutions that they would see ideal and realistic, in transforming the education system?”Harrison questioned.

In her presentation Harrison highlighted several disruptions faced by the education sector and argued that the urgency displayed by the Government in rebuilding structures and restoring operations has not been given to recovering learning.

“COVID-19 interrupted the education system of an entire generation. Then came Hurricane Beryl [July 2024], Hurricane Melissa [October 2025]. In between, there have been floods…fires, infrastructural failures, and teacher shortages, and that is just since 2019, we have not even gone back decades,”

“We have spent considerable time recovering buildings, and those recovery of buildings have certainly not been to the standard that we are desirous of, and the pace, the alacrity. Because for us to be able to report as a nation that 40 of some 600 plus schools have been rebuilt, that’s 6.67 per cent of our schools that have been retrofitted to provide an atmosphere for safe, comfortable learning of our children,” Harrison frowned.

Pointing to the Government’s emergencies in education plan, including the modification of objectives from the National Standards Curriculum, (NSC) post-Hurricane Melissa, Harrison charged that establishing such a plan after a disaster is ineffective.

“We need to identify those who have fallen behind. We need targeted initiatives. We need additional instructional support where necessary. We need stronger literacy and numeracy initiative benchmarks to support. We need trained teachers and interventionists at varying levels of the system. And we need to measure whether children are actually catching up. Attendance is not recovery. Promotion is not recovery. Completing a grade is not recovery. Learning is recovery. Teachers cannot be expected to recover six years of educational disruption with the same resources, same staffing, and in some cases under staffing, and after these weather challenges and with worsening infrastructure,” said Harrison.

“The Government is going to tell you that we have the emergency in education stuff, but it has to be proactive in nature. It can’t be that it is when the event happens, then we come up with something that will help to take us through another event. So we have to sit down and look and say how are we going to, one, ensure learning, how are we going to engage teachers, how are we going to engage parents.

“Jamaica needs a national foundational learning emergency plan. I deliberately use that language. Not another programme project to treat with the illiteracy problem. Not another intervention to treat with learning gap, as this is just not another education challenge. It is an emergency. Because when children are progressing through our schools without mastering reading, comprehension, writing, and numeracy, we’re not simply dealing with an academic problem. We’re compromising Jamaica’s future,” Harrison charged.

World.title: Garbage truck obstacle
World.content:
Falmouth Mayor C Junior Gager addressing Thursday’s regular monthly meeting of the Trelawny Municipal Corporation.

FALMOUTH, Trelawny — A derelict garbage truck is standing in the way of plans by the Trelawny Municipal Corporation (TMC) to establish temporary headquarters, prompting Falmouth Mayor C Junior Gager to give the vehicle’s owner an ultimatum to remove it or face having it towed.

Gager, who is also chairman of the TMC, told Thursday’s regular monthly meeting of the corporation that the truck is occupying the spot earmarked for two newly acquired containers, which are to be converted into offices and a meeting room.

He said repeated attempts to locate the owner have failed, despite the corporation obtaining contact information for a person believed to be associated with the vehicle.

“We have a garbage truck that is parked on the premises of the Trelawny Municipal Corporation for some time now. We have tried all that we can. It seems to be maybe a private contractor. We have tried to reach him. We cannot reach him,” Gager said.

With the project considered urgent, Gager said the TMC would not allow the abandoned vehicle to delay the work.

“If the truck isn’t removed within maybe another day or two, we’ll be taking it out and we’ll be placing it in an open land,” he warned.

The ultimatum comes as the TMC continues to operate from makeshift facilities following severe damage inflicted by Hurricane Melissa to its previous location at the historic Falmouth Courthouse last October.

The local authority is currently operating from containerised units on the grounds of its Roads and Works premises, while other functions have been squeezed into the Roads and Works building. Its monthly meetings are being held at the Port Authority of Jamaica’s conference room at the Falmouth Port.

Gager said the two recently purchased containers are to be retrofitted to provide badly needed office and meeting space, with the work expected to be completed within about a month.

“I would be happy if next month we can move in and have our council meeting there, because you see this room is getting so small, and we want a little more space,” Gager said.

He disclosed that a portion of the funding needed is already available and that technical officers, including the acting chief engineering officer, are being mobilised to expedite the work.

“We have some funding, and we are working with it. But we are going to make sure that next month, when you come back here it is nearly finished, or it is finished, or maybe in another two weeks,” Gager told his fellow councillors.

He described the facility as a temporary but potentially long-term investment, saying it could be used for other purposes even after the corporation establishes permanent headquarters.

The mayor also disclosed plans for an official opening of the facility once the work is completed, with Local Government Minister Desmond McKenzie expected to be among those invited.

World.title: Sher Luxury Doll takes a ‘Victory Lap’ into music production
World.content:
SHER... I want to leave a legacy, so when my family looks back at my journey dem si seh I was a trying person.

NOBODY saw Sher Luxury Doll’s latest move coming. But, according to the dancer-turned-entrepreneur and now music producer, that was precisely the point.

After building a name in dancehall as a dancer and choreographer before expanding her reach through the locally popular Luxury Beauty brand, Sher has stepped confidently into another arena with Victory Lap, her debut project as a producer.

For Sher, the unexpected transition is less about abandoning one identity for another and more about refusing to limit what she can become.

“Nobody saw this coming, but that’s me. I like surprising people,” she said. “From hairdresser, to dancer, to entrepreneur, to producer — I always want to grow and challenge myself. Trying new things keeps my brain active, and from me small I don’t like to do one thing.”

That desire to continually evolve has become one of the defining threads of her journey. While each career move has seemingly carried her into unfamiliar territory, Sher said she is motivated by the legacy she hopes to leave behind.

“I want to leave a legacy, so when my family looks back at my journey dem si seh I was a trying person,” she shared. “I like to master things and prove to myself that I can and push myself beyond the measures and limits people put on me.”

Interestingly, her venture into production began with a casual conversation and an idea she initially expressed in jest. While speaking with a close associate about the need for more female-centred songs in dancehall, Sher jokingly declared that she would take matters into her own hands. Her colleague, however, immediately took her seriously.

“I was on the phone with someone I work with closely, and we were just having a regular conversation saying we miss the girl songs in dancehall and we need more,” she recalled. “I was saying I was going to make it happen, but I was saying it as a joke. Instantly, him seh him have some riddims and him ago send me dem.”

Once she received the riddims the joke quickly became a mission. Sher began contacting artistes, coordinating recordings and quietly laying the groundwork for what would eventually become Victory Lap.

“When him send me dem, me link the artistes dem, and dem did very open to the idea. When me get half of the songs on the current playlist him see seh a serious thing,” she said, noting that work on the project began around February or March. “I was doing a lot of work behind the scenes.”

Victory Lap currently features eight tracks, with contributions from AI Milly, Jahvillani, Chronic Law, Felony 19, Rytikal, Ding Dong, Renee 6:30 and Deno Crazy. Sher said several other artistes have also expressed an interest in joining the project. Despite being a newcomer to production, she encountered little resistance when approaching established entertainers. She believes the reputation she has built for taking her work seriously helped the artistes trust her vision.

World.title: Melissa puts PE on pause in some western Jamaica schools
World.content:
Carisbrook Primary and Infant School Principal Patrick Malcolm leads the Jamaica Observer on a tour of the compound on Monday. Naphtali Junior

As temporary classrooms take over playing areas of some schools in St Elizabeth, principal of Carisbrook Primary and Infant School Patrick Malcolm is warning that physical education (PE) is becoming an unfortunate casualty of the push to get damaged schools functioning again.

According to Malcolm, this reflects a wider tendency to treat PE and sport as less important than academic subjects, despite their role in developing healthy, well-rounded children.

The concern is particularly acute at Maggotty High School, where temporary classrooms have left the school without enough space to conduct practical PE sessions, and properly facilitate its netball and football programmes.

Maggotty High’s Principal Sean Graham said the school has been forced to make a significant adjustment, with practical PE sessions put on hold for the current term while administrators work around the loss of playing space.

“The PE teacher expressed concern in terms of how she will facilitate training… because the school does not have a big enough play field. We also facilitate some level of football training here as well, especially for the junior team. So, those are going to be compromised, and we are going to have to find other ways to work it out,” Graham told the

Jamaica Observer on Monday.

He said the school understands the urgency of getting students back into suitable classrooms, but stressed that the temporary arrangement cannot be allowed to become prolonged.

“But we have to figure it out. Because the most important thing is to have the students here. All PE sessions for this term have to be theory-based. So, that is why I really still have to insist that by December, temporary classrooms have to be gone, because we don’t have the space to facilitate physical education, practical, plus the netball training and so on,” added Graham.

The situation is not confined to the high-school level.

At Middle Quarters Primary and Infant School, temporary classrooms are also being constructed on the school’s netball court, forcing administrators to look elsewhere for space for physical activity.

Principal Pauvine Watson-Barrett, who also spoke with the Observer on Monday, said the school intends to use its grassy areas rather than abandon PE altogether, although the loss of the hard surface presents its own challenges.

But Malcolm is adamant that the issue goes beyond finding alternative spaces.

He believes the temporary loss of playing areas exposes a long-standing failure to give physical education the same consideration afforded to subjects such as mathematics and English.

Malcolm, who is also president of the St Elizabeth Football Association, pointed to Carisbrook’s own experience as evidence of the determination required to keep sport alive despite inadequate facilities.

The school has 137 students, including 30 infants, and has built a strong sporting programme despite limited resources.

Malcolm said the school has trophies, medals and plaques reflecting its achievements, while its football field — which he said is the only one in the area capable of accommodating a 200-metre track — is also shared with the wider community.

He charged that the school’s sporting success has often come despite, rather than because of, the resources available to it.

“This is the myopicness of the people around. We all want to be bright, maths and English people, but we don’t want to be fit and strong. So we’re going to be doctors, but sick doctors. We’re going to be teachers, but sick teachers. Sports is such that the impact of it can be felt everywhere in this country,” he said.

Malcolm questioned the decision to place temporary classrooms on playing areas when alternative spaces may be available, particularly at Middle Quarters.

“When you put a temporary classroom on the court, what are you suggesting to those who are interested in PE? That they’ll sit down and do nothing for the next two months, three months?…and it’s just sad because there is more space that they could use,” he said.

He argued that the recovery effort should not treat sport as an optional extra, particularly at a time when children are already coping with disruption caused by Hurricane Melissa and the rebuilding of their schools.

“Somebody has to get up and start to show a little bit more appreciation for sports and physical education in this country. We cannot do without it. It is the stress buster. It is where we go for a break, and if the students are not encouraged to do this, then we are in trouble,” Malcolm added.

He also linked the decline in physical activity to broader concerns about the health of Jamaican society, arguing that schools have a critical role to play in encouraging children to remain active.

“Later on, we’re going to have a sick society… Look at the size of some of the teachers we have around. Look at the size of the society. I mean, probably two-thirds of the society is overweight. We better fix that, and the only way we can fix that is with physical education,” argued Malcolm.

World.title: How to watch Sweden’s election like a pro
World.content:
That means there are only two realistic candidates to be prime minister: the incumbent, conservative Moderate party leader Ulf Kristersson; and Magdalena Andersson, the former PM who leads Sweden’s biggest party, the center-left Social Democrats.

Swedish Prime Minister and Moderate Party leader Ulf Kristersson speaks to the media upon arrival to a televised election debate hosted by TV4 in Stockholm, Sweden, on September 10, 2026, three days ahead of the country’s general election. | Jonathan Nackstrand/ AFP via Getty Images

Kristersson has run the right-wing coalition for the past four years thanks to influential support from the second biggest party, the far-right Sweden Democrats. They backed him in votes in parliament and drove policy in a hardline direction, including crackdowns on crime and especially immigration. But the Sweden Democrats did not join the coalition cabinet. That could now change.

Can the far right enter the government?

Kristersson divided opinion in 2022 when he broke a decades-long taboo against working with the far right and did his deal with the Sweden Democrats, who had won 20% of the vote. The SD was founded in the 1980s and some members in those days had roots in neo-Nazi movements. The party has taken steps to clean up its act in recent years, though not to everyone’s satisfaction.

Now Kristersson says he will give the SD ministerial seats in government if his side wins on Sunday, as part of an agreement with the far-right leader, Jimmie Åkesson. That would be another huge step for Sweden and one that the opposition has seized on.

“Of course this would be a different country with a government with half of the ministers from the Sweden Democrats,” opposition leader Andersson told AP recently. “It would not be good for Sweden if they would get the keys to the ministry of defense or the ministry of foreign affairs.”

Kristersson insists he would still be in charge overall. He points to his work with Åkesson over the past four years which he says has revived the economy and cut rates of violent crime and immigration, both of which had been major public concerns. “I can guarantee you that it will only be very skilled and experienced and people with good judgment that would be part of my government,” he told POLITICO.

World.title: Will Lagarde bite the apple? ECB President leaves everyone guessing in Normandy
World.content:
On stage, she even encouraged reporters who made the trip to Normandy to cover her potential political comeback to pack up early, promising that they would be disappointed.

But there are signs suggesting that the ECB chief, who entered into politics during the presidency of France's apple-loving Jacques Chirac, is increasingly willing to weigh in on the campaign.

While she promised to stay at least until the end of the year, Lagarde previously refused to rule out leaving before the end of her term, which ends in October 2027.

Earlier this week, she announced that she would publish her first autobiography, Lady First, in January. She also waded into the French presidential debate by rejecting French far-left presidential contender Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s proposal to wipe out government debt.

Her presence at the apple festival in the 15th-century Manoir de la Fortière — an unconventional locale for a central banker's speech — might be yet another signal. Opening the event, Morin said that he tried to invite her for years but never managed to make it work. Until this year.

Christine Lagarde at the Fête de la Pomme, France, on September 12, 202. | Giorgio Leali/POLITICO

“Everyone is happy to have you here and I realized to what extent you have an exceptional reputation,” said Morin, who worked with Lagarde when they both served as ministers under conservative president Nicolas Sarkozy, including during the 2008 financial crisis.

World.title: EU-Parlament öffnet sich für härtere China-Politik
World.content:
Brüssel und Peking führen derzeit Verhandlungen darüber, wie das Handelsdefizit der EU gegenüber China in Höhe von 1 Milliarde Euro pro Tag ausgeglichen werden kann. Ein Anstieg der chinesischen Exporte hat die einheimischen Hersteller unter Druck gesetzt und Schrecken geschürt, dass der Kontinent angesichts vielbeachteter Werksschließungen in der Automobil- und Chemieindustrie eine Deindustrialisierung durchläuft.

EU-Handelskommissar Maroš Šefčovič wird im Oktober im Rahmen der Gespräche nach Peking reisen. Er erklärte, die Union sei bereit zu handeln, falls bis zu diesem Zeitpunkt keine Fortschritte erzielt würden.

Die Kommission erwägt Maßnahmen, um Chinas industrieller Dominanz entgegenzuwirken, darunter neue Vorschriften, die Unternehmen dazu anregen sollen, ihre kritischen Lieferketten zu diversifizieren, sowie Schutzmaßnahmen, die die Einfuhr wichtiger Güter wie Hybrid-Elektrofahrzeuge begrenzen würden.

In einer gemeinsamen Erklärung vom Donnerstag sprach sich der Ausschuss für auswärtige Angelegenheiten des Europäischen Parlaments für eine Eindämmung der chinesischen Exporte und der übermäßigen Abhängigkeit Europas von Rohstoffen bis hin zu Halbleitern aus und forderte die EU auf, Maßnahmen zu ergreifen, um die „Instrumentalisierung der wirtschaftlichen Abhängigkeit der EU“ einzudämmen.

„Business as usual“ gibt es nicht mehr

Canfin erklärte, unter den EU-Abgeordneten setze sich zunehmend die Erkenntnis durch, dass „Business as usual“ in den Beziehungen der Union zu Peking keine Option mehr sei. Als Beleg für den Wandel in der Haltung gegenüber China verwies er auf die wachsende Unterstützung im Parlament für eine offensivere Industriepolitik.

Die Abgeordneten arbeiten derzeit an ihrer Position zum vorgeschlagenen „Industrial Accelerator Act“, mit dem im Rahmen der umweltorientierten öffentlichen Beschaffung eine europäische Präferenz in strategischen Industriezweigen verankert werden soll. Die federführenden Abgeordneten dieses wegweisenden Gesetzentwurfs streben einen eng verbundenen „Made in Europe“-Club sowie eine strengere Prüfung ausländischer Direktinvestitionen an.

World.title: Trump says he would ‘love’ to see a united Ireland
World.content:
Donald Trump and Taoiseach Micheál Martin listen to a question from the media at Farmleigh House in Phoenix Park in the Irish capital Dublin on September 12, 2026. | Brendan Smialowski/AFP via Getty Images

“It’s going to happen eventually,” the U.S. president said in Dublin during a golf-focused trip to the long-divided island.

DUBLIN — U.S. President Donald Trump waded into another age-old conflict Saturday, declaring on a golf-focused visit to Ireland that he’d like to see the island unified — the nightmare scenario for Northern Ireland’s British unionists.

Sitting beside Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin after an overnight flight from Washington, Trump said he couldn’t understand why Northern Ireland — the part of the island that remained in the U.K. when the rest of Ireland won independence over a century ago — hadn’t already joined the Republic of Ireland.

“I’d love to see it unified. I think it’d be great. A great feather in everybody’s cap if that happened. It’s going to happen eventually,” Trump said, gesturing to Martin, who has spent years trying behind the scenes to build better relations with unionists, to little avail. “You’ve got the right man over here to get it moving. But I think it would be a fantastic thing. Now the U.K. will have something to say about it obviously. But I think it’d be a great thing. How can it be bad?”

World.title: Farage’s Reform UK gets two £36M donations from crypto billionaires
World.content:
Delo argued in an opinion piece for The Telegraph that Reform needed the injection to make the election “a fair fight.” Delo, who was already one of Reform’s largest donors, said he wanted to give Reform “a level playing field” at the next general election.

The paper on Saturday also published an opinion piece from Harborne, where he called his donation “a philantropic gift to our country.”

Farage thanked the two men for their contributions. “Both men know that we are the only party that can turn the country around,” he said in a statement.

Reform UK was leading the polls since April 2025 , according to POLITICO’s Poll of Polls. But the party has now slumped slightly behind Labour, with new Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the helm and after a bizarre by-election where Farage defeated satirical candidate Count Binface.

The right-wing force is currently rushing to get battle-ready amid speculation Burnham could trigger an early general election, though one is not due until 2029. Reform UK is on the hunt for potential candidates to run as MP, and has only about 100 star candidates considered ready to run at the moment.

World.title: Portugal wants EU cash to pay for firefighting goats
World.content:
José Manuel Fernandes Minister of Agriculture and Fisheries of Portugal at the European Council in Brussels in Belgium on 9 December 2024. | Martin Bertrand/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images

As budget negotiations intensify, capitals are reaching for a new argument to keep money in the farming pot: climate change.

Portugal’s minister for agriculture has a burning desire for the next EU long-term budget: more goats.

José Manuel Fernandes wants Brussels to help pay shepherds to let goats, cows and sheep graze on shrubs in areas at high risk of wildfires — a low-tech approach that experts say the EU has been ignoring for too long. Portugal and some regions in Spain are already running their own programs.

“We are using our national money, but it is work that we are doing for all the European Union,” Fernandes told POLITICO at an informal meeting of ministers in Dublin, arguing that preventing fires helps lower carbon emissions.

World.title: EU delays key tobacco tax vote until after Swedish election
World.content:
The European Commission proposed increasing levies on cigarettes and setting minimum rates on newer products like vapes, heat-not-burn tobacco and nicotine pouches in July last year.

The plan has become a flashpoint for Sweden, which has a long tradition of using snus — a pouch of tobacco that sits between the gums. As such, Stockholm has strongly opposed raising taxes on similar nicotine pouches.

Delaying the vote gives extra time for Sweden to appoint a new finance minister and for the capitals to negotiate a way out of the current stalemate.

The Irish presidency of the Council of the EU, which is steering the talks, confirmed the vote has been pushed from October to November's ministerial meeting.

Four diplomats granted anonymity to speak candidly about the sensitive negotiations said the postponement is meant to give Sweden's next government extra time to change its mind.

A spokesperson for the Irish presidency said they will "continue[s] to engage bilaterally with the aim of securing unanimous political agreement at the November ECOFIN" meeting of finance ministers.

World.title: Escaping the AI safety nightmare: What can governments do?
World.content:
A case in point is that OpenAI agents hacked a German website back in May to use it as a messaging board, Reuters reported last week. OpenAI had not publicly announced the incident and responded to the Reuters reporting on X saying: “We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment.”

“[Reporting] timelines are going to need to be dramatically shortened [for incidents], and so we need much better continuous monitoring capabilities,” said Imogen Stead, AI policy manager at London-based think tank the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, adding that the data will be needed in real time “and that will be true for governments and for labs.”

Speaking at a London event for U.K. lawmakers arranged by campaign group ControlAI on Monday, computer scientist Stuart Russell said that the most concerning aspect of the Hugging Face incident for him was that “by running a thousand agents communicating with each other, they were able to generate behaviors that no one agent could do by itself,” referring to investigations showing the incident was far more severe than OpenAI first acknowledged.

“But [in] the evaluations, standard testing is done with a single AI system, not with a thousand,” he told lawmakers, so now the industry must anticipate the possibility of many agents all collaborating at once.

Out of alignment

Beyond avoiding any obvious mistakes in testing, there are issues in the culture of AI testing that are more deeply embedded.

The concept of the alignment of AI models or agents — i.e. making sure AI systems do what they're told by human users and don’t go off-piste — has been one of the cornerstones for AI safety in the industry’s eyes.

World.title: From tiny houses to skis: This Swedish company is finding creative uses for retired wind turbines
World.content:
Europe is on track for a record wind year, with 8.8 GW of new capacity installed in the first half of 2026 – a 30 per cent jump year on year.

 

That’s enough electricity to power around seven million European households and replace fossil fuel imports equivalent to 25 LNG tankers a year, according to industry nonprofit WindEurope.

But every turbine that goes up eventually means one coming down – and manufacturers are still working out how to make sure none of the materials go to waste.

Up to 90 per cent of a wind turbine’s mass is made of easily recyclable materials like steel, copper, aluminium and concrete. Composite materials, which make up the majority of blades, are more problematic.

“Separating the composite materials from the resin requires specialised processes, often involving high temperatures or other energy-intensive treatment methods,” Eva Julius-Philipp, Director of Environment and Sustainability of Business Area Wind at Vattenfall, tells Euronews Earth. “In some cases, these processes can affect the quality and value of the recovered materials, making large-scale recycling more challenging.”

Since introducing a landfill ban on blades, nacelle covers and nose cones in 2021, the Swedish company has come up with some creative alternatives.

Inside the tiny house converted from a wind turbine nacelle by Vattenfall and design studio Superuse. Vattenfall

From blades to buildings: Turbine components get a second wind

From the ground, it’s hard to appreciate just how large wind turbines are. Putting it into perspective, Vattenfall teamed up with design studio Superuse to turn a retired wind turbine nacelle cover – which houses the mechanical and electrical equipment – into a compact living space.

Four metres wide, 10 metres long and three metres high, the box once sat atop an Austrian wind tower. It’s now a tiny house fitted with a kitchen, bathroom and living space equipped with a heat pump, solar panels and a solar water heater.

It was showcased at Dutch Design Week in 2024 as part of an initiative exploring how materials could be reused with as little energy and emissions-intensive processing as possible.

Blades, too, have been re-envisioned as building materials. After being decommissioned in 2023, the 57 blades from Danish onshore wind farm Nørre Økse Sø found new life as a facade for a multistorey carpark in the city of Lund.

It’s opened the door to a multitude of inventive uses for retired blades, from frames for solar panels to alpine skis.

“Projects such as the Tiny House, blade-based building projects and recycled skis are not yet a large-scale solution, however they are intended to help us gain experience, develop new applications and stimulate the market for circular solutions,” says Julius-Philipp.

Provided it’s safe to do so, extending the operational lifetime of existing components through reuse and refurbishment is the preferred option, she adds.

The Niels Bohr car park in Lund is partly constructed from rotor blades from decommissioned wind turbines. Vattenfall

Recycling wind turbine blades: A multilayered challenge

Wind turbine blades can be between 50 and 100 metres long and are designed to spin in harsh weather for up to 25 years. What makes them so durable is also what makes them difficult to recycle: materials such as glass fibre, carbon fibre, epoxy resin, balsa wood, metals and various fillers pressed tightly together in layers.

Aiming to achieve 100 per cent circularity for these composite materials by 2030, Vattenfall is working on new ways of reusing, repurposing, refurbishing and recycling blades.

“When composite materials cannot be recycled at a high value, they can be processed through energy recovery and/or cement co-processing,” says Julius-Philipp.

Currently, Vattenfall uses mechanical recycling processes to turn blade material into composite flakes or fillers for new products, while pyrolysis – a thermal recycling process – recovers fibres and other secondary materials.

But technology isn’t the only challenge: “Decommissioned blades do not become available in a steady and predictable flow, which makes it harder for recycling solutions to scale economically,” adds Julius-Philipp.

As the first generation of major European wind farms reaches the end of its operational lifespan in the coming years, more blades will enter retirement, increasing the need for solutions that are “scalable, cost-efficient and low in energy use,” she adds.

The EU has not yet enforced a ban on landfilling decommissioned blades. Only Austria, Finland, Germany and the Netherlands have their own binding national bans, and WindEurope is now pushing Brussels to make the commitment legally binding across all member states.

“What is needed now is a regulatory framework that enables circular value chains and secondary raw materials to scale,” says Julius-Philipp, who hopes the European Commission’s Circular Economy Act, expected to be proposed later this year, will help provide it.

EVI Ski and Norwegian recycling company Gjenkraft collaborated with Vattenfall to use glass and carbon fibres from decommissioned wind turbine blades to manufacture skis. Vattenfall

Designed to recycle: The future of turbine blades?

Increasingly, manufacturers are taking end-of-life into consideration when designing turbine blades.

Siemens Gamesa’s RecyclableBlades, which are used at Vattenfall’s offshore windfarm Hollandse Kust Zuid (HKZ) in the Netherlands, are one example.

These blades use a resin type that dissolves in a low-temperature, mildly acidic solution. This separates the resin from the other materials in the blade: fiberglass, carbon fiber, plastic, wood and metal, without significantly impacting their properties – allowing for a broader use of the recycled materials in new high-quality products.

“While recyclable blades are not yet widely adopted, we see growing emphasis on developing technologies that enable more efficient blade recycling and help retain the value and quality of the recovered materials,” says Julius-Philipp.

World.title: Europe dominates ranking of the world’s most beautiful cycling routes – these are rides to try
World.content:
Tourism on two wheels is on the rise with a surge of 292% in Google searches for “cycling holiday”. There’s so much more to a cycling trip than just the bike, though, and new research has revealed the most beautiful routes worldwide.

 

It’s good news for European cycling fans, as a majority of the top 15 in the ranking are based on the continent.

A study by adventure booking platform Explore used eye-tracking software to assess the reactions of 200 participants to 52 renowned and attractive cycling routes from around the world.

The technology measured how quickly each route caught their attention and how long it held it for, and the metrics were combined into a weighted "eye-catching" score out of 100 to provide a definitive ranking.

“There's something about seeing a country from the saddle that no other kind of travel can match; you're moving fast enough to cover real ground, but slow enough to take it all in,” said Luke Judd, travel expert at Explore.

“What's interesting about this research is that it puts science behind what cyclists have always debated: which views genuinely stop us in our tracks.”

Canada’s Bow Valley Parkway, a scenic winding route between Banff and Lake Louise, was far and away the most popular option, with a score of 97 out of 100.

It was followed closely by Australia's Great Ocean Road, on the southwest coast of Victoria, which was awarded a score of 94.

Despite the top two being some distance from Europe, and the list spanning four continents, eight out of the 15 are actually in Europe itself.

Here’s where to head for a beautiful cycling experience closer to home.

European destinations dominate the rankings

In third place, with a score of 91, are the stunning Tuscany Gravel Routes in Italy. Most famous for the professional one-day race held there in the spring, the stunning route features cypress tree-lined climbs, working vineyards and centuries-old hilltop towns.

With a score of 90, the Elbe Cycle Route in Germany is in fourth place.

It follows the Elbe River for around 1,220 kilometres from Czechia towards the North Sea, and the route passes through Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt, skirts several German states and travels right through Hamburg, offering a journey through historic cities, countryside and some of eastern and northern Germany’s most interesting landscapes.

In sixth place, Amsterdam Cycle Route 10 has a score of 86. The Netherlands goes hand in hand with cycling, and there’s arguably no better way to explore Amsterdam than by bike.

This circular route offers a brilliant introduction to the city and its surroundings, taking you past canals, parks and historic neighbourhoods before heading into quieter countryside.

Provence's iconic lavender fields can be explored by bike on a relatively easy route Thomas Despeyroux/Unsplash

In seventh and eighth places, with scores of 82 and 81 respectively, are Italy’s Stelvio Pass and the Provence Lavender Route in France.

While the Stelvio Pass is notorious as one of the most difficult cycling routes in the world – and the second-highest in the Alps – the Provence Lavender Route is, mercifully, significantly easier.

The scenic trip is best taken in the summertime when lavender plants are in full bloom. It winds through rolling countryside, hilltop villages and the Luberon and Valensole Plateau’s vast fields of purple blooms.

It’s back to challenging routes with Scotland’s North Coast 500, which is in 11th place with a score of 78.

Starting and finishing in Inverness, this route is more than 800km long and can take even the most competent cyclists up to five days to complete. Despite its trickiness, it’s well worth it for those who want to experience the rugged beauty of the Scottish coast.

The Route des Grandes Alpes is one of Europe’s great mountain road trips, stretching from Lake Geneva to the Mediterranean through some of the French Alps’ most spectacular scenery.

It’s in 13th place, with a score of 78 – the same as the North Coast 500 in Scotland – and isn’t easy either. Expect towering peaks, deep valleys, mountain passes and picturesque villages along the way. It’s fairly challenging, with long, winding and sometimes steep sections, so it’s best suited to experienced cyclists.

The last European entry in the top 15 is the Lake Ohrid Circuit in 14th place, with a score of 76. The trip covers roughly 90 to 96 kilometres and crosses an international border between North Macedonia and Albania.

Those tackling it will take in the historic towns of Ohrid and Struga and the Monastery of Saint Naum near the southern border, as well as Pogradec on the Albanian lakeside. Just remember to bring your passport in order to experience the whole route.

World.title: 'Woman Unknown' wins Golden Lion award at the 83rd Venice Film Festival while 'Naza' wins special jury prize
World.content:
“Woman Unknown,” a drama about Denmark in the aftermath of the Nazi occupation directed by May el-Toukhy, won the prestigious Golden Lion at the 83rd Venice Film Festival on Saturday.

 

El-Toukhy was the only woman to have solely directed a film in the main competition this year.

Her film centres on a young Marie, played by Mathilde Arcel, whose Best Actress win makes it a rare double victory. Marie is a nanny and housemaid who is about to marry her wealthy employer in the immediate aftermath of the war. But she harbours a secret past intimate relationship with a German soldier that threatens to upend her reputation.

South Korean auteur Lee Chang-dong’s poetic portrait of class and labour, “Possible Love,” won the Silver Lion grand jury prize, the runner-up award. “Possible Love” is Lee’s first film in eight years, following his acclaimed 2018 title “Burning.”

“NAZA,” a harrowing documentary about military strategies employed in the war in Gaza from Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, was awarded a special jury prize.

“It is really, really especially important to us that Israelis watch this film,” Abraham said.

The was added to the main competition late — at the request of the filmmakers — and debuted late in the schedule as well, but its impact was felt: It received a record-breaking standing ovation, lasting some 25 minutes, after its premiere.

Shot on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night in extreme secrecy over three years, “NAZA” features testimony from 24 Israeli military insiders including intelligence officers and soldiers give who insight into the war in Gaza and what they say is the systemic killing of Palestinian civilians.

The jury gave the Silver Lion for directing to Ilya Krzhanovsky for his film “Dau,” a project about the Soviet physicists who built the atomic bomb that has taken over 20 years to make.

Krzhanovsky, who renounced his Russian citizenship in protest of the war in Ukraine, dedicated the prize to Ukrainians, including his mother who was born there.

The Maggie Gyllenhaal-led jury announced the winners in a ceremony on Saturday night, which included a best actor prize for John Malkovich for his performance in the dark CIA comedy “Wild Horse Nine”.

Malkovich was not in attendance at the ceremony, but he sent a video message, explaining that he is shooting in Montreal.

“I am humbled to be chosen for this award which has been given to so many wonderful actors,” Malkovich said.

Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine was also met with a standing ovation, lasting well past 10 minutes. The dark comedy follows two CIA agents travelling to Easter Island shortly before Chile's 1973 military coup.

The film's stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell's performances were among the elements that drew attention at the premiere.

McDonagh has previously premiered two films at the festival, Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri and The Banshees of Inisherin.

He has previously won screenplay prizes for both films, while Colin Farrell received an acting award for the latter.

“Unknown Woman” star Mathilde Arcel was visibly emotional accepting the best actress award, which she said was very heavy and decided to place on the floor while she spoke.

“This is my first lead role in a movie and my first time at a film festival,” she said. “I’m extremely honoured.”

French director Stéphane Brizé’s won the screenplay prize for his corporate drama “A Good Little Soldier.”

Malou Khebizi was given the Marcello Mastroianni award for emerging actor for her role in Cédric Kahn’s “15/18 (A Place to Heal)” which is set in an adolescent psychiatric ward in a public hospital.

World.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calls on AI companies to slow down development amid superintelligence risks
World.content:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Saturday called on artificial intelligence (AI) companies to slow down the development of the powerful technology, as concerns mount over the risks of "superintelligent" computer systems.

 

Superintelligence is the theoretical point when AI's capabilities exceed human intelligence.

His comments came a few days after AI researcher Jacob Coxon, who left OpenAI to join Anthropic, decided to leave the industry, accusing both US companies and industry giants of "gambling with our lives" in the race to develop models capable of self-improvement.

"We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain," wrote Amodei in a post on his personal website.

"AI brings risks, and because it is such a powerful technology, these risks are serious."

FILE - Pages from the Anthropic website and the company's logos are displayed on a computer screen in New York, Feb. 26, 2026 Patrick Sison/Copyright 2026 The AP. All rights reserved.

"Not building the technology deprives humanity of benefits or simply places AI in the hands of authoritarian powers, while building it too fast is reckless. We have sought a middle way," said Amodei, who co-founded Anthropic, which developed AI model Claude, with his sister Daniela in 2021.

"But over the last few months, I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence," added the Anthropic chief executive.

Amodei's statement echoes another call by Anthropic in early June to slow or suspend development. Then in late July, Sam Altman, head of Anthropic rival OpenAI – developers of ChatGPT – said developers might need to voluntarily pump the brakes on their rapid advances to give society a chance to catch up.

Around the same time as the June statement, more than 1,000 employees at cutting-edge AI companies, including Amodei himself, signed a petition calling on the US government to help "deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development."

OpenAI had revealed that during testing, the AI models broke out of their confined environment, connected to the internet and infiltrated Hugging Face, a site developers use to store and share code.

Earlier this week, 27-year-old Jacob Coxon, sounded the alarm after spending the past three years pre-training AI models, first at OpenAI and then, this year, at its rival Anthropic, which he considered more cautious in its approach.

Pretraining is the stage where AI models absorb vast quantities of data of all different kinds, from pictures to videos to voice recordings, which help it understand things to then be able to generate images or answer user prompts on chat platforms.

"Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives," said Coxon in a chain of posts on X on Tuesday.

"The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade," he added.

World.title: Capgemini sells US unit criticised over ICE contract
World.content:
French IT giant Capgemini announced on Saturday that it has reached a definitive agreement to sell its US subsidiary, following controversy over its links with ICE, Donald Trump's immigration police force.

 

The buyer is ITC Federal, "a US provider of digital services and solutions for federal agencies responsible for homeland security and defence", Capgemini said in a press release (source in French).

"This transaction is subject to the usual conditions for a deal of this kind and is expected to be completed in the coming weeks," the group said.

In February, Capgemini announced its intention to sell Capgemini Government Solutions, its US subsidiary specialising in services for federal agencies. The decision came after the disclosure of a contract with ICE covering the provision of a tool designed to identify foreign nationals present on US soil and track their movements.

At the time, Capgemini argued that "the usual legal constraints in the United States on contracting with federal entities engaged in classified activities did not allow the Group to exercise proper control over certain aspects of this subsidiary's operations".

Members of parliament, along with Economy and Finance Minister Roland Lescure, then called on the company to shed light on its activities in the United States.

Tasked with implementing the hardening of Donald Trump's immigration policy, the heavily armed ICE officers have faced fierce criticism across the United States for intervention methods considered violent. The agency was notably blamed after the shooting deaths of two US citizens in Minneapolis earlier this year.

Operating in around fifty countries, Capgemini is among the leading French companies listed on the stock exchange. The group generated turnover of 22.5 billion euros in 2025.

The subsidiary in question represented only 0.4% of the group's global turnover that year, and less than 2% of its revenues in the United States, according to Capgemini.

World.title: AfD's Ulrich Siegmund's comments on arms and 'remigration' spark fiece criticism
World.content:
The AfD's lead candidate in the Saxony-Anhalt state, Ulrich Siegmund, has sparked fierce criticism with remarks about the possible use of military equipment in a future "remigration and deportation offensive".

 

The background is the planned establishment of a production site of the Israeli defence company Elbit Systems in Sangerhausen. At a press conference, Siegmund drew a link between the production of armaments, domestic security and the migration policy his party is pursuing.

Siegmund initially stated that the AfD did not fundamentally oppose the production of armaments. Arms production could, among other things, be important for domestic security, the stability of the country and national defence. He then referred to his party's migration policy objectives.

"The production of military equipment was not being demonised across the board," he said, because suitable means would be needed later for "remigration and deportation offensives."

Following the criticism that ensued, Siegmund clarified his remarks.

Arms production was a broad field and covered not only weapons but also vehicles, protective technology and other equipment on which the Bundeswehr, the police and security agencies depended.

In his view, these areas needed to be strengthened, not least in order to enforce the law, carry out deportations consistently and make a "genuine remigration offensive" possible.

If a new site served national defence, domestic security and the enforcement of law and order, this was, from the AfD's point of view, a duty of the state.

'No arms for foreign wars'

At the same time, the AfD politician stressed that his party rejected supplying military equipment for "foreign wars".

There was, he noted, a major difference between Germany producing such equipment itself and supplying it to conflicts abroad and thereby possibly taking part in them.

The AfD therefore wanted to examine closely what would be produced in Sangerhausen and under what conditions.

The possible arrival of Elbit Systems in Sangerhausen has already been causing controversy for some time. There have been protests against the project from the local population, which are also supported by the The Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW).

The company is an Israeli defence group based in Haifa that develops and manufactures, among other things, drones, howitzers, rocket launchers as well as communication and self-protection systems for military use.

Its best-known products include the Hermes and Skylark drone models.

In Germany, the company's headquarters are in Ulm. According to its own information, Elbit is already working for the Bundeswehr and supplies, among other things, self-protection systems for aircraft.

No stance yet on Israeli arms manufacturer

An industrial site of around 130 hectares has been earmarked for the potential factory in Sangerhausen. The town's mayor, Torsten Schweiger, recently stated that neither final assembly of drones nor of shells or ammunition was planned there.

A final decision on the plant has not yet been taken. Siegmund also said that his party had not yet adopted a definitive position. In addition to security and foreign policy issues, the economic impact on the region also has to be taken into account.

The AfD politician's remarks, meanwhile, have prompted fierce reactions.

The Social Democratic Party's (SPD) parliamentary group leader in the Saxony-Anhalt state parliament, Katja Pähle, described Siegmund's comments as a political threat. In her view, they were not a case of an unfortunate choice of words.

"Anyone who brings military equipment into play in connection with a planned mass expulsion of people is talking about violence as a means of politics," Pähle said. At the same time, she called on the BSW to state its position on the AfD politician's statements.

The BSW in turn also reacted critically. Fabio De Masi, the party's co-chair at federal level, accused the AfD of backing rearmament and of justifying the possible arrival of the Israeli defence company by linking it to the use of military technology for "remigration".

This showed, in his view, that the AfD had no real intention of governing and was instead seeking a way out through provocation.

The statements are politically explosive also because the BSW is the only party in the new Saxony-Anhalt state parliament that is fundamentally willing to hold talks with the AfD. No decision on cooperation has however been taken yet.

Following the state election, the BSW signalled that it was prepared to discuss cooperation on specific projects and issues. The Christian Democratic Party (CDU), SPD, Greens and Left Party continue to rule out working with them.

In the Saxony-Anhalt state election, the AfD emerged by a clear margin as the strongest party. It won 43.8 percent of the vote but still fell short of an absolute majority.

Siegmund subsequently reaffirmed his party's claim to form a government. He did not rule out a government with an extremely narrow majority. The aim, the AfD politician said, was to form a government that was as stable as possible.
