World.title: Hong Kong homes flattened for US$28 bn high-tech hub
World.content:
Hong Kong – Chan Yuk-tong hoped to spend his remaining years in the row of small, blue-brick houses where he was born and raised, but the 71-year-old’s Hong Kong village home will soon be bulldozed to make way for a vast tech hub.

An area roughly a third of Hong Kong including villages, natural wetlands and farmland is being converted into the “Northern Metropolis”, an ambitious project aimed at deepening integration with the mainland, diversifying the economy and providing new homes.

“I can’t bear to leave… If not for the government developing this area, I would likely spend the rest of my life here. After all, I belong here,” Chan told AFP as he packed up belongings in his yard.

Touted as a “new economic engine” to accommodate around 2.5 million residents and provide 650,000 jobs, the project will link Hong Kong more closely with Macau and nine cities in mainland China that make up the Greater Bay Area.

But the government’s vision for a Silicon Valley-like high-tech hub in Hong Kong comes at a huge cost to the city’s wildlife, local communities and public finances, environmental and social groups warned.

“If you build a new city in a place that was well preserved before, it would inevitably be very destructive, no matter how you mitigate it,” said Brian Wong of Liber Research Community, an NGO focused on land issues.

“Do we need to build it so big? Is it too ambitious?” he added.

– Return on investment –

The Northern Metropolis project, announced five years ago, will eventually cover 30,000 hectares (74,000 acres).

Liber said at least 25 villages will be demolished to make way for it.

Government departments told AFP they aim to integrate rural areas into the development project, but that Chan’s ancestral houses were not culturally significant enough to preserve.

Plans to integrate Hong Kong with mainland China have long faced opposition in the former British colony, where critics warn such moves would erode the city’s autonomy.

But a sweeping national security law imposed by Beijing on Hong Kong in 2020 after huge pro-democracy protests has stymied dissent in the financial hub.

It “effectively put an end to the ‘one country, two systems’ framework that allowed Hong Kong a ‘high degree of autonomy’, so greater integration with the Greater Bay Area would logically follow,” Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute, told AFP.

The government says the Northern Metropolis will cost at least HK$224 billion (US$28.6 billion), while global ratings agency S&P estimates it could top HK$360 billion.

Authorities have promised a return on investment, citing bank estimates — and a rough 20-year timeline — that the project will account for 13 percent of Hong Kong’s gross domestic product.

Tech hubs across the border in mainland China, such as Alibaba’s hometown of Hangzhou, are expanding far faster, spurred by AI investors such as Deepseek and Unitree Robotics.

Hong Kong is “less relevant for China’s national tech ambitions” than mainland powerhouses like Shenzhen, said Gary Ng, a senior economist at Natixis.

But it can nevertheless provide what they cannot: international connections, university research, and deep capital markets.

– ‘Sacrifice’ –

Last month, the first large-scale land sale in the Northern Metropolis was awarded to a consortium of six companies, including Chinese state-owned enterprises and e-commerce giant JD.com, to build housing and a logistics centre in Chan’s area.

Hannah Jeong of commercial real estate firm CBRE told AFP that policy support will first attract mainland Chinese companies wanting to build research centres and take advantage of its lower taxes and talent, data and capital flows.

“With that flow, more manpower coming in, talent coming in… forefign companies will also gradually (invest),” Jeong said.

The biggest hurdle to the Northern Metropolis’ success is “how to maintain an efficient cross-border flow, and at the same time maintaining the confidence that the international community has in Hong Kong’s uniqueness”, said Wilson Chan, co-founder of the Pagoda Institute think tank.

In her village, Niki So had watched helplessly as her neighbours’ homes were torn down, waiting for the bulldozers to reach the house where her family lived for three generations.

The 42-year-old received a public housing flat in compensation, but told AFP she will miss the village where neighbours are like family.

In July, So opened her gate to dozens of lands department officials and police, who declared the area government property.

“I hope the development here will go well, that it will thrive,” So said.

“If it doesn’t turn out as expected then I think the sacrifice of this village would be quite unfortunate.”

World.title: All eyes on US Fed to tackle high inflation
World.content:
Washington – The US Federal Reserve goes into a key rate-setting meeting this week with markets expecting policymakers to pull the trigger on a rate hike to tackle persistently high inflation — and analysts say central bank chief Kevin Warsh’s credibility is on the line.

The world’s largest economy has been dealing with years of higher-than-target inflation, and prices have surged in the wake of US President Donald Trump’s war on Iran, his signature tariff policies and the ongoing AI boom.

The Fed has held rates steady since January, choosing to wait to gauge the effects of energy price shocks and to let the tariffs’ effects on prices ripple through the economy.

In recent weeks, however, several Fed policymakers — including Warsh himself — have hinted that if inflation does not show clear signs of slowing, the central bank will have to act by raising interest rates.

On Friday, new data on consumer inflation for August showed it remaining steady at 3.4 percent — no change from the month before, but still well above the Fed’s long-term two percent target.

Market expectations of a 25-basis-point rate hike on Wednesday surged in the wake of the data, with the probability at more than 85 percent according to CME’s FedWatch tool.

The Fed last raised rates three years ago, when it was fighting surging inflation in the wake of the pandemic. They currently stand at between 3.50 and 3.75 percent.

Trump has railed against the Fed over interest rates since taking office for his second term, launching unprecedented attacks on the central bank’s independence as he demands lower rates to spur economic activity.

The US president launched a criminal probe against previous Fed chair Jerome Powell, is attempting to fire another Fed governor and has even threatened to cut trade ties with certain countries if the Fed raised rates.

Warsh was appointed by Trump and analysts say this is his first real test since taking office: Will the Fed raise rates to combat inflation, or hold steady in line with what the White House prefers?

“This is the test. This is what comes with that job, and now he has to decide how to handle it,” said David Wessel, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution.

“He’s either going to completely disappoint the markets, or he runs the risk that he’s going to start to anger Donald Trump.”

The Fed’s Federal Open Market Committee, with its 12 voting members, will announce its decision after a two-day meeting on Wednesday at 2:00 pm (1800 GMT).

– ‘Costly medicine’ –

“It’s quite likely that the Fed will raise interest rates next week,” said Claudia Sahm, chief economist at investment firm New Century Advisors who previously worked at the Fed.

But “it’s not a done deal,” she cautioned in comments to AFP. “This is a difficult decision for them to make.”

Raising interest rates would increase borrowing costs across the board for the US economy, acting as a brake on further investment and consumption activity.

Sahm warned such a move was “not a magic wand and it is a costly medicine.”

She said the Fed could still hold rates steady rather than administer that medicine, but it would have to explain its decision clearly to markets.

“If they surprise markets and they can’t explain why they’re surprising markets, then Wednesday afternoon will be pretty messy,” she said.

Since taking office, Warsh has changed the way the Fed communicates about its decisions, advocating for less transparency into the process as he thinks it locks policymakers into courses of action that may need to be adjusted.

Investors have had mixed reactions to the cut in what is known as “forward guidance,” with analysts saying it has introduced more uncertainty into how financial markets price in inflation and interest rate expectations.

Warsh has advocated in the past for lower interest rates due to expected productivity gains from AI technology, but in recent weeks he has doubled down on the Fed’s mandate to bring inflation down.

“There’s always been this doubt about whether Kevin Warsh is going to be like his predecessors and do what’s right for the economy, even if it’s politically inconvenient,” said Wessel of Brookings.

“If he raises rates now and Trump goes ballistic, he will have established his credibility as an independent Fed chair for the rest of his term.”

World.title: Messi scores but Miami held by Nashville
World.content:
Miami – Lionel Messi extended his incredible scoring streak against MLS-leaders Nashville on Saturday as Inter Miami battled to a 2-2 draw in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference clash.

Messi curled in a superb strike on 62 minutes at Miami’s Nu Stadium to fire Inter into a 2-1 lead but Nashville grabbed a share of the points after striker Sam Surridge bundled in an injury-time equaliser.

The 39-year-old Messi has now scored a remarkable 17 goals in 14 games against Nashville in all competitions since joining Miami in 2023.

And Messi could have even improved his goals record against in Saturday’s game between the first and second-placed sides in the Eastern Conference.

Messi saw a shot crash off the underside of the bar in the 50th minute and also saw a shot cannon off the post in the 78th minute. A late Messi effort was also headed clear by Nashville defender Jeisson Palacios before Surridge’s leveler.

The result leaves Inter nine points adrift of Nashville in the race for top seeding with nine regular season games remaining.

Earlier, Nashville had got off to a dream start when English striker Surridge sprang the offside trap before burying a low shot into the bottom corner in the fourth minute.

But Miami drew level midway through the half and again Messi was involved. The World Cup-winner’s wicked in-swinging corner found the head of Nashville defender Reed Baker-Whiting, who glanced in an own goal.

It looked as if Messi had grabbed the winner midway through the second half when he combined with former Argentina international team-mate Rodrigo De Paul on the edge of the area before curling a shot beyond the dive of Brian Schwake.

But Miami’s failure to extend their lead proved costly as Surridge scored from close range in injury time to steal a point.

World.title: Iraq sign 25-year deal with KEPPT to develop Ajil oil and gas field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi oversaw the official signing ceremony on Saturday, September 12, 2026, for a comprehensive 25-year contract to develop and operate the Ajil oil field, sealed between the state-owned North Oil Company (NOC) and KEPPT.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the long-term upstream venture represents a strategic component of the Ministry of Oil’s broader master plan to maximize domestic hydrocarbon resources, curb gas flaring, and directly channel critical feedstock to the national electricity grid.

Under the agreed development blueprint, the consortium aims to execute a progressive, phased expansion across the field’s producing reservoirs, with a decisive emphasis on non-associated and associated natural gas recovery.

Gas extraction at the field is projected to scale up from current baselines of roughly 135 million standard cubic feet per day (mscfd) to a targeted output of 300 mscfd, a massive increase expected to provide essential, domestic gas volumes to feed nearby power generation plants and alleviate the country’s persistent power shortages.

In addition to the substantial boost in gas capture, the agreement outlines targets to expand crude extraction capabilities over the lifespan of the concession.

Field operations are set to lift crude output incrementally from 30,000 barrels per day to 40,000 barrels per day, enhancing northern production flows managed by NOC while reinforcing the federal government’s drive to attract international technical and operational expertise into mature hydrocarbon basins across central and northern Iraq.

World.title: Arteta blasts ‘unacceptable’ Sunderland penalty despite Arsenal win
World.content:
Sunderland – Mikel Arteta said the decision to award Sunderland a penalty could have cost Arsenal the Premier League title, even though his side emerged 2-0 winners at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

Sunderland had the chance to take the lead early in the second period when Ezri Konsa was penalised for wrestling Dan Ballard to the floor.

Arteta was furious as pictures showed Ballard was also pulling the England international as the pair fell to the ground inside the Arsenal box.

The decision ultimately mattered little as Enzo Le Fee’s spot-kick was brilliantly saved by David Raya.

Just two minutes later Bruno Guimaraes blasted Arsenal in front with his first goal for the club before Bukayo Saka’s penalty sealed all three points in stoppage time.

But the result did not hold back Arteta’s ire towards the officials.

“We have to go through what was done today that in my opinion is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has not intervened,” said Arteta.

“I don’t know what to think really. I’m sad that we have to discuss in such a beautiful game something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship.

“At this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.”

Guimaraes was Arsenal’s big-money recruit of the transfer window, but the £75 million ($87 million) signing is yet to start for his new club as Arteta has kept faith with Myles Lewis-Skelly alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard in midfield.

The Brazilian was introduced at half-time and proved his worth with a brilliant strike to break the deadlock and silence the Sunderland fans that took aim at the former Newcastle captain.

Guimaraes also had a hand in Arsenal’s second goal as from his pass, Saka was chopped down for the penalty.

“The personality that he has. He comes in and this is a special game for him as well, what it means for him, and how he grabs the game,” added Arteta.

“The decisions that he’s made and the two actions. The goal is incredible and the assist as well to Bukayo to put him through in front of goal, it’s unbelievable as well.”

A fourth win from four Premier League games takes the defending champions three points clear at the top of the table.

World.title: Mbappe at the double as Real Madrid sink Rayo
World.content:
Madrid – Kylian Mbappe struck twice to help Real Madrid smash Rayo Vallecano 4-1 on Saturday to pull level with Barcelona at the top of La Liga.

Jose Mourinho’s side got back to winning ways after a defeat by Real Betis in their previous top-flight outing, with a convincing victory against neighbours Rayo.

Jude Bellingham and Alvaro Carreras were also on target for Real Madrid, while Sergio Camello pulled one back for the visitors early in the second half.

Champions Barcelona visit Levante on Sunday looking to extend their 100 percent start to the campaign and restore their lead on Madrid.

Mourinho’s side took a commanding three-goal lead against Rayo by half-time.

“(It was) fundamental to win, above all after losing the last game in La Liga,” Mourinho told Real Madrid TV.

“We killed the game in the first half — that’s not easy, working like we did after the Champions League game, not just physically, but mentally.”

Los Blancos took the lead from the penalty spot in the 14th minute after Florian Lejeune clumsily felled Carreras. Mbappe sent Rayo goalkeeper Emil Audero the wrong way.

The French forward helped create the second, after Lejeune gave the ball away under pressure from Vinicius Junior. Carreras exchanged passes with Mbappe and drilled home.

Handed a first start for Madrid, the club’s record signing Yan Diomande cut inside from the right flank with a rapid dribble that left Rayo’s defence scrambling but lashed his shot high and wide.

Bellingham notched Madrid’s third goal and his third of the season after Vinicius charged down the left and cut the ball back for the England international, who has started the season in top form.

Mourinho defended Vinicius in midweek after some Madrid supporters whistled him in the Champions League win over Inter Milan.

Mbappe powered a strike from distance against the post as Madrid sought a fourth, while Pedro Diaz forced a rare save from Thibaut Courtois at the other end, the Belgian with a strong hand to push away his effort.

Diaz hit the post early in the second half as Rayo tried to find a foothold at the Santiago Bernabeu.

– Golden ambitions –

Mbappe, who stated his case for why he should win the Ballon d’Or this week, almost added a second with a low drive.

Rayo pulled one back in the 51st minute when Vinicius gave the ball away to Camello under pressure and the forward poked past Courtois.

It was the Spanish forward’s sixth goal of the campaign, making him joint-top scorer with Barcelona’s Raphinha and Mbappe.

Benat San Jose’s side, 15th, had further chances to score but Courtois pushed out Giorgi Tsitaishvili’s drive and an effort from Lejeune.

Mourinho brought on Turkish midfielder Arda Guler to help regain some control.

“Arda is very good, he’s got a lot of quality, he influences the team’s play in a good way and today he made a difference in terms of the stability of the game,” said Mourinho.

Guler helped create Madrid’s fourth for Mbappe in stoppage time, lethally finished low and across goal.

It was Mbappe’s seventh goal of the season across all competitions.

“Conceding the (early) penalty was a blow, then we had another mistake when bringing the ball out,” said Rayo coach San Jose.

“I think we could have scored in the first half too, but it’s true that they were better…

“We have to congratulate Madrid, but I’m proud of the players because the second half was much better.”

On Tuesday Real Madrid travel to face Elche, while Rayo Vallecano host Espanyol.

Earlier on Saturday, Racing Santander defeated third-place Alaves 2-1, while Espanyol won 2-0 at Osasuna and Athletic Bilbao drew 1-1 at home against Elche.

World.title: Yemen government forces say hit Houthis in Red Sea city
World.content:
Dubai – Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces said Saturday that they had struck Iran-allied Houthi fighters in the Red Sea city of Mocha, as the number of civilians forced to flee the renewed fighting soared.

US news site Axios reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman had twice called US President Donald Trump to request American strikes on the Houthis last week but the request was rejected.

The ongoing clashes follow a week-long Houthi offensive that culminated in the group capturing the remainder of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and several strategic islands, and cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the sea’s southern entrance.

The waterway has become an important artery for Saudi Arabian oil exports after Iran largely cut off shipments through the Gulf with its blockade on the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the Middle East war. The Houthis have recently declared their own maritime blockade of Riyadh’s Red Sea ports.

The government news agency Saba reported on Saturday that Yemeni “forces destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed members of the Houthi terrorist militia” near the port of Mocha, and quoted a spokesman for the forces as saying they had also struck Houthi targets just outside the city.

The Houthis, meanwhile, said on Saturday evening that over the past 48 hours, “Saudi enemy aircraft conducted 129 airstrikes” on areas under their control.

Yemen’s civil war, which began in 2014 with the Houthi capture of the capital Sanaa, had been dormant since a ceasefire in 2022 but roared back to life in July.

Saudi Arabia first entered the war on the side of Yemen’s internationally recognised government in 2015 and continues to support the Aden-based administration.

On Saturday night, Saudi authorities said a Houthi projectile fell in an area near the border, hours after issuing alerts warning of the risk of possible attacks.

The civil defence directorate said the incident resulted “in two injuries and material damage to a mosque, several buildings, and vehicles”.

– ‘Not even a shelter’ –

The Yemeni civil war uprooted millions of people, and the latest fighting has led even more to flee their homes.

The fall of Mocha to the Houthis on Thursday drove many residents to Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based.

One of the displaced, Abdulali al-Rajihi, said the Houthis “told us: ‘Leave, scatter, you have half an hour'”.

“We fled wearing the clothes on our backs. And we took our children, as much as we could manage.”

Saddam Ali escaped from Al-Waziyah with his 11 children and a few possessions crammed into a small pick-up truck. He said he hadn’t found a single free house in the city, “not even a shelter”.

The UN’s migration agency said on Saturday that, since July, 76,000 people had fled the fighting, a figure that had quadrupled since last week.

It said it was providing support but warned that “needs are far outpacing what we can deliver”.

“The situation is deteriorating by the day,” it added.

The renewed fighting in Yemen has killed more than 500 people, according to sources on both sides.

– ‘Fine and dandy’ –

Following the Axios report on the Saudi request for help, Trump on Saturday acknowledged speaking to the de facto Saudi leader, but said the Houthis had also “called us and they don’t want to fight with us”.

He did not elaborate on whether the United States would take any action, but he told reporters that “everything’s gonna work out fine and dandy” in the region.

In 2025, the United States conducted a seven-week bombing campaign against the Houthis in response to their repeated attacks on Red Sea shipping in support of Hamas in the Gaza war.

That effort ended with a negotiated ceasefire, though the Houthis kept up their missile and drone attacks targeting Israel.

More recently, the group has resumed attacks on ships in the Red Sea after declaring their maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia.

In the capital Sanaa, meanwhile, Houthi supporters were celebrating the freeing of 210 prisoners held in areas that fell to the group.

The group said they were prisoners of war who had spent up to eight years in jail.

“I have rediscovered the taste of life,” freed prisoner Mohammed Bajash told AFP. “For five years, I suffered every day.”

World.title: Iraq closes three Iran crossings as hunt begins for Saudi pipeline attackers
World.content:
Baghdad – Iraq closed three border crossings with Iran on Saturday, officials told AFP, after a drone attack on a Saudi Arabian pipeline that both Riyadh and Baghdad said was launched from Iraq.

Soon after the attack, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed the military commander in Missan province, bordering Iran, after authorities determined that the drones had been launched from there.

No group has claimed responsibility, and an alliance of powerful Tehran-backed Iraqi armed groups said they hadn’t struck the pipeline, but Riyadh has previously accused these groups of targeting its oil infrastructure.

An Iraqi security source and a government official told *AFP *that authorities ordered the closing of three border crossings with Iran.

The security source said that the decision is “part of an intelligence effort to track down the perpetrators and prevent their escape… and to hinder the smuggling of drones through these crossings”.

Both sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not allowed to speak to the media, could not specify when the crossings would reopen.

The closed crossings are Shalamsheh in Basra province and al-Shib in Missan, as well as al-Mandali in the central province of Diyala.

– Other border crossings with Iran are still open –

The government’s security media cell said that authorities “have started administrative and security reorganisation operations at several border crossings”.

It added that they have stepped up “intelligence activities” to determine “the breaches and violations that took place at these crossings”, without specifying which border posts.

It later announced that passengers stranded for hours at two crossings were permitted to pass.

In July, the United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed militants in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities.

Pro-Iran armed groups have supported Tehran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks on US bases in Iraq and across the region.

On Saturday, those groups, operating under the umbrella of the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, said they had not struck the pipeline.

“Accusations against the Iraqi resistance regarding the targeting of vital Saudi installations on Friday are an honour that we do not claim,” they said in a statement.

Under mounting US pressure, Zaidi has pledged to ensure that armed factions surrender their weapons to the state.

The issue has fuelled tensions in recent weeks, with several groups refusing to disarm.

World.title: Brics embraces AI but leaves job displacement largely unaddressed
World.content:
Brics New Delhi Declaration backs AI-driven growth and worker re-skilling but leaves unanswered what happens to jobs lost to automation.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Brics has set out an ambitious plan to prepare people for an AI-driven economy, but its New Delhi Declaration leaves a key question largely unanswered â what happens to workers whose jobs are lost or sharply changed because of automation and AI?The declaration calls AI an âimmense opportunity to stimulate economic growth and sustainable development for allâ and backs wider access to AI, while stressing safety, security, inclusion and reliability. But on employment, its response is largely to prepare workers for changing skill needs rather than spell out what happens when technology replaces existing work.The declaration commits Brics countries to strengthen cooperation in âforecasting skills needs by analysing labour market trends in digital, green, care and other priority sectorsâ. It also welcomes Brics Connect, the âBRICS Cooperation Network for Capacity Building, Employability, and New Skills and Technologiesâ, focused on skills for changing labour markets.The declaration addresses some changes already taking place. It calls for nationally tailored approaches to expand social protection for gig and platform workers and recognises the need to protect workers moving across borders, including through portability of benefits. It also notes an initiative to establish an âInternational Digital Platform for Remote Employmentâ for Brics countries.But there is no equivalent, specific commitment on workers whose existing jobs may disappear because of AI.The declaration does not propose a Brics system to identify occupations exposed to automation, provide transition support to affected workers or measure AI-related job losses.That gap stands out because Brics is simultaneously encouraging wider use of AI across its economies. Its Centre for Industrial Competencies supports manufacturing companies, including SMEs, in adopting Industry 4.0 and advanced digital production technologies, including AI.Brics does recognise some AI-related risks beyond employment. In the intellectual property section, it notes ârisks relating to misappropriation and misrepresentation of knowledge, heritage, and cultural valuesâ that are insufficiently represented in datasets and AI models.For workers the declaration promises labour markets that are âfuture-readyâ, âensuring that no worker is left behindâ.

World.title: Three years before 9/11, CIA warned Clinton that Bin Laden wanted to strike India
World.content:
Three years before the 9/11 attacks shocked the United States, then-President Bill Clinton was warned by the CIA that Osama bin Laden intended to carry out attacks in India, Pakistan, Uganda and possibly Nigeria.

A newly declassified CIA warning dated August 28, 1998, said Bin Laden had survived US missile strikes in Afghanistan and retained a network of individuals and allied groups across at least 60 countries that could be used to mount attacks.

The assessment specifically listed India and Pakistan, along with Egypt, the Arabian Peninsula â particularly Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Yemen â Uganda and possibly Nigeria, as countries where Bin Laden intended to conduct attacks.

Bin Laden also viewed India as part of what he described as a âCrusader-Zionist-Hinduâ conspiracy against the Islamic world, reflecting the ideological lens through which he framed India and its relationship with the US and Israel.

The CIA said Bin Laden was also considering further attacks against the US and UK, although he had not indicated precise targets or timing.

The assessment came weeks after the August 1998 bombings of US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania, which killed more than 200 people and brought Bin Laden's organisation firmly into the sights of US counterterrorism agencies.





The newly released document said Bin Ladenâs infrastructure in North America, Europe and East Asia also lent credibility to reports that he could target US interests in those regions.

The CIA assessment further noted that Bin Laden had authorised an associate to explore attacks in the US and that US officials had recently helped arrest Bin Laden operatives preparing attacks in Tirana and possibly Baku.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The India reference is significant because it shows that the threat posed by Bin Ladenâs network was being assessed as extending beyond the Middle East, Africa and the US well before the September 11 attacks.

The August 1998 assessment was part of a series of intelligence warnings about Bin Laden that accumulated in the years before 9/11. The newly released material includes warnings about his pursuit of unconventional weapons, potential attacks on US soil and, later, the possibility of aircraft hijackings.

The documents also show that Bin Ladenâs network was not viewed as a purely Afghanistan-based threat. The CIA described a global infrastructure capable of supporting or inspiring attacks across multiple regions.

For India, the 1998 assessment offers an early glimpse of how New Delhi had already figured in US intelligence assessments of the emerging Bin Laden threat, years before the attacks that would transform global counterterrorism policy.

World.title: Brics calls for uninterrupted energy flow, infra protection
World.content:
New Delhi: Amid disruptions to global energy supplies, Brics leaders have called for uninterrupted flows of energy from diverse sources and stronger protection of critical energy infrastructure, including cross-border infrastructure, while stressing the continuing role of fossil fuels in the global energy mix.

They also called for greater cooperation on smart grids, energy storage and critical minerals, recognising their growing importance to energy security and the transition to cleaner energy.

The emphasis comes at a time of heightened risks to major global energy supply routes, with disruptions around Strait of Hormuz and possible disruption of another key route, Bab el-Mandeb, by Iran-backed Houthis, affecting oil and gas flows and raising concerns over energy security and prices.

Brics leaders said energy security was a "crucial foundation for social and economic development, national security and the welfare of all nations" and called for greater stability in energy markets.

"We highlight the need to enhance energy security by ensuring energy market stability and maintaining undisrupted flows of energy from diverse sources," the declaration said. It also stressed the need to "maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law".





Brics also recognised the continuing role of hydrocarbons, saying "fossil fuels will still play an important role in the world's energy mix, particularly for emerging markets and developing economies", while stressing the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in line with climate goals.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The declaration also recognised the role of renewables, fossil fuels, nuclear, hydropower, hydrogen, low-carbon technologies and energy storage in ensuring energy security and sustainable development.

Brics countries backed greater cooperation on smart grids and energy storage to modernise power systems and integrate more renewable energy, while highlighting the role of AI and data analytics in improving grid management and efficiency. The declaration also welcomed the "Brics Guiding Principles on Smart Grids and Energy Storage" and India's initiative to set up a digital centre of excellence in the area.

The bloc also stressed the need for reliable, diversified and resilient critical mineral supply chains, recognising their role in zero- and low-emission energy technologies and energy security. It said resource-rich countries should retain sovereign rights over their mineral resources and the ability to adopt measures needed to pursue legitimate public policy objectives.

World.title: India to get another major DRDO missile testing range in Bengal
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a boost for the country's defence testing capabilities, India will get another weapon and missile testing range in Bengal's Junput coastal village in Purba Medinipur district.

In April 2024,

had proposed a testing range along the Purba Medinipur coast to complement its integrated testing range in Odisha's Chandipur. However, the then TMC govt had not given land for it. During an event Friday, CM Suvendu Adhikari revealed that DRDO had sent a letter for the project but the then TMC govt at the helm did not respond. "I have okayed it. This will be a big project for West Bengal's development," he said.

A source in DRDO also confirmed to TOI that the missile testing project is coming up in Bengal.

The proposed testing range in Junput will be the third major hub for DRDO after the Chandipur sites and the proposed testing centre in Andhra. India has one missile testing facility, known as the Integrated Test Range, which operates across two launch complexes in Odisha: Launch Complex-III at Chandipur-on-Sea and Launch Complex-IV, off Odisha coast.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





While Launch Complex-III is used primarily for testing short-range tactical missiles, surface-to-air systems and multi-barrel rocket launchers like the Akash and Pinaka, Launch Complex-IV is designated for long-range strategic weapon trials, including Agni ballistic missile series and K-series submarine-launched missiles.

The Chandipur testing facility provides a secure coastal location with a wide, unobstructed eastward trajectory over the Bay of Bengal. The proposed Junput range, located approximately 70km along the Bay of Bengal from Chandipur, will share the workload of the Odisha testing range.

NEW DELHI: Over 60 nutrition and public health scholars from 17 countries, including researchers from Harvard, Johns Hopkins and Oxford, have backed India's mandatory warning labels on packaged foods and beverages high in nutrients of health concern, while urging FSSAI to strengthen system.In a written comment to Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, the scholars called for removal of the proposed "two or more nutrients" requirement, saying products high in one nutrient of concern should carry a warning. They said sugar, saturated fat and sodium can pose health risks and cited WHO guidance supporting thresholds.The intervention comes amid the debate over front-of-package labelling. Supreme Court has also questioned FSSAI's proposed phased rollout, including its "two or more nutrients" threshold, and sought a timeline for implementing front-of-package warnings.Dr Arun Gupta, founder of Breastfeeding Promotion Network of India and convenor of Nutrition Advocacy for Public Interest, said the scholars' recommendations counter position taken by All India Food Processors Association, which opposed warning labels and advocated per-serving labelling.The scholars said warning labels have evidence of changing consumer behaviour, improving nutritional profile of the food supply and making purchases and dietary intake healthier. They cited evidence of reductions in calories, sugar, saturated fat and sodium.

World.title: News in Frames: A village with no people
World.content:
In just 10 years, an entire village in Andhra Pradesh has emptied. The houses still stand, bereft of their owners, who have moved away after repeated crop failures that were dependent on rain.

Gattumeedapalle, about 125 km from Tirupati, is now a ghost village. Located in Kosuvaripalle panchayat of Annamayya district, the village sprawled across nearly 1,000 acres and had nearly 300 acres under groundnut cultivation. But the vagaries of the weather and depleting groundwater levels in the village gradually forced the people to move away. For some time, those left in the village depended on a single borewell for drinking water, but in the end, those families too moved away.

Thimmakkagari Subbi Reddy was once a farmer who cultivated groundnuts in the village. He has now moved down the hill and taken up work as a shepherd to make ends meet. He sadly says he has written off his village permanently and would not want to return. Like Subbi Reddy, several other villagers have moved seeking a livelihood. The shift began in 2015 when some families moved to Kosuvaripalle or shifted to the nearby Madanapalle town. For a while, some families stayed on, determined to make the best of it. However, with no solution in sight, they too started moving away in search of new livelihood sources. “An exodus triggered panic among the few who were finally left. Then, everyone decided to move,” says Subi Reddy.

Many of the houses were vacated, but the furniture and electronic items were left behind. Theft grew rampant when news of the empty village spread. Even the temple bell was not spared. “I would once hear the temple bell while grazing cattle. I did not think that even that would get stolen,” he says.

Most of the people who migrated from the village now support themselves by working for daily wages in nearby towns.

Only a large telephone tower watches from atop the hillock in the village that once bustled with activity.

Text by A.D. Rangarajan

In disuse: Subbi Reddy, who owns land in Gattumeedapalle, inspects the village well that has dried up.

Uninhabited abode: The dilapidated huts present a sorry state of affairs.

Desolate view: A quaint window of a house that stands empty in Gattumeedapalle.

Not welcome: Doors remain locked as families have moved to Kosuvaripalle.

Gathering dust: A handpump that was once used for drinking water.

Empty classroom: The Mandal Parishad Primary School, which has been closed down by the government for want of takers.

Fading memory: The presence of a smart meter at a house shows that the residents were till recently staying in the village.

Silent sentinel: The uninhabited Gattumeedapalle village is now home to a mobile phone tower.

Stepping away: Villagers who once stayed in Gattumeedapalle and have now settled in Kosuvaripalle.

Left behind: A dish antenna that has not been removed even after the family moved out of the village.

World.title: Street dog in Chennai’s Besant Nagar ‘adopted’; habitues of the locality in shock
World.content:
Can you picture a dog being stolen right under the nose of its pet parent and the latter being a mute witness to the thievery? One does not have to jog their imagination to picture that: something of this kind seems to have happened in Besant Nagar, and the “act” has been frozen in pixels.

Habitues of Besant Nagar would now be accustomed to a selfie point on their commute down Besant Avenue Road, a road that was co-opted into a Health Walk initiative by Greater Chennai Corporation. Those exhausted from a health walk could rest at this selfie point that comes complete with benches. And for the company, they have two human beings in fibreglass, glowing gold, and a dog cut of the same cloth, well, material, and similarly glowing. Of the two representational human beings, a lady holds this dog on a leash; both woman and animal are in suspended animation, frozen in mid-stride.

On September 11, loneliness engulfed her. She has no leash to hold nor a dog to walk anymore. Along with the leash, the four-legged pet seems to have been savagely sawed from its footings and taken away. The lowermost part of the dog’s legs is still rooted to the pavement.

Gayatri Nair, a resident of Thiruvanmiyur, a photographer, and a key member of Chennai Photo Biennale, clicked images of the woman robbed of her pet. The photographer had been alerted by a girl studying in a school nearby. And notably, this girl is a member of what is called the Thiruvanmiyur Changemakers Club, a children’s collective that seeks to address civic issues in the neighbourhood their parents and older relatives have given up as hopeless causes.

“This incident was brought to light by Rudra, a young Thiruvanmiyur Changemaker who studies at Adyar Theosophical Academy and crosses this statue on her daily commuter. She is just nine years old,” Gayatri points out.

To all appearances, this dog seems to have been “adopted’ by someone when it was not up for adoption, and the street, Besant Avenue Road, is meant to be its forever home. This animal has to be rescued and restored to its rightful place and its parent.

World.title: Chennai’s golden dog ‘safe and glowing still’
World.content:
A street dog regularly seen on Besant Avenue Road in Besant Nagar went missing last week, sparking a discussion that found resonance beyond the neighbourhood. Those regularly driving through Besant Avenue Road had also noticed the canine’s absence.

One of them was Rudra, a girl studying in a school nearby. And notably, this girl is a member of what is called Thiruvanmiyur Changemakers Club, a children’s collective that seeks to address civic issues in the neighbourhood their parents and older relatives have given up as lost causes.

“This incident was brought to light by Rudra, a young Thiruvanmiyur Changemaker who studies at Adyar Theosophical Academy, and she sees this dog on her daily commute. She is just nine years old,” points out Gayatri Nair, also a resident of Thiruvanmiyur.

Now, as luck would have it, Gayatri happens to be a photographer and a key member of Chennai Photo Biennale and believes in taking problems head-on, particularly those of the civic category. On being informed about the missing dog, Gayatri clicked images of the woman robbed of her pet and spread the word. about the catastrophe that had befallen her. For contrast, Gayatri ferreted out an old image of the woman in happier times, walking the dog leash in hand. When the two photos were juxtaposed and shared, there was an outpouring of concern. The missing dog had become Chennai’s collective loss.

Anyone who has not seen this dog might dismiss all of this as brouhaha. But this was no ordinary four-legged creature: it glowed golden and was always in the company of this lady, equally gold-spangled.

The lady is a permanent resident of what is called “selfie point” on Besant Avenue Road, frequented by those who believe in walking their illnesses away, a belief partially strengthened by a Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) initiative.

GCC had designed a Health Walk Route in Besant Nagar with much of the walking taking place on Besant Avenue Road under the shade cast by the trees on the Theosophical Society peeping out curiously. And a halting point where people, the walking crowd, could rest and click a few selfies was created; hence the name “selfie point”. And this lady, a fitness freak always accompanied by an equally spry dog, now missing, had been signed on as brand ambassador for the Health Walk and stationed at this selfie point. Two others recruited for the same role as brand ambassador are men, also gold-coloured from head to toe.

Silaii, a sculpture brand, had “recruited” this team of fitness-focussed brand ambassadors for Health Walk. All three humans and the dog, also a brand promoter, are made of industrial fibre and painted glow. But those in Silaii talk of them, the three humans and dogs, as if they were breathing and thinking creatures. Many of the regulars at the selfie point share this sentiment and have seen themselves in the presence of real humans and a real dog.

This is how Maverick Prem, who heads branding at Silaii and lives at a place not too far from the selfie point, remarks that he has seen people talking to these statues, which he describes in this manner: “You will find a man sitting, a very laidback man sitting on a chair and then you will find a woman and she also will hold a dog. And you will find another man who is running. Each of them has a distinct character. You will find a companion in the man (the one sitting on the bench). You will find grace in the woman and you will find playfulness in the dog. So, each will connect with visitors in its own way.”

And when Prem learnt about the widespread consternation over the missing dog, he allayed fears.

“On a morning run, I saw the dog lying, dismantled, on its side. Something had happened, and in a lifeform language, an injury had happened. We took measures, transferring it safely to our factory in Tambaram, and right now, the dog is in safe hands. It will be back soon, and in the dog’s voice, we should say, ‘I will be back with a new avatar!’”says Prem. Rough handling by visitors had caused this “injury” to the dog. Prem notes that he and the rest of the people at Silaii are not unduly upset over this mishap.

“At Silaii, we have created this, and we wanted people to touch and feel it. That is the idea of a sculpture. In any other art form, people would say, 'Please do not touch.' But we would want to have people touch and feel works of sculpture. And that is the beauty of sculpture.”

According to Silaii founder Arun Titan, "A work of sculpture is meant to be touched and felt, and it is in the hands of the people to ensure its safety, through responsible behaviour.”

Prem shared pictures of the dog being “treated” at the factory in Tambaram and of its journey towards assuming a new avatar.

World.title: Suvendu eats fish offering at Kalighat temple amidst Bageshwar Baba row
World.content:
Amidst the controversy raging over the remarks made by a Madhya Pradesh religious preacher advocating vegetarian food for Bengali Hindus during Durga Puja, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari late on Thursday (September 10, 2026) partook in the traditional fish and pulao bhog at Kolkata’s Kalighat temple.

The video of the Chief Minister having pulao and fish was shared largely on social media including by West Bengal BJP . “On the sacred occasion of Kaushiki Amavasya, Chief Minister Shri @SuvenduWB offered prayers to Maa Kali at Kalighat and, following the temple’s traditional customs, partook of the sacred bhog of pulao and fish,” the West Bengal BJP said on social media, sharing the video.

The video surfaced days after Dhirendra Krishna Shastri alias Bageshwar Baba on September 6 urged Bengalis to give up non-vegetarian food during the pujas.

“I want to appeal to the Hindus of Bengal that during Navratri, even if you don’t keep the idols of the Goddess, do not sell non-veg near the idols,” the self-styled godman had said during an event at Liluah in Howrah on September 6.

Also Read: Suvendu Adhikari backs freedom of food choice, religious practices

West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya, on September 7, expressed strong differences with the Madhya Pradesh religious preacher by saying nobody could ask Bengalis to give up non-vegetarian food.’

“How can Bengalis not have fish and meat? Even Swami Vivekananda said Ma Kali will have mutton [as an offering]. It is dangerous if someone tries to rise above Vivekananda. This is his [Shastri’s] personal opinion,” Mr. Bhattacharya had said on September 7.

The Chief Minister, however, defended Mr. Shastri and directed the police to arrest those protesting against the preacher. One Congress leader was arrested on Friday (September 11, 2026) for burning photographs of the Madhya Pradesh religious preacher.

“Those who want to accept will accept, and those who do not want will not. He did not impose it on anyone. I saw a number of people burning his photographs outside Bhawanipore police station. I am directing the CP [Commissioner of Police] from here that these people need to be arrested,” the Chief Minister had said in the State Assembly on Thursday (September 10, 2026).

Several leaders of the West Bengal unit of the BJP including president of State unit and several Ministers have said that there was no question of giving up non-vegetarian food. There is a long tradition of offering and having non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja festival in West Bengal.

World.title: Bengal Congress lodges police complaint against Bageshwar Baba over Durga Puja meat diktat
World.content:
West Bengal Congress leaders lodged a police complaint in Kolkata on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) against Bageshwar Dham chief priest Dhirendra Shastri over his recent remarks asking people in the State to avoid eating non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja festivities.

Also Read: Suvendu Adhikari backs freedom of food choice, religious practices

The comments have triggered a major political row in West Bengal, with the Congress accusing him of hurting Bengali sentiments and insulting the State’s culture and traditions.

“Those who speak the language and belong to our State are all Bengalees or Bangalis, as there is no such division. He has uttered vile sentences and preached what to eat and what not to eat during the Durga Puja in our State, which is a prestigious festival and puja,” the police complaint filed at the Bhawanipur police station stated. The Congress also objected to the language used by Mr. Shastri, which it said was derogatory and insulting to Bengali culture.

The complaint was filed by Pradip Prasad, president of the South Kolkata District Congress Committee. Congress workers also held a protest outside the police station and demanded that an FIR be registered against Mr. Shastri based on the complaint.

Similar complaints were filed by other Congress leaders at the Muchipara police station in north Kolkata. According to party leaders, the party has filed multiple complaints against Mr. Shastri across all districts of West Bengal.

“Who wants fish and meat shops to be closed in Bengal during Durga Puja? Those who are in support of this, turn on your phone lights. May this appeal reach the people of the State government. I am offended by the fact that during Navratri and Durga Puja they make ‘dirty’ food (non-veg) behind the pandals,” Mr. Shastri had said at an event in Howrah a few days ago. He said people who eat such food are not religious, and described them as pakhandis (hypocrites).

“Bengali culture, lifestyle, eating habits, or religious practices, or who we believe in, or pray to cannot be dictated by a godman like him,” senior Congress leader Suman Roy Chaudhuri told The Hindu on Tuesday (September 8).

Mr. Roy Chaudhuri also alleged that such godmen are “like the sleeper cells of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh” who travel to different parts of the country to provoke people and impose what he described as North Indian culture.

Even as the State BJP leadership sought to downplay the controversy, the Opposition stepped up its attack on Mr. Shastri and the BJP over his remarks.

World.title: Anthropic says UAE-linked AI op targeted UN experts over Sudan
World.content:
AI firm Anthropic has said it detected a UAE-linked influence operation that targeted the Muslim Brotherhood and United Nations experts critical of Abu Dhabi's alleged role in Sudan's war.

In a report on misuse of its AI models on Thursday (September 12, 2026), Anthropic said it uncovered and disrupted the broad campaign it linked "with high confidence" to UAE government officials.

Also Read: AI industry needs to slow down for safety: Anthropic CEO

Aimed primarily at the Muslim Brotherhood, the operation used the company's Claude chatbot to generate reports, advocacy materials, social media content and testimony on Sudan.

Since April 2023, Sudan has been engulfed in a war between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), triggering what the United Nations has described as one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

The UAE has repeatedly been accused, including by UN experts, of supporting the RSF and fuelling the conflict, allegations Abu Dhabi denies.

Last week, the UN's independent fact-finding mission on Sudan said that private entities, intermediaries and recruiters operating from countries including the UAE and Colombia used transit locations in Chad, Libya and Somalia to facilitate the delivery of personnel, training, weapons and logistics to the RSF in Sudan.

Anthropic said the operation focused on an AI persona known as "Deadshot", guided by a doctrine calling for "a coordinated transatlantic and regional operation to dismantle the Muslim Brotherhood globally".

Founded in Egypt in 1928, the Sunni pan-Islamist movement has been accused of links to the Sudanese army, which denies the allegation.

Targeting UN critics

Anthropic said the operation compiled what it described as "counter-accountability dossiers" on UN special rapporteurs who had criticised the UAE's conduct in Sudan.

Another effort involved appropriating the identity of a genuine Sudanese human rights organisation and drafting testimony for two named individuals so that "materials serving a party to the Sudan conflict would reach the UN as from independent local witnesses, rather than state messaging".

Anthropic said the operation also ghost-wrote official testimonies intended for delivery at the 62nd session of the UN Human Rights Council, drafting them under "specific restrictions" that neither speech mention the UAE.

The UAE did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.

Anthropic said the operation ran roughly 300 fake social media accounts, though it could not determine whether the testimonies or dossiers reached their intended audiences or influenced policy decisions.

More than 200,000 people have been killed since the war began in Sudan, according to estimates by aid workers, while millions more have been displaced in what has become the world's largest displacement and hunger crises.

Attempts at diplomacy have floundered as fighting escalates on several fronts across Africa's third-largest country.

‘Outdated’

The UN Security Council renewed its arms embargo on western Darfur for another month on Friday (September 11), maintaining the existing restrictions as members continue to debate a US-led push to widen the measure to cover the entire country.

Moscow swiftly signalled its opposition to any broader sanctions. Following the vote, Russia's deputy UN ambassador Anna Evstigneeva said her country "will not allow even a hint of broadening the restrictions by the council on Sudan".

Russia, a permanent member of the Council with veto powers, has aligned itself with Sudan's army in its conflict with the RSF.

During a Security Council session late last month, the U.S. argued that extending the embargo nationwide could help curb the flow of weapons and encourage a political settlement between the warring sides.

At Friday's (September 11) session, U.S. deputy ambassador Jeffrey Bartos said the existing embargo was "outdated" and "insufficient to address the realities of the war today".

"Inaction means more suffering and death," Mr. Bartos said. "That is unacceptable, and we refuse to rubber stamp another year of maintaining the status quo."

The Darfur arms embargo, in place for over two decades, expires on Saturday (September 12).

World.title: Russia imports record fuel from India as Ukraine strikes hit refineries
World.content:
Russia imported a record 172,000 tonnes of oil products in August, including gasoline refined from Russian crude at a refinery in India that is partly owned by Russia's Rosneft, as Ukrainian drone strikes disrupted Moscow's domestic refining capacity, according to a report by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).

India supplied 70% of Russia's oil product imports in August, including 120,000 tonnes of gasoline worth 78 million euros, CREA said in its monthly analysis of Russian fossil fuel exports and sanctions. The volume of Russian fuel imports was more than seven times the previous monthly record and three times the total imported during all of 2025.

All of the gasoline from India was loaded at the Vadinar refinery and sold by EU-sanctioned Nayara Energy to Rosneft, CREA said. Rosneft owns 49.13% of Nayara Energy, while Vadinar sourced all of its crude from Russia during the first eight months of 2026, compared with 81% for all of 2025, according to the report.

"Russia is therefore paying a refinery that it partly owns to process its own crude into fuel it can no longer produce domestically, before shipping it back halfway around the world," CREA said.

The shipments underscore the impact of a sustained Ukrainian drone campaign against Russia's oil refineries and energy infrastructure, which has reduced domestic fuel production and contributed to shortages, according to CREA.

Each cargo of gasoline exported from Vadinar to Russia was transferred between vessels in a ship-to-ship operation off Egypt before being unloaded at Russia's Arctic port of Beloe More, the report said. All the vessels involved were sanctioned tankers, while four of the six had previously operated under false flags, CREA said.

Russia's gasoline imports surged even as the country, historically one of the world's largest exporters of refined petroleum products, faced declining exports. Gasoline accounted for 74% of its total oil-product imports in August, compared with just 6% on average between 2023 and 2025.

South Korea supplied a further 18,000 tonnes of oil products to Russia in August, mostly gasoil, while Egypt exported 25,000 tonnes of diesel worth 16 million euros, CREA said.

Russia's seaborne oil-product exports fell 21% by volume in August, while revenues from products unloaded at destination ports dropped 32% from July to 78 million euros per day — the lowest level since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Oil-product loadings at Russian ports have fallen for three consecutive months and are less than half their August 2025 level, CREA said.

Tuapse, Russia's fourth-largest oil-product export port before the full-scale invasion, did not load a single oil-product cargo for the third consecutive month after sustained Ukrainian drone attacks since May.

Ukrainian strikes also disrupted crude exports through Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiysk. Crude loadings there fell 58% month-on-month in August, while loadings stopped for nine consecutive days, the longest reported interruption at the port since the start of the full-scale invasion, according to CREA.

Overall, Russia's fossil-fuel export revenues fell 8 per cent in August to 604 million euros per day, while export volumes declined 7%.

The fuel trade comes as India remained Russia's second-largest fossil-fuel customer in August, behind China.

India imported 4.8 billion euros of Russian hydrocarbons during the month, with crude oil accounting for 4.1 billion euros, or 87% of its purchases, CREA said.

Indian imports of Russian crude nevertheless fell 24% from July after reaching record levels in the previous two months. Imports at the Jamnagar refinery fell 15%, while those at Vadinar rose 5% and Paradip increased 1%, according to the report.

China was Russia's largest fossil-fuel customer in August, accounting for 8.4 billion euros, or 51%, of the revenues generated by its five largest buyers. Russian seaborne crude imports into China rose 16% month-on-month and were 62% above August 2025 levels, CREA said.

Despite the decline in export volumes, Russia continued to benefit from elevated global energy prices.

The average price of Russia's Urals crude rose 23% in August to $69.90 a barrel, well above the G7 and European Union price cap of $44.10, according to CREA.

The research group estimated that higher oil and gas prices following the U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran increased Russia's seaborne fossil-fuel export revenues by about 31 billion euros in the six months after the strikes.

World.title: State Bank in tight spot as inflation rises
World.content:
KARACHI: Pakistan and other regional states are unable to adopt a clear position on economic and monetary policies due to the prolonged Gulf war, which has driven up fuel prices, according to researchers and analysts.

An increase in inflation in 2026-27 and a global trend of higher interest rates have also forced the State Bank of Pakistan to take cautious steps regarding the policy rate to be announced at the next meeting of the monetary committee on Monday.

The current interest rate is 11.5 per cent, but trade and industry think it is high compared to competitive markets.

Bankers anticipate a status quo, but some analysts believe the central bank will lift its policy rate by 50 basis points at the Monetary Policy Committee meeting.

Institutional traders expect 50bps rate hike; analysts see status quo

The SBP raised its policy rate to 11.5pc by 100bps on April 27 in response to rising global energy prices and supply chain risks.

As the war in the Gulf expands to the Red Sea, fuel prices have shot above $100 as constant attacks have made it impossible for oil tankers to cross the route.

Some analysts said the State Bank is in a difficult position on tightening its monetary policy stance amid rising inflation. However, the SBP is believed to prefer maintaining the status quo.

Inflation returned to double digits to 11.1pc in August after falling to 9.2pc in July.

A senior banker said the State Bank must consider long-term prospects and could decide to counter inflationary pressure with a slight interest-rate hike.

“Pakistan’s interest rate outlook may no longer be about Pakistan’s inflation.

It may be about everybody else’s inflation problem,” said Faisal Mamsa, CEO of Tresmark.

For instance, the global markets are going awry. Brent is above $105, the ECB (European Central Bank) has raised rates by 25bps, global bond yields have surged, and US inflation remains elevated around the 3.4pc mark. “None of these problems started in Pakistan, but the SBP may increasingly have to respond to them,” he said.

A poll conducted by Tresmark on Wednesday showed 20pc of institutional traders expecting a 50bps rate hike in Monday’s MPC. “Two weeks ago, we stated that the status quo was probably the best-case scenario for the September MPC. We still think it is,” said Mr Mamsa.

Bloomberg Economics and BMI have now moved to a similar view, expecting no change on Monday but growing upward pressure on rates going forward.

Published in Dawn, September 13th, 2026

World.title: BRICS urges ‘maximum restraint’ in Mideast
World.content:
• Joint statement demands protection of civilians, respect of sovereignty, global trade routes; condemns strikes on N-plants as breaches of international law

• Calls for ceasefires in Gaza, Lebanon, Sudan, Syria

NEW DELHI: Members of the 11-nation BRICS group, including China, Russia, Iran and UAE, urged “maximum res­traint” in the Middle East on Saturday, papering over months of division to issue a joint statement even as fighting between the US and Iran shows no sign of abating.

The declaration, relea­sed on the opening day of the group’s summit in New Delhi, called on countries to avoid steps that might inflame the conflict further and demanded protection for civilians, sovereignty and the free flow of trade, energy and shipping through the region.

“We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in the Middle East/West Asia and, recalling our respective national positions, call for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation,” said the statement.

Pointedly, the 11 natio­­ns also condemned strikes on nuclear sites, warning that attacks on facilities under the safeguard of the International Atomic Ene­rgy Agency (IAEA) bre­­ached international law.

“We express serious con­­cern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards of the IAEA, in violation of international law and relevant resolutions of the IAEA,” the declaration said.

“Nuclear safeguards, safety and security must always be upheld, including in armed conflicts, to protect people and the environment from harm.”

The bloc, which also addressed the crises in Gaza, Lebanon, Sudan and Syria, called for ceasefires and humanitarian access across all four.

Reaching any consensus at all marked a shift from May, when BRICS foreign ministers meeting in the Indian capital fai­led to agree a joint text on the Middle East because of sharply differing views among member states.

Much of the diplomatic effort in New Delhi has gone into narrowing the gap between Iran and the United Arab Emirates, whose disagreements have intensified as Tehran and Washington trade strikes.

Iran has targeted the US bases across the Gulf during the war, hitting the Al Minhad Air Base in the UAE as recently as late August.

Foreign policy analysts said reaching a common statement reflected the bloc’s effort to maintain dialogue despite disagreements among its members.

They added that the dec­laration was unlikely to immediately alter the cou­rse of the conflict but sho­­wed an attempt by eme­rg­ing economies to present a coordinated position.

“The key to ending the war lies with the US and Israel,” Sunjay Sudhir, a former Indian ambassador to the UAE, told Reuters. “What India has done is keep the difficult conversations going by showing that countries of the region can sit at the same table.”

China’s president, Xi Jinping, used the summit to press for a political settlement, telling the state broadcaster CCTV that the war served nobody’s interests.

“Relevant parties must remain committed to a po­­litical settlement and work towards achieving a permanent and comprehensive ceasefire,” he said.

Xi also said China was ready to play its “due role” in achieving peace and sta­­bility in the Middle East.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said BRICS members should focus on turning their cooperation into practical outcomes.

Published in Dawn, September 13th, 2026

World.title: Pakistan calls for unified global framework for digital assets
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has called for the immediate establishment of global regulatory and institutional frameworks to govern digital assets and shape the next generation of international finance.

Speaking virtually at a United Nations briefing on Saturday, Minister of State and Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) Chairman Bilal Bin Saqib urged member states to build the institutional structures necessary to manage next-generation finance.

He noted that coordinated governance is essential to ensure these financial innovations drive economic inclusion and efficiency.

Held at the United Nations headquarters, the session on “Digital Assets and Blockchain for Sustainable Development: Advancing Digital Finance through Innovation” was convened by the Permanent Mission of Pakistan to the United Nations in collaboration with UNDP, UNCTAD and the Office of the Secretary-General’s Envoy on Technology, bringing together Member States, UN entities and private-sector stakeholders.

PVARA chief tells UN governance key to equitable growth

The PVARA chief stated digital assets, tokenisation and distributed ledger technologies present emerging economies with an opportunity to rethink financial infrastructure around inclusion, efficiency and access.

He emphasised that emerging technologies such as tokenisation and distributed ledgers offer a critical opportunity to modernise global financial infrastructure and cooperation on global finance.

“The question before this room is not whether these technologies will scale. They will. The question is: who will shape them, and in whose interest?” he asked.

Mr Saqib placed ordinary people at the centre of the debate, pointing to the 1.4 billion adults globally who remain outside the formal financial system, alongside billions more who participate on unequal terms through expensive remittances, slow settlement and limited access to credit.

The minister argued that digital finance’s development potential extends well beyond payments.

Digital identity and verifiable financial histories could help small businesses, farmers and women entrepreneurs demonstrate economic activity without relying exclusively on traditional collateral or documentation.

Meanwhile, tokenisation could create new ways to mobilise capital by fractionalising assets ranging from infrastructure bonds to renewable energy projects, while distributed ledgers could strengthen transparency across public expenditure and supply chains.

These priorities closely align with the briefing’s broader focus on payments, remittances, financial inclusion, capital mobilisation, digital identity, traceability and responsible implementation.

However, Mr Saqib cautioned against treating technology as an automatic solution.

He highlighted risks ranging from retail volatility and illicit finance to the concentration of power and a widening divide between countries with sophisticated regulatory capabilities and those without.

“The choice before every member state is not regulate or don’t regulate. It is simpler, and starker than that: to govern the future, or be governed by it.”

He argued that regulation must evolve alongside innovation, warning that frameworks introduced too late can fail consumers and markets, while regulation driven primarily by fear can push technological activity into less transparent environments.

The emerging lesson from jurisdictions around the world, he said, is that regulation should be treated as market-building rather than market-blocking.

“No nation rises alone, and no nation should be left to rise alone.”

He urged member states to use the briefing as the start of deeper cooperation rather than as an isolated discussion.

Published in Dawn, September 13th, 2026

World.title: Posting of seventh health secretary in 18 months raises concerns
World.content:
• Adhocism prevalent in ministry despite Pims tragedy

• Several wings and depts still being run through acting heads, undermining continuity

ISLAMABAD: While consistency in policies is considered directly linked to the continuity of secretaries’ tenures in ministries and divisions, the federal health ministry has had its seventh secretary during the 18-month tenure of Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal.

Health experts believe the ministry is suffering severely from adhocism, which is widely practised in most of its ancillary departments and facilities.

A senior ministry officer said the health minister was not empowered to remove or appoint secretaries as such appointments were made through the Cabinet Secretariat and Establishment Division.

According to a document available with Dawn, Dr Muhammad Fakhre Alam Irfan, a BS-22 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service currently posted as Power Division secretary, has been assigned additional charge of National Health Services secretary, in addition to his existing duties, for three months or until the posting of a regular incumbent, whichever is earlier.

No lessons learnt

A health expert, requesting anonymity, said it was strange that even after the incident at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), in which 14 newborn babies were burnt alive, the health ministry was still being run through adhoc arrangements.

“Currently, Pims, Polyclinic, a number of wings of the health ministry and departments are being run through acting heads. It is strange that seven health secretaries have been changed during the last 18 months. If we look at the health director general, we will see an almost similar trend as hardly any director general served for three months,” he said.

When asked about the changes in secretaries, he said Nadeem Mahboob, Mirza Nasiruddin Mashood, Waqarul Hasan, Hamed Yaqoob, Aslam Ghauri and retired Capt Mahmood had been replaced, and the post had now been given to Dr Fakhre Alam.

“Nadeem Mahboob survived till March 2025, Nasiruddin Mashood till May 2025, Waqarul Hasan till June 2025, Hamed Yaqoob till Feb 2026, Aslam Ghauri till August 2026, Captain Mahmood till Sept 2026 and now Fakhre Alam has been given charge for three months, but the notification clearly mentions that he can be removed much earlier,” he said.

Another health expert said acting heads and secretaries preferred to run departments and ministries on a short-term basis and rarely took decisions with long-term implications.

A senior administrative officer of the ministry, wishing not to be named, said the health minister could not appoint officers in Basic Pay Scale (BPS) 20 and above.

“So the health minister cannot be blamed for frequent changes in the ministry. The fact is that two secretaries were removed during high-level meetings that were not being headed by the minister. In one meeting, a secretary was removed and within a minute it was announced that Hamed Yaqoob would be the next secretary,” he added.

When contacted, Health Minister Kamal told Dawn that he had carried out 30 years’ worth of work during his 18-month tenure.

“There were 2,100 beds in the public-sector hospitals of Islamabad, but I included 2,595 more beds by introducing health cards in 15 new hospitals. A trauma centre is being established in Islamabad, basic health units have been made operational, telemedicine has been introduced and I have put the health sector on a track which will address all the issues,” he claimed.

Published in Dawn, September 13th, 2026

World.title: Four National Logistics Cell employees martyred near Pak-Iran border in Gwadar
World.content:
GWADAR: Four employees of the National Logistics Cell (NLC) were martyred when unidentified armed men opened fire on their pickup near the Pakistan-Iran border in Gwadar district, police said.

According to police, the incident occurred on Saturday at Border Post No 250, about 60 kilometres from Jiwani Tehsil in Gwadar district, where the armed motorcyclists opened fire on a pickup carrying the four victims.

The deceased were identified as 24-year-old Ghulam Mustafa, son of Riaz Hussain, a resident of Chak No 132 in Punjab’s Layyah district; 34-year-old Sanam Masih, son of Saleem, from Sheikhupura district; 36-year-old Kanwal Shehzad, son of Dilshad Ahmed, a resident of Teacher Colony, Nawan Killi, Quetta; and 26-year-old Danish Iqbal, son of Falak Naz, from Ghundi Killi, Takht-i-Nasrati, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district.

Police said the attackers later set the vehicle on fire, completely destroying it. The victims were NLC employees and were reportedly carrying a large amount of cash, which the attackers allegedly took after the assault.

Police recovered a motorcycle from the crime scene, which is believed to have been left behind by the attackers.

Published in Dawn, September 13th, 2026

World.title: Used car imports fall sharply
World.content:
KARACHI: The government’s January move to abolish the baggage scheme for used car imports and enforce mandatory pre-shipment inspections for gifted and resident-transferred vehicles is now showing results, with arrivals in this category declining.

Indus Motor Company (IMC) in its annual report FY26 mentioned that “the import of used vehicles has plunged to approximately 38,000 units in FY26 from 42,000 units in FY25.”

IMC said these policy measures are expected to further reduce the inflow of used-vehicle imports in the coming years, improving utilisation of the domestic automotive industry’s installed production capacity.

Despite this progress, imported used vehicles still account for 19 per cent of total sales, as reported by the Pakistan Automotive Manufacturers Association (PAMA), representing a significant share of the domestic market.

IMC said that this is despite the fact that Pakistani consumers today have access to 31 brands and more than 100 locally assembled models, offering a wide range of choices across all major segments.

However, the domestic auto industry is currently operating at less than 50 per cent of its installed production capacity, leaving substantial manufacturing capability underutilised.

IMC said improved capacity utilisation would enhance value addition, create employment, accelerate localisation, strengthen the vendor base and increase the sector’s contribution to Pakistan’s GDP.

All Pakistan Car Dealers and Importers Association (APCDIA) Patron-in-Chief Mian Shoaib Ahmed told Dawn on Saturday that no units have arrived since the ban on the baggage scheme, and used vehicle imports under the gift scheme are also negligible.

When asked whether overall automobile imports are rising, he said this is because of increasing imports of new cars.

According to data from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), imports of completely built-up (CBU) units surged by 36pc to $377.7 million in FY26 compared to $278m in FY25.

In July, CBU imports slowed to $57m from $70m in June, while imports were $33m in July 2025.

A number of new entrants have been importing new CBU models, particularly electric vehicles, to gauge consumer response before moving towards local assembly. As a result, imports of new vehicles are rising.

Published in Dawn, September 13th, 2026

World.title: Pakistan has potential to become international arbitration hub: LHC judge
World.content:
